# #FactCheck-Two Old Videos Falsely Linked to Devastating Floods in Nepal

![Research Wing]()

Research Wing

Innovation and Research

PUBLISHED ON

Aug 27, 2026

10

### Executive Summary

Following the flash floods that struck the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday morning, 289 bodies have so far been recovered, while around 1,500 people remain missing. A large number of foreign nationals, along with Nepali citizens, are also among those reported missing. Meanwhile, a video showing a massive landslide is being widely circulated on social media. The viral clip is actually a compilation of two separate videos. The first shows a landslide rapidly turning into a torrent of muddy floodwater, while the second shows a two-storey house on a riverbank being swept away by rising floodwaters. A research done by the Research Wing of the CyberPeace found that both videos are old and unrelated to Nepal. The first video is from Myanmar, while the second was recorded in the United States.

‍

### Claim:

A user on social media platform Facebook shared the video, claiming that it shows the initial scenes of the devastating floods and landslides that struck Nepal.

<https://www.facebook.com/reel/1572666177989617>

‍

‍

### Fact Check:

To verify the first video, we conducted a reverse image search of its keyframes. During the search, we found a longer version of the same footage, which was shared on an Instagram account on June 30. This confirmed that the viral clip is unrelated to the recent floods in Nepal.

<https://www.instagram.com/reels/DaLtKtjzTtq/>

‍

‍

During the research, we also found the full version of the video on a YouTube channel, where it was uploaded on January 28, 2024. Although the video caption did not clearly specify the location of the incident, it mentioned Myanmar several times. This confirms that the viral video is old footage from Myanmar and not related to the recent disaster in Nepal.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_z2_IEqOBNg&t=3s>

‍

‍

We found another report, published on January 25, 2024, that carried screenshots from the viral footage. It stated that the incident took place between January 24 and 25, 2024, in Myanmar’s Hpakant mining area. Further verification led us to a report published by EOS.org, the digital science news outlet of the American Geophysical Union. The report examined the incident by comparing Planet Labs satellite imagery captured before and after the event, providing further evidence about the location of the incident.

<https://www.geoengineer.org/news/mine-waste-dam-failure-in-myanmar-caught-on-video>

‍

‍

<https://eos.org/thelandslideblog/myanmar-1>

‍

‍

### Second Clip

For the second clip, a reverse image search of its keyframes led us to a CBC report dated June 14, 2022, which carried a photograph of the same two-storey house seen in the viral footage. The report identified the location as Gardiner, Montana, USA, where the Yellowstone River experienced severe flooding and a rapid rise in water levels. It also stated that the house belonged to Parker Manning, who recorded the footage himself while vacationing with his family at a spot roughly half a mile upstream from the house.

<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/yellowstone-flooding-video-house-collapses-river/>

‍

‍

We also found a post related to the viral video on FOX 61, where the footage was shared with a generic caption. The link to the post and a screenshot are provided below.

‍

‍

### Conclusion

Our research found that both videos are old and unrelated to Nepal. The first video is from Myanmar, while the second is from the United States.

‍

## Introduction

Recent advances in space exploration and technology have increased the need for space laws to control the actions of governments and corporate organisations. India has been attempting to create a robust legal framework to oversee its space activities because it is a prominent player in the international space business. In this article, we’ll examine India’s current space regulations and compare them to the situation elsewhere in the world.

### Space Laws in India

**India started space exploration with Aryabhtta, the first satellite, and Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian astronaut,** and now has a prominent presence in space as many international satellites are now launched by India. NASA and ISRO work closely on various projects

India currently lacks any space-related legislation. Only a few laws and regulations, such as the [Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) Act of 1969 and the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) Guidelines of 2011,](https://www.google.com) regulate space-related operations. However, more than these rules and regulations are essential to control India’s expanding space sector. India is starting to gain traction as a prospective player in the global commercial space sector. Authorisation, contracts, dispute resolution, licencing, data processing and distribution related to earth observation services, certification of space technology, insurance, legal difficulties related to launch services, and stamp duty are just a few of the topics that need to be discussed. The necessary statute and laws need to be updated to incorporate space law-related matters into domestic laws.

### India’s Space Presence

Space research activities were initiated in India during the early 1960s when satellite applications were in experimental stages, even in the United States. With the live transmission of the Tokyo Olympic Games across the Pacific by the American Satellite ‘Syncom-3’ demonstrating the power of communication satellites, Dr Vikram Sarabhai, the founding father of the Indian space programme, quickly recognised the benefits of space technologies for India.

As a first step, the Department of Atomic Energy formed the INCOSPAR (Indian National Committee for Space Research) under the leadership of Dr Sarabhai and Dr Ramanathan in 1962. **The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was formed on August 15, 1969.** The prime objective of ISRO is to develop space technology and its application to various national needs. It is one of the six largest space agencies in the world. The Department of Space (DOS) and the Space Commission were set up in 1972, and ISRO was brought under DOS on June 1, 1972.

Since its inception, the Indian space programme has been orchestrated well. It has three distinct elements: satellites for communication and remote sensing, the space transportation system and application programmes. Two major operational systems have been established – the Indian National Satellite (INSAT) for telecommunication, television broadcasting, and meteorological services and the Indian Remote Sensing Satellite (IRS) for monitoring and managing natural resources and Disaster Management Support.

### Global Scenario

The global space race has been on and ever since the moon landing in 1969, and it has now transformed into the new cold war among developed and developing nations. The interests and assets of a nation in space need to be safeguarded by the help of effective and efficient policies and internationally ratified laws. All nations with a presence in space do not believe in good for all policy, thus, preventive measures need to be incorporated into the legal system. A thorough legal framework for space activities is being developed by the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA). The “Outer Space Treaty,” a collection of five international agreements on space law, establishes the foundation of international space law. The agreements address topics such as the peaceful use of space, preventing space from becoming militarised, and who is responsible for damage caused by space objects. Well-established space laws govern both the United States and the United Kingdom. The National Aeronautics and Space Act, which was passed in the US in 1958 and established the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to oversee national space programmes, is in place there. The Outer Space Act of 1986 governs how UK citizens and businesses can engage in space activity.

### Conclusion

India must create a thorough legal system to govern its space endeavours. In the space sector, there needs to be a legal framework to avoid ambiguity and confusion, which may have detrimental effects. The Pacific use of space for the benefit of humanity should be covered by domestic space legislation in India. The overall scenario demonstrates the requirement for a clearly defined legal framework for the international acknowledgement of a nation’s space activities. India is fifth in the world for space technology, which is an impressive accomplishment, and a strong legal system will help India maintain its place in the space business.

### Executive Summary ‍

A video is being widely shared on social media claiming to show a delivery boy assaulting a woman. In the viral clip, a man approaches a woman to deliver some items. An argument soon breaks out between the two, followed by pushing and shoving that escalates into a physical fight. The purported delivery boy is then seen knocking the woman to the ground and allegedly beating her. Research by CyberPeace Research Wing found that the viral video is scripted.

‍

### Claim:

‍

“A delivery boy brings a parcel, and the customer comes outside to collect it. As soon as the delivery boy hands the parcel to the woman, it falls from her hands, following which the female customer starts assaulting the delivery boy. In anger, the delivery boy also begins hitting the woman and knocks her to the ground, brutally beating her with kicks and slaps. Although the woman was at fault, the delivery boy should not have reacted so violently.”

<https://www.facebook.com/reel/2826948067671726>

<https://archive.is/xwmky>

‍

‍

### Fact Check

To verify the viral video claiming to show a delivery boy assaulting a woman, we conducted a reverse image search using keyframes from the clip. During the search, we found the same video posted on the Facebook account of a user named Vipin Chauhan on August 21, 2026. The viral clip appears in the 2-minute-33-second-long video. The caption accompanying the video states that it is a pre-planned (scripted) video.

<https://www.facebook.com/reel/1551896343642588>

‍

‍

During the research, we also found the same video on the same user's Instagram account, where it was described as scripted.

<https://www.instagram.com/reels/DcTAF_ZsUnv/>

‍

‍

Upon reviewing the Instagram user's account, we found several other videos featuring men and women engaged in physical altercations. The captions of all these videos clearly state that they are scripted.

‍

‍

### Conclusion

‍

The evidence gathered during our research clearly establishes that the video being shared with the claim that a delivery boy assaulted a woman is scripted and does not depict a genuine incident. The same video was found on the social media accounts of the creator, where it was explicitly described as scripted. We also found several other similar videos on the user's account, all of which were identified as pre-planned or scripted content.

July 13, 2026](/resources/blogs/factcheck-videos-of-thai-army-falsely-shared-as-chinese-troops-entering-arunachal-pradesh)

### Introduction

Two videos are being widely circulated on social media with the claim that Chinese troops have entered Arunachal Pradesh, India. The first video shows a large group of soldiers marching in formation, while the second shows armed personnel disembarking from military trucks. Social media users claim that the footage shows Chinese soldiers advancing into Indian territory. CyberPeace Research Wing’s research found the claim to be false. The two viral videos are unrelated to India and actually show Thai Army personnel during military training exercises. Both the Government of India and the Indian Army have also dismissed the claim of any recent Chinese intrusion into Indian territory.

‍

### Claim

‍

An Instagram user, "mtkv.ideo," shared the viral videos on July 7, 2026, with the caption,"Chinese army has entered 60 km inside India."

<https://www.instagram.com/reels/DaehrgExzUl/>

<https://perma.cc/ZQV9-C6KJ>

### Fact Check

‍

To verify the claim, we extracted several keyframes from the viral videos and conducted a reverse image search using Google Lens.

During the research, we found one of the videos posted on June 16, 2026, on the Facebook page "Liangpha Kha Khaeng."

<https://www.facebook.com/reel/992963226961409>

<https://perma.cc/6YJB-RT9Z>

‍

According to the information provided with the post, the video shows a training exercise of Non-Commissioned Officers (NCOs) from the 3rd Battalion, 2nd Regiment of the Royal Thai Army. The page also contains several other posts featuring Thai military drills and training activities. We further reviewed the Facebook page and found multiple training videos featuring the same flag carried by soldiers in the viral footage, confirming that the personnel shown belong to the Thai Army, not the Chinese military.

<https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61588894033585&locale=hi_IN>

‍

‍

We also found a report published by **The Times of India**, quoting Union Minister Kiren Rijiju, who dismissed claims of any Chinese intrusion into Arunachal Pradesh. Rijiju clarified that no intrusion had taken place, adding that occasional movement across undemarcated areas occurs because the boundary has not been fully delineated. https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/no-intrusion-transgression-in-absence-of-demarcation-kiran-rijiju/articleshow/132101410.cms

‍

‍

‍

### Conclusion

‍

Our research found that the viral claim is false. The videos being shared as evidence of Chinese troops entering Arunachal Pradesh actually show Royal Thai Army personnel participating in military training exercises in Thailand. There is no evidence that the footage is related to India or that it depicts any recent Chinese military intrusion into Indian territory. Government officials have also rejected the viral claim.

# Old video of Buddha statue in floodwaters falsely linked to Nepal-Tibet disaster

* Published on August 30, 2026 at 05:46
* 2 min read
* By [Livia LIU](https://factcheck.afp.com/livia-liu),  [AFP Hong Kong](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-hong-kong)

Catastrophic flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border in August 2026 killed hundreds of people and left thousands more missing, but a video circulating on social media showing a Buddha statue standing serenely in floodwaters predates the disaster by nearly two years. The statue is located in Bharatpur, Nepal, and the footage was filmed during flooding in September 2024.

"The statue of Buddha stands amid the floodwaters, with muddy water submerging its base, yet it remains serenely unmoved," says part of the simplified Chinese caption of an [X video](https://perma.cc/A3SL-26C7) shared on August 27, 2026.

"In the face of disaster, there is only so much people can do,  but this scene suddenly brought people to a state of quiet," the caption continues, alongside the hashtags "Nepal Floods" and "Tibet Gyirong Landslides".

The video shows a Buddha statue standing strong against rushing floodwaters.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/e29affe2abd48bb1a007656e57cb8b0f-en.jpeg?itok=1RdApaRY)

Screenshot of the false X post taken on August 27, 2026, with a red X added by AFP

The same footage was also shared in similar [Weibo](https://perma.cc/C9XQ-N9L8?type=image) and [Facebook](https://web.archive.org/web/20260828075619/https://www.facebook.com/reel/1069033048842990) posts, as well as by [Indian media](https://perma.cc/9HRM-4E4Q) organisations such as [India Today](https://perma.cc/7UFY-GXKV) and [The Sentinel](https://web.archive.org/web/20260828060412/https://www.facebook.com/reel/1390714425764812), after a devastating tsunami-like [wall of water](https://www.msn.com/en-us/weather/general/nepal-orders-rescuers-to-safety-as-overflow-brings-new-flood-risks/ar-AA2b4XTL) tore through the Nepal-Tibet border region on August 26 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/23ZD-GSDS)).

Figures from Nepal and from Chinese authorities in charge of Tibet put the total number of missing close to 3,000 with 691 bodies recovered as of August 30, underscoring the [scale of the disaster](https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260830-nepal-china-floods-disaster-latest-developments) that swept away entire villages ([archived link](https://perma.cc/5HVU-B86L)).

The US Geological Survey said the disaster -- the deadliest for Nepal since a 2015 earthquake -- was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.

But the circulating video predates the August 26 disaster.

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared video led to a similar clip posted on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/I_AliFdgNl8) almost two years earlier, on September 28, 2024 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/4R4C-ARKN?type=standard)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/d3abfbe49d0e3c70bc19a53e47c3b041-en.jpeg?itok=3a1gOEUD)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (L) and the YouTube clip, with corresponding features and the clip's publication date highlighted by AFP

Nepalese media organisation Republica [published](https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/water-level-of-narayani-river-crosses-danger-mark) a similar image in a September 28, 2024 report about water levels in the Narayani river reaching a dangerous threshold ([archived link](https://perma.cc/GL5D-G2UP)).

At the time, large swathes of Nepal had been inundated with [monsoon downpours](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40324560/) that triggered deadly floods and landslides ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260830031122/https://www.brecorder.com/news/40324560/)).

Features of a [geotagged Google Maps photo](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Vwub9FisgocGtJag8) of the statue on the Narayani river in Bharatpur, in Nepal's Chitwan District, resemble the falsely shared video ([archived link](https://perma.cc/GC7F-B4UC?type=image)).

The statue is more than 110 kilometres (around 68 miles) from the Nepal-Tibet border, where the August 26 disaster occurred.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/918b17c78a450ae766e75405f0258e81-en.jpeg?itok=7XTsf80l)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (L) and the Google Maps photo taken in 2017, with visual similarities highlighted by AFP

An [aerial video](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/drone-footage-shows-debris-along-125209731.html) showing the debris-littered banks of the Narayani river on August 26 shows the water level near the [Buddha statue](https://maps.app.goo.gl/C9bd4oJvatze9S4w9), at around the 30-second mark, is not as high as depicted in the falsely shared video (archived [here](https://perma.cc/5AMN-DFBY) and [here](https://perma.cc/P2LV-46M9?type=image)).

People who live near the statue told AFP via WhatsApp on August 28 that flooding there was not as massive as the falsely shared video shows, but it did bring a lot of debris.

AFP has debunked other misinformation about the [Nepal-Tibet floods](https://factcheck.afp.com/fact-checking-search-results?search_api_fulltext=Nepal-Tibet).

# Old India disaster footage misrepresented as Nepal-Tibet floods

* Published on August 28, 2026 at 10:49
* 3 min read
* By [Vishesh SINGH](https://factcheck.afp.com/vishesh-singh),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

After deadly floods tore through the Nepal-Tibet border in August 2026, social media posts recirculated unrelated footage from India falsely claiming they showed the calamity. The videos in fact depict flash floods that struck India's northern state of Uttarakhand in August 2025 and 2026.

"The scene of devastation in Nepal is such that every new video that surfaces seems more horrifying than the last one," reads the Hindi-language [X post](https://perma.cc/2YML-KJUS) published on August 27, 2026.

The post includes a video of a flash flood gushing through a valley, damaging properties and infrastructure.

Another [X post](https://perma.cc/U4WB-5K6J) from August 26 shares a clip of raging floodwater, with several vehicles swept away by a torrent of mud.

"Disaster in Nepal, Terrifying footage," it reads.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/4e5b2fbcd0136407c21dbafa99af36d1-en.jpeg?itok=WogebyyK)

Screenshots of the false X posts taken on August 28, with red Xs added by AFP

Similar posts spread elsewhere in different languages including [Bengali](https://perma.cc/U4KT-2PRC?type=image) and [English](https://perma.cc/YNK2-CWP8?type=image) on [Facebook](https://perma.cc/R7MK-FFLE?type=image), [Instagram](https://perma.cc/G3YX-P2MG?type=image) and [X](https://perma.cc/2RYF-7TTQ?type=image).

The videos surfaced after catastrophic flooding and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed waves of water and debris that have [killed](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/pilgrims-seeking-peace-caught-deadly-032632593.html) more than 470 people and left upwards of 1,400 missing ([archived link](https://perma.cc/9YZX-T45J?type=image)).

The surge of water hit villages and towns on the path of two rivers -- Bhote Koshi and Trishuli in Nepal.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including trekkers in the Himalayan nation, as well as scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet's sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.

The US Geological Survey (USGS) said the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.

Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.

But the circulating clips are unrelated and were in fact filmed in India.

## Uttarakhand floods

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google of the first video using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8), followed by [keyword searches](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FfugMVf5WuY), surfaced an [Instagram video](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DM-rGp0Jcx8/) published by the weather platform AccuWeather on August 5, 2025 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/LU8W-8M68?type=standard)).

"Dharali, India," its caption says -- referring to a village in the Uttarakhand state -- with the footage credited to visual licensing platform [Reuters Connect](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/india-flood-in-kheerganga-river-in-uttarkashi-district-of-uttarakhand-after-cloudburst/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX09XU0hCQzEwNjUxMDg) ([archived link](https://perma.cc/Z7D3-CP5F)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/7c8a832b377fbd7be4915d8c02b4fc34-en.jpeg?itok=Z4pC_H-W)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared footage (L) and video from Reuters Connect shared in August 2025

The falsely shared footage also corresponds to [Google Earth Satellite imagery](https://earth.google.com/web/@31.03996082,78.78123668,2544.08357388a,225.87785082d,35y,165.1222457h,59.99621745t,359.99999895r/data=CgRCAggBOgMKATBCAggASg0I____________ARAA?authuser=0) of India's Dharali ([archived link](https://perma.cc/N4KZ-TVB6)).

Indian officials say at least 70 people were [killed](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250812-toll-of-india-himalayan-flood-likely-to-be-at-least-70) after a deadly wall of icy water swept away the Himalayan town and buried it in mud ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260828045842/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250812-toll-of-india-himalayan-flood-likely-to-be-at-least-70)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/b678d9fb012846131b1c967ea22a301e-en.jpeg?itok=0Nk-mYd9)

Screenshot comparison of the Instagram video (L) and Google Earth satellite imagery, with the same elements highlighted by AFP

A separate reverse image search of the second video led to [footage](https://www.newsflare.com/video/911535/dramatic-visuals-cloudburst-triggers-flash-floods-in-chamoli-bridge-swept-away-in-seconds) from British video news agency Newsflare [distributed](https://perma.cc/E7P6-UHYG) by AFP on August 10, 2026, with a caption saying it shows flash flooding in Uttarakhand triggered by a sudden downpour ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260828075210/https://www.newsflare.com/video/911535/dramatic-visuals-cloudburst-triggers-flash-floods-in-chamoli-bridge-swept-away-in-seconds)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/832fd12fa595b236907c031477bbdfc5-en.jpeg?itok=xHubSQqb)

Screenshot comparison of the false video (L) and the same clip as seen on Newsflare's website

Another video from Newsflare also [distributed](https://perma.cc/X79T-EVRJ) by AFP shows the same scene from another angle.

Indian media organisation NDTV [reported](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/uttarakhand-rainfall-weather-watch-flash-flood-in-uttarakhand-niti-valley-washes-away-vehicles-after-bridge-collapse-11893823) that flash floods struck Uttarakhand’s Tamak region, India on the day, after a heavy cloudburst sent a destructive mix of water, mud, and debris surging through the Niti valley ([archived link](https://perma.cc/Z5Z5-C37N)).

AFP has [debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6M39WH) other [false claims](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6PE9G3) related to the Nepal floods.

# Video of mosque withstanding Nepal floods manipulated from footage of 'miracle house'

* Published on September 9, 2026 at 11:17
* 3 min read
* By [Felix NATHANIEL](https://factcheck.afp.com/felix-nathaniel),  [AFP Indonesia](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-indonesia)

Flash floods triggered by a glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 swept away entire settlements in the Himalayan region, but video purportedly showing a mosque withstanding the destructive waves is in fact manipulated footage of a home that miraculously survived the disaster. The video appears to have been manipulated with the help of AI, and Google Street View imagery shows the affected area in Hindu-majority Nepal did not contain a mosque.

"Believe it or not, whether you like it or not, many places of worship, homes, and schools belonging to Muslims survived the floods in Nepal," says Indonesian-language text superimposed on a [TikTok video](https://perma.cc/2LHW-X9DA) posted on August 31, 2026.

The video appears to show a mosque with an emerald green dome standing firm against raging muddy floodwaters.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/4b7633842ce1ce206c58bc69654bea42-en.jpeg?itok=8HO_Dlbn)

Screenshot of the false post captured on September 9, 2026, with AI label and red X added by AFP

The video was [also shared](https://perma.cc/J4RG-VCZS) in similar [TikTok posts](https://perma.cc/3ZES-P756) after a high-altitude glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered [devastating floods](https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/nepal-flood-death-toll-rises-100247906.html) that killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 5,840 still missing nearly two weeks later ([archived link](https://perma.cc/F4F9-ZFBP?type=image)).

"Every time disaster strikes, the house of Allah always stands firm," read a comment on one of the posts from Muslim-majority Indonesia, another said: "God is the greatest."

The tsunami-like glacial floods also destroyed more than 2,500 buildings in Nepal's Trishuli valley, according to an [AFP computation of data](https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2026/08/1522990/least-2500-buildings-destroyed-nepal-valley) from Europe's Copernicus observatory ([archived link](https://perma.cc/VRH9-646C)). When partially damaged buildings are included, the proportion of structures affected rises to more than seven out of 10, underscoring the flood's violence as it tore through the valley.

As well as homes, the disaster destroyed roads and bridges, making it more difficult to deliver aid and search for the missing.

The circulating footage, however, has been manipulated with the help of AI.

## 'Miracle house'

A [reverse image search](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.36RH9NT) on Google using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared video led to a similar [Instagram clip](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dcst387iP8Y/) posted by Australian media outlet News.com.au on September 1 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/6N55-635Q)).

"A mint-green house stood strong while devastating flash floods swept through Nepal," reads its caption, adding that follow-up reports confirmed the house did not subsequently succumb to the freezing waters and the family seen sheltering on an upper balcony was rescued safely.

Aside from the mosque, elements in the falsely shared video -- including a flag in the foreground and an adjacent structure -- match the Instagram clip.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/5063010eec93b1289f42136bcdb02574-en.jpeg?itok=bef3qAlU)

Screenshot of the falsely shared video (L) and the Instagram clip, with corresponding features highlighted by AFP

A subsequent [keyword search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVAKQqO2BE4) found the same video in the [Reuters video database](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/nepal-green-house-stands-firm-against-nepal-flood-fury-trapped-family-rescued-from-raging-waters/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX09XU0hCQzExODA1ODU), credited to Rohit Nishad ([archived link](https://perma.cc/F36J-BPK2)).

Its video description says the footage was filmed in the Nuwakot region of Nepal's Bagmati Province on August 26.

AFP also took [photos](https://perma.cc/ZCB5-5QSF) and [videos](https://x.com/AFP/status/2095441748088459346) of what has been dubbed the "miracle house" from different angles ([archived link](https://perma.cc/2HMS-PQJH)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/7a1d774c794dda12b11f1dac61b48b93-en.jpeg?itok=GOewh70m)

A turquoise-green house, dubbed the "miracle house" stands tall amid sludge near Trishuli river in the aftermath of flash floods. (AFP / Arun SANKAR)

This footage matches [Google Street View imagery](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Jhewg8261WkvGavk9) of the area, but there is no sign of a mosque as depicted in the falsely shared video ([archived link](https://perma.cc/6LU9-PT8K?type=image)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/c94af5cba6d6a329b58b09920300b253-en.jpeg?itok=q3p7kJ8M)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (top left), the September 1 Instagram clip (bottom left) and Google Street View imagery, with similarities highlighted by AFP

The falsely shared video contains visual inconsistencies that indicate it may have been manipulated with AI, such as the splashing floodwaters not appearing to interact with the mosque and leaving no marks on its facade.

An analysis of the clip using Google's [SynthID Detector](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/google-synthid-ai-content-detector/) detected invisible SynthID watermarks in the video, indicating it was manipulated with the help of its AI tools ([archived link](https://perma.cc/8C3W-MQP5)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/e578245bab961a3ac280dc514aa2f925-en.jpeg?itok=eWZR22Zm)

Screenshot of results from Google's SynthID Detector

AFP has debunked other misinformation about the [Nepal-Tibet](https://factcheck.afp.com/fact-checking-search-results?search_api_fulltext=Nepal-Tibet) floods.

# Old Video From Jammu & Kashmir Shared As Landslide In Manali

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Jul 10, 2023

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/07/Thumbnail-1394.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

**Claim**  
Visuals of a landslide in Manali amid incessant rainfall in Himachal Pradesh.  
  
**Fact**  
2019 video of shooting stones at Jammu-Srinagar highway in Ramban district.

As incessant downpour triggered landslides and flash floods in [**Himachal Pradesh**](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/five-killed-as-heavy-rains-lash-himachal-pradesh/article67060108.ece), leaving at least five dead, social media platforms are inundated with unverified visuals of overflowing rivers, waterlogging, and landslides, claiming to show the dire situation in the northern state. One such video of massive rocks, and boulders falling freely from a mountain near a roadside is being widely shared, with users alleging that it shows a landslide in Manali. Newschecker found the claim to be untrue. The video dates back to 2019 and was shot at the Jammu-Srinagar highway in Ramban.

## Fact Check/Verification

A [**Google lens**](https://lens.google.com/search?ep=subb&hl=en-IN&p=Acn1BYcYuM2tMIHEmFyaxpmyVb6ItFGf20L-ZLXhZCCPJvbYo2S7nvpces-s6Cf_aRL9lD4g1LJTDr4tzxceQ8Bl35tBSePhb1ycWwbSONNGcGY_5fQ7P2cnWsUiHwIH1JDNv3TYkk6DSqJ2KwG7hNLnL5aWBEkt8PO4M8MtfJICIyQaj4gIDLbmhwWCGoNm5GrhxWdq0E7S0A0azDAyKY6TaPGjLQllNOZe0IYvspudoBc4VDBFPkkGwwNTIsN5hJIE5ceU6dy4uJjK-r8mbZSjI0tzE7SeXaH_jzX9wrdVV7lJFhVXRvzfVUuqhtGttrPfA-8BrSVVAu7qjz0Ul-rx_T5CJX4zRwMFgyZM6BbxjD2kLdvc6wVfx3tqN-yOGEJl10HejnZhh4d9KSC8ygVRAXagUJ5wg6Rc#lns=W251bGwsbnVsbCxudWxsLG51bGwsbnVsbCxudWxsLG51bGwsIkVrY0tKR1JsTVRjMll6TXlMVFF6WWpBdE5ESm1PQzA1WVdNMUxURmpaVGRpWlRKbVpEa3hOeElmUVRONGN6UlVSRmRITlVsWmMwWldkMUYzZG5veE4wZHRWbGRRYTJ0NFp3PT0iLG51bGwsbnVsbCxbW251bGwsbnVsbCwiMS0wIl0sWyIwOGNiYWUyMy02MWY4LTQxYmUtODRjYi1kZDQzOTk1NzJmMWMiXV1d) search on the keyframes of the alleged clip of a landslide in Manali led us to a Facebook post by **[@Savejmmu](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=418591568760388)**, dated July 28, 2019. Carrying the viral footage, the post stated, “(Attention commuters of NHW 44) In view of incessant rainfall,adverse weather conditions, frequent shooting stones/ blockages at multiple vulnerable places…commuters of NHW 44 are advised to avoid travel on Ramban- Banihal vulnerable stretch till the weather improves…” The advisory was attributed to the Traffic Police, NHW Ramban.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/07/Save-jammu-Facebook.png)

Screengrab from Facebook post by @Savejmmu

Taking a clue, we looked up “Ramban,” “highway” and “shooting stones” on [**Google**](https://www.google.com/search?q=Ramban+Highway+shooting+stones&tbs=cdr%3A1%2Ccd_min%3A7%2F1%2F2019%2Ccd_max%3A7%2F31%2F2019&ei=2KKrZOj5CtG0oASi9q7ADQ&ved=0ahUKEwjoxbysv4OAAxVRGogKHSK7C9gQ4dUDCBA&uact=5&oq=Ramban+Highway+shooting+stones&gs_lcp=Cgxnd3Mtd2l6LXNlcnAQAzIFCCEQoAEyBQghEKABOggIABCiBBCwAzoFCAAQogQ6CAghEKABEMMEOgQIIRAVOgcIIRCgARAKSgQIQRgBUK4hWOpUYOlWaAZwAHgAgAHxAYgBxBOSAQYwLjE0LjGYAQCgAQHAAQHIAQI&sclient=gws-wiz-serp#ip=1), and set the time frame of the search from July 1, 2019 to July 31, 2019. This yielded a YouTube video by **[The Tribune](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aldZxl2H10A)**, dated July 28, 2019. It featured snippets of the viral footage, and stated “Jammu-Srinagar highway closed due to shooting stones in Ramban”

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/07/Jammu-Srinagar-highway-closed-due-to-shooting-stones-in-Ramban-YouTube-1024x671.png)

Screengrab from YouTube video by The Tribune

**Also Read: [No, GST Rates Not Reduced For Electronic Items, Viral Graphic Misinterpreted](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/no-gst-rates-not-reduced-for-electronic-items-viral-graphic-misinterpreted)**

A detailed report on the incident, published in **[The Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/j-k/shooting-stones-force-nh-closure-809419)**, stated, “The Jammu-Srinagar National Highway was closed for traffic due to shooting stones at various places between Ramban and Banihal stretch of the highway, falling in Ramban district of the state.” Adding, “All types of vehicular movement on the highway was stopped, including the Amarnath yatra, after heavy rain lashed the region, due to which Panthal area witnessed shooting stones. Other places, including Battery Chashma, Digdol and Marog, witnessed landslides.”

Video reports by **[Aaj Tak](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NOPtY_tCrv0)** and **[ABP News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0T4UuJWXGB0)** from July 2019, also carried snippets from the viral clip to show an incident on Jammu-Srinagar highway in Ramban district.

**Also Read: [2019 Video Of Protest Against Algerian President Falsely Linked To Ongoing Riots In France](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/2019-video-of-protest-against-algerian-president-falsely-linked-to-ongoing-riots-in-france)**

## Conclusion

We can thus conclude that an old video from Jammu & Kashmir’s Ramban has been falsely shared as visuals of a landslide in Manali as rainfall wreaks havoc in Himachal Pradesh.

# Movie scene falsely linked to decades-old Venezuelan landslide

* Published on March 3, 2026 at 05:26
* Updated on April 3, 2026 at 11:12
* 2 min read
* By [Nyan Tun SHEIN](https://factcheck.afp.com/nyan-tun-shein),  [Pasika KHERNAMNUOY](https://factcheck.afp.com/pasika-khernamnuoy),  [AFP Thailand](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-thailand)

A screengrab from a short film has surfaced on social media with a false claim that it was taken after a landslide in Venezuela more than a decade ago, showing a father who refused rescue so he could save his daughters. Part of the movie was uploaded to YouTube with a description saying it was made for a Venezuelan film festival, while its producer said in a separate clip it was not filmed at the scene of a disaster.

"'Don't pull me out ... my two daughters are holding my hand' -- the last words of a father who gave his life for his children," reads part of a Burmese-language [Facebook post](https://perma.cc/Z5T2-NRZS) uploaded on February 17, 2026.

The attached image shows a rescue worker trying to help a man stuck in the ground with only his neck and head visible.

"Father who refused to be rescued because he did not want to let go of his daughters (underneath)," reads the Burmese-language text on the image.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-04/c27f28f28f9139d564158556d3446f2e-en.jpeg?itok=g4kamxJp)

Screenshot of the false post taken on February 25, 2026 with a red X added by AFP

The caption goes on to claim it was a tale from the [Vargas landslide](http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/8412249.stm) in Venezuela in December 1999, which killed between 10,000 and 30,000 people, according to estimates ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20171008225923/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/8412249.stm)).

Similar posts were shared elsewhere on [Facebook](https://web.archive.org/web/20260225051512/https://www.facebook.com/plugins/post.php?href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fsye69jjx5s%2Fposts%2Fpfbid0UeVREdcCMad34tKXkyiuVPAkr4i8BFG6bYRi2UggQRPXdvPihJ4Moc99Sh4fx7Rrl), [X](https://perma.cc/ZL9A-D3GR), [Instagram](https://perma.cc/G685-787A), and [TikTok](https://perma.cc/G6SK-ZX7U). It also circulated in different languages, including [Arabic](https://perma.cc/5E8K-9ZQK), [Burmese](https://perma.cc/TER2-DW4T), [English](https://perma.cc/C33K-X74B), [Korean](https://perma.cc/QG6A-38UE), [Spanish](https://perma.cc/3JVT-DKQX), [Thai](https://perma.cc/XV8Z-WVC7), and [Turkish](https://perma.cc/GFE3-U2KJ).

"As a father of two girls, my heart is broken," reads a comment in one of the posts.

Another wrote: "I got tears in my eyes reading this."

But the circulating image is in fact taken from a Venezuelan short film in 2007.

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google led to a [YouTube](https://youtu.be/4tDxRJheb44?t=61) video uploaded by a channel called Siete Filmes on October 13, 2024 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/LS8V-8WNL)).

The clip is titled "Sofia and Daniela" and its description reads that it was produced in 2007 as part of the [Cine Átomo marathon](https://festivaldelcinevenezolano.com/portfolio/iii-festival-del-cine-venezolano-2007/) of the Venezuelan Film Festival ([archived link](https://perma.cc/PH8X-93YM)).

The image in the false post matches the scene at the 1:01 mark of the YouTube video.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-04/8cbb07d7fc75be24d2ea38a692660ea8-en.jpeg?itok=q7NE_WUB)

Screenshot comparison of the false video (L) and part of the original film uploaded to YouTube

The description also says Venezuelan actor [Sebastián Torres](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3934666/) produced the film and played the part of the partially buried man ([archived link](https://perma.cc/77LH-YQCL)).

He shared a [short clip](https://www.instagram.com/p/DJLL1pXA34D/) on Instagram on May 3, 2025, where he dismissed claims that the footage showed an authentic scene taken during a disaster ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260302080241/https://www.instagram.com/p/DJLL1pXA34D/)).

"I am an actor who played that character. Also I wrote that short film," he said in the video.

AFP previously debunked misinformation using parts of art creations [here](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.94LL3ZQ), [here](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.34U46H9), and [here](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.34PQ6M7).

# Old Video From Himachal Shared Claiming To Show Recent Landslide At Goa-Karnataka Border

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1)

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Jul 19, 2022

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/Anmod-Ghat-Cover-.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

Monsoon rains are wreaking havoc in some parts of the country with Maharashtra, Assam and Gujarat being among the most impact states. More than 190 people have lost their lives in [Assam](https://www.outlookindia.com/national/flood-situation-improves-in-assam-58-523-still-affected-news-210161) due to floods and landslides this year, while the death toll in [Maharashtra](https://twitter.com/ANI/status/1548927431255662592) stands at 105 so far.

Social media is rife with posts of flooded roads and countryside in various states. We found a very viral video showing a massive landslide in which a portion of a hillside collapses along with a section of the road constructed on it. Those sharing the video claimed it to show a landslide on Anmod Ghat located on the Goa-Karnataka Border (location given below). Newschecker’s investigation reveals that this video is old and unrelated to the said event.

![Old Video From Himachal Shared Claiming To Show Recent Landslide At Goa-Karnataka Border](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/C1.jpg)

Screenshot of Facebook post by user Ravi Ravi

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/c2.jpg)

Screenshot of Facebook post by user Asru Ukkuda

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/T2.jpg)

Screenshot of Tweet by @lavanyadeepak

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/T-1.jpg)

Screenshot of Tweet by @caatfeesh

Links to such posts can be found [here,](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1066014257622976/?s=1x1) [here](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1109973333199889/?s=single_unit), [here](https://archive.ph/AwiOG) and [here](https://archive.ph/YgjWt).

The video has also found its way to YouTube as well with netizens posting the same with the caption “Anmod Ghat Landslide, Near Karnataka-Goa border.”

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/YT1-1-1024x793.jpg)

Screenshot of YouTube video by Travegu

Links to such YouTube videos can be found [here](https://archive.ph/JsuEl), [here](https://archive.ph/ia25A) and [here](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/C1tfE1g7dn0).

**Also Read: [Video Of Bridge Collapse From Indonesia Passed Off As Visuals Of Assam Floods](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/viral/bridge-collapse-assam-floods-false-claim)**

## Fact Check/Verification

We started our investigation by checking if there were any official reports of a landslide in the said area.  Located near Goa-Karnataka border, the [Anmod Ghat](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/two-landslides-at-anmod-ghat-bring-traffic-to-a-halt/articleshow/92662705.cms)  witnessed two landslides in the first week of July owing to incessant rains in the area. Reportedly, about 8km from the Goa border check post at Mollem, a large portion of the hillside had crashed in two separate areas.

[![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/Map-copy.jpg)](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Anmod/@15.4895519,73.8722216,109779m/data=!3m1!1e3!4m6!1m2!2m1!1sanmod+ghat!3m2!1s0x3bbf08cd78ba4dbf:0xbc1767425c32bfec!15sCgphbm1vZCBnaGF0kgEIbG9jYWxpdHk!5m1!1e4?hl=en)

Screenshot from Google Maps

Further, we conducted reserve image searches on the keyframes of the viral video which did not yield any relevant results. Then we scanned through the comment sections of the posts associated with the clip claiming to show a landslide at Anmod district. On analysing the comments to the Facebook reel posted by user ‘Ravi Ravi’, we noticed a reply from user ‘Shabbir Khan’ saying, “Last year video of Himachal (sic).”

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/Copy1.jpg)

Screenshot of comment section of Facebook post by Ravi Ravi

Taking a clue, we again conducted [Google](https://www.google.co.in/search?q=himachal+landslide&hl=en-IN&source=lnt&tbs=sbi%3AAMhZZivSvs3z78whOM2C5rgYsDoOoPLU1rokMQKniQkC1xyzQgHHKLxLHz3cmz_1oM9ee_1kbzJbXTWT5YnnTmXTzUpcUCh623oBJrc3HkBpdwnmaSL1xoncI8BAqJNVZ3CoTt5_1L4yV-0G9T4QF8suea9HBSGgfi2EX4hwkZq1Y6Eri6cFZM0KhrAe23TmVoTFnYfkvlQPyPuVixaXUI46qEBG9gb881gRyw4rSVjH4nqsN_19j283dtQnRap3XTKn3lBf4tv_17Z3B_1pim3Z6qn_1SrOROIDtm99d7iKvhuUU61MQnaDlI8egetn1x6pgI0nFkBc6v5nGN8jEu3bOQaXElWmErA8Rkfrw%2Ccdr%3A1%2Ccd_min%3A1%2F1%2F2021%2Ccd_max%3A12%2F31%2F2021&tbm=) reverse image searches on the keyframes of the viral video along with the keywords “Himachal Landslide” and adjusted the time frame of results from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2021. This led us to a video report by [NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/video/news/news/watch-dramatic-road-collapse-after-landslide-in-himachal-pradesh-595926) dated July 31, 2021 titled ‘Watch: Dramatic Road Collapse After Landslide In Himachal Pradesh.’

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/Copy-2.jpg)

Screenshot of Google search result

Featuring the same visuals as the viral video, the report detailed that a stretch of road collapsed as a hillside crashed down in dramatic visuals of a landslide in Himachal Pradesh. “The road caved at Sirmaur after two days of incessant rain. A clip that has been widely shared shows a chunk of the hillside falling, taking the road with it. About 100 metres of the road slides down and vanishes in moments. There are no reports of casualties,” it added.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/07/Com.jpg)

(L-R) Screenshot of video showing 2021 landslide in Himachal’s Sirmaur (Credits: NDTV) and screenshot of viral video (Credits: Facebook/Ravi Ravi)

Further, we conducted a keyword search for Sirmaur Landslide 2021 which led us to multiple media reports from July 2021 elaborating on the incident. One such report by [News18](https://www.news18.com/news/india/himachal-pradesh-sirmaur-passenger-bus-massive-landslide-washes-off-100m-road-4029026.html), carrying a longer version of the viral clip, stated that a landslide in Himachal Pradesh’s Sirmaur district led to an entire stretch of a 100m road collapsing into the valley below.

After the landslide incident, Ram Kumar Gautam, deputy commissioner, Sirmaur, held a video conferencing with officials from Paonta Sahib and Shillai and directed them to add barricades on both sides of slide point with the warning to people to remain alert on the road.”

You can read other reports on the incident [here](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/himachal-pradesh/story/video-landside-himachal-sirmaur-road-caves-watch-rescue-1834693-2021-07-30), [here](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/sirmaur-landslide-took-a-bus-along-with-portion-of-mountain-video-viral-101627707204958.html) and [here](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/scary-video-road-collapse-landslide-sirmaur-himachal-pradesh-7430659/).

## Conclusion

The viral video is neither recent nor shows visuals of the landslide at Anmod Ghat. The clip is from 2021 and shows a massive landslide in Himachal Pradesh’s Sirmaur.

## Result: False

**Our Sources**  
  
Report By **[NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/video/news/news/watch-dramatic-road-collapse-after-landslide-in-himachal-pradesh-595926)**, Dated July 31, 2021

# Old, Unrelated Videos Shared As Libya Floods

Written By [Kushel Madhusoodan](/author/kushel/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Sep 15, 2023

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/09/Thumbnail-1778.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

**Claim**  
Multiple videos showing the devastating floods in Libya that killed at least 10,000 people.  
  
**Fact**  
Viral videos were found to be of extreme-weather events in Japan, Saudi Arabia and Spain.

Several social media users are circulating multiple videos, purportedly of the devastating floods in Libya, particularly Derna, where at least 11,000 people [have been killed.](https://edition.cnn.com/2023/09/14/middleeast/lethal-factors-leading-to-libya-floods-intl/index.html) The videos can be seen [here](https://twitter.com/theunp0pu1ar/status/1702093937568342057), [here](https://twitter.com/journoturk/status/1701336393107066913) and [here.](https://twitter.com/lalitdubey1507/status/1702397040062505343)

 

## **The Libya Floods**

The death toll in Libya’s coastal city of Derna has soared to 11,300 with local officials suggesting that it could be much higher than announced. Daniel, an unusually strong Mediterranean storm, [caused deadly flooding](https://www.livemint.com/news/world/libya-flood-updates-death-toll-in-derna-rises-to-over-11-000-10-points-11694738257524.html) in communities across eastern Libya, where the worst-hit was Derna. As the storm pounded the coast on Sunday night, two dams outside the city collapsed causing floodwaters to gush down Wadi Derna, a valley that cuts through the city, crashing through buildings and washing people out to sea.

**Also Read:** [These Visuals Are Not From Ayodhya Ram Mandir. Here’s Where They Are Actually From](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/viral/debunked-these-visuals-are-not-from-ayodhya-ram-mandir-heres-where-they-are-actually-from/)

## **Video 1**

Newschecker ran a reverse image search of keyframes of the video, which led us to this [Facebook post,](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=395582301875640landslide) dated July 3, 2021, stating, “Massive landslide destroys a portion of the town in Izusan, Atami (Japan). Reports say over a dozen people were missing.”

A relevant keyword search led us to this [Al Jazeera report](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/3/japan-torrential-rains-unleash-landslides-20-missing-report), dated July 3, 2021, stating, “At least two people have been killed and many others have been reported missing on Saturday, after heavy rains hit Japan’s central city of Atami in Shizuoka, triggering landslides, according to the public broadcaster NHK.” Similar reports can be seen [here](https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/15478014/horror-landslide-japan-missing-buries-houses/) and [here,](https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/07/4fdfcd0277e5-heavy-rain-lashes-pacific-coast-of-japan-highest-alert-issued.html) confirming that the viral video is of the 2021 landslide in Japan.

## **Video 2**

Newschecker ran a reverse image search of keyframes of the video, which led us to this [Youtube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=v063it_3tTA), uploaded on April 8, 2016, stating that it is a flood at Wadi El Farsha.

A further search led us to multiple Facebook posts by Arabic media outlets, dated [April 8, 2016](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1269670986396258) and [April 9, 2016](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1032383040189958) respectively, stating that the clip showed a flood in Wadi Al Farshah in Saudi Arabia.

## **Video 3**

Newschecker noticed that several users in the comments pointed out that the video was from Spain. A relevant keyword search led us to this [Youtube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Umrf7HpK4u0), dated July 10, 2023, by 9 News Australia. “Vision has emerged from the Spanish city of Zaragoza, where streets have been inundated with water following torrential rain earlier this week,” read the description.

“A violent storm has caused major flooding in Zaragoza, Spain, making rescue efforts difficult and causing parked cars to be washed away by the raging water as their desperate owners cling to the roofs,” read a [Daily Express report](https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/1788601/car-drivers-cling-to-roofs-flash-flood-spain), dated July 7, 2023, confirming that the viral video is of the July 2023 flash flood in Spain. A similar report can be seen [here.](https://newsable.asianetnews.com/world/watch-cars-swept-away-residents-stranded-as-torrential-rains-trigger-flash-floods-in-spain-s-zaragoza-ajr-rxh9mf)

**Also Read:** [Debunking the Seismic Waves Card: Can It Really Hack Your Phone in Seconds?](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/financial-online-scams/debunking-the-seismic-waves-card-can-it-really-hack-your-phone-in-seconds/https://newschecker.in/fact-check/financial-online-scams/debunking-the-seismic-waves-card-can-it-really-hack-your-phone-in-seconds/)

## **Conclusion**

Old videos of landslides and floods in Saudi Arabia, Japan and Spain falsely claimed as visuals of the deadly 2023 Libya floods.

## **Result: False**

**Sources**  
[Al Jazeera report](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/3/japan-torrential-rains-unleash-landslides-20-missing-report), July 3, 2021  
[Facebook post](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1269670986396258), April 8, 2016  
[Youtube video,](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Umrf7HpK4u0) 9 News Australia, July 10, 2023

# This Video Doesn’t Show Bus Escaping Landslide in Himachal Pradesh

## Neither is this video recent nor is it related to Himachal Pradesh.

[Abhishek Anand](/author/1685310/abhishek-anand-7)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video of a bus crossing a narrow path during a landslide is being circulated on social media platforms with a claim that it shows a recent incident from [Himachal Pradesh](https://www.thequint.com/topic/himachal-pradesh)'s Chamba.

***(More archives of similar such claims could be found [here](https://archive.is/P1oLm) and [here](https://archive.is/ZH4VX).)***

**What is the truth?:** The video actually dates back to **May 2024** and shows a truck narrowly escaping a landslide in [Indonesia](https://www.thequint.com/topic/indonesia)'s Padang City. It has no connection with Himachal Pradesh.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find that out?: Team WebQoof** performed a simple Google Lens search on the keyframes of the viral clip and found similar [visuals posted](https://archive.is/WhmPw) on a YouTube channel called '@weathernetwork'.

* It was uploaded on 20 May 2024 with a title that said, "Truck escapes #landslide after prolonged heavy #rainfall in #Indonesia."

**Other sources:** Next, we found a news [report published](https://www.kompas.tv/video/508454/detik-detik-truk-bbm-nyaris-tertimbun-longsor-di-jalur-sitinjau-lauik) by *KompasTV* that said a truck nearly escaped a landslide while travelling in Padang City, West Sumatra in Indonesia.

* The route was closed for more than hours due to the landslide.
* The official YouTube channel of *tvOneNews* published [similar visuals](https://archive.is/kKYlN) on 17 May 2024 with a title when translated to English said, "Horrifying! This is the Moment a Truck Nearly Was Buried in a Landslide in Padang | AKIM tvOne."

**Conclusion:** It is evident that the viral video is old and unrelated to Himachal Pradesh.

# This Video of a Dog Being Rescued Is Old & Unrelated To Recent Wayanad Landslide

## Neither is this video recent nor is it connected to the recent landslide in Wayanad.

[Abhishek Anand](/author/1685310/abhishek-anand-7)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video which shows some people rescuing a dog, who can be seen stuck in mud, and two puppies is being shared on the internet as recent visuals from the landslide in [Kerala'](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/iuml-supporters-wearing-pakistan-cricket-team-jersey-kerala-viral-video-fact-check)s [Wayanad](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/old-image-idukki-kerala-disaster-shared-wayanad-landslide-fact-check).

**What have users said?:** Those sharing the video have uploaded it with a caption that said, "Big salute to rescue team....A dog and her two puppies rescued from Landslide...#WayanadDisaster #WaynadLandslide #Disaster."

At the time of writing this report, the post had garnered over **three lakh views** on the platform. ***(Archives of similar claims can be found [here](https://archive.is/9G7ET), [here](https://archive.is/VPNrw), and [here](https://perma.cc/K4NA-HETJ).)***

**What is the truth?:** The video is old and unrelated to the recent landslide in Wayanad. It could be traced back to October 2021 and reportedly shows a dog being rescued in [Palakkad](https://www.thequint.com/topic/palakkad), Kerala.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out?:** Using the help of Google Lens, we performed a reverse image search and came across a longer version of the video published on a [website](https://www.newsflare.com/video/459359/dog-and-her-two-pups-were-rescued-after-48-hours-as-they-were-struck-in-a-landslide-south-india#) called 'Newsflare'.

* It said that a dog and her two puppies were rescued on 15 October 2021 in the Palakkad district of Kerala.
* The incident happened after tonnes of earth slid down a mountainside due to heavy rains in the area.

**News reports:** Another round of reverse image search directed us to a news [report published](https://www.manoramaonline.com/environment/wild-life/2021/10/14/mama-dog-and-her-puppies-trapped-under-mudslide-rescued.html) in *Manorama Online*.

* The report said that locals came to the rescue of the dog after they heard the animal crying loudly.
* The dog and her two puppies (out of six) were rescued alive from underground.
* The report further mentioned that the landslide occurred at the house of a resident in Palakkad.

* A [report published](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2021/Oct/13/dog-and-two-pups-buried-in-kerala-landslide-rescued-after-three-day-ordeal-2371262.html) in *The New Indian Express* said that the animals were rescued after they lied covered in mud for three days behind a shop on the Palakkad–Malappuram border.
* The shopkeeper's husband, Ashraf, mentioned that only two puppies out of six could be saved.
* The report said that the dog and her puppies have been kept at a safe place and are regaining their health.

**Conclusion:** It is clear that the video is old and unrelated to the recent landslide in Wayanad.

# Years-old video of river rescue falsely linked to disaster in India's Uttarakhand state

* This article is more than one year old.
* Published on August 22, 2025 at 08:45
* 2 min read
* By [Devesh MISHRA](https://factcheck.afp.com/devesh-mishra),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

After a torrent of muddy water smashed into the town of Dharali in India's Uttarakhand state, killing at least four people with around 100 others missing, a video was shared in posts falsely claiming it showed residents being saved from roaring floodwaters in the tourist region. The video has in fact circulated since July 2022 in news reports about five youths who were rescued from a river swelled by monsoon rains in the neighbouring state of Himachal Pradesh.

"New video from Dharali," reads Hindi-language text superimposed on an [Instagram video](https://perma.cc/VQA6-RU4S) posted on August 6, 2025.

The clip shows two men who appear to be stranded on a rock in the middle of a fast-flowing river, as people on the riverbank attempt to pull them to safety using a rope.

The footage circulated a day after a [torrent of mud](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flash-flood-washes-himalayan-town-112014445.html) tore down a narrow mountain valley in India's Uttarakhand state before smashing into the town of Dharali, killing four people with around 100 others missing ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7J67-N8G4?type=image)).

Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the flood was caused by a sudden and intense "cloudburst", calling the destruction "extremely sad and distressing".

The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert warning for the tourist region, saying it had recorded "extremely heavy" rainfall of around 21 centimetres (eight inches) in isolated parts of Uttarakhand.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/fde541b40fd1303d3b9e5ba89201201c-en.jpeg?itok=CTiBOgF8)

Screenshot of the false Instagram post captured on August 22, 2025, with a red X added by AFP

The video was also shared in similar [Facebook](https://perma.cc/8WET-Q8P8), [Instagram](https://perma.cc/MX4M-W7QP) and [Threads](https://perma.cc/7X3H-HG7T) posts claiming it shows a rescue in Dharali.

But the Uttarakhand police refuted the claim on their [verified X account](https://x.com/uttarakhandcops/status/1952998484430471622) on August 6, calling it "completely false and misleading" ([archived link](https://perma.cc/SU99-PFRW)).

"The video has no connection with the Dharali. Please do not spread confusion by sharing wrong information on social media," read their Hindi-language statement.

## Himachal Pradesh river rescue

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared clip led to a longer version [published](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1bI4bXO_E2w) on the verified Indian Express Punjab YouTube channel on July 29, 2022 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/LWL5-TJ8Z)).

The media outlet's video is titled, "Nalagarh: Five migrants land in river to take photo, stuck in flash flood due to heavy rains".

Nalagarh is a city 200 kilometres (124 miles) west of Dharali, in the neighbouring state of Himachal Pradesh.

According to the video's description, the five men had been trapped by a flash flood caused by recent heavy rains.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/3c596a7b20378a02e4a66347d077401b-en.jpeg?itok=RW-qrUrC)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared clip (left) and the Indian Express Punjab video (right)

A screenshot from the footage was also used in a report by [The Tribune newspaper](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/himachal/five-youth-caught-in-flooded-river-rescued-in-nalagarh-417007/) ([archived link](https://perma.cc/UWN6-KTXA)).

"Five youth, who were caught in the midst of gushing river water near Gurukund village in Chikni river, were rescued after much effort by the locals last evening in Nalagarh sub-division," read the report.

The footage used by the Indian Express Punjab corresponds to [Google Street View imagery](https://maps.app.goo.gl/yve6cEmMdo4EzmEV9) of the landscape near Gurukund ([archived link](https://perma.cc/F2KB-KX2A?type=image)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/b5b8d9d22d3fa397d6d04129a9fd4e19-en.jpeg?itok=hfHROSTK)

Screenshot comparison of the Indian Express Punjab footage (left) and Google Street View imagery near Gurukund (right), with corresponding features highlighted by AFP

AFP has previously [debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.68384WE) other false claims related to India's [monsoon rains](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.699E6CQ).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/37c2bd4ceffd812d4db65c1ac191a577-en.jpeg?itok=OCgUaTSI)

# Old video of flash flood in India's Uttarakhand resurfaces with false 'broken dam' claim

* This article is more than two years old.
* Published on July 19, 2024 at 08:48
* 2 min read
* By [Sachin BAGHEL](https://factcheck.afp.com/sachin-baghel),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

An old video of a flash flood in Uttarakhand has resurfaced in social media posts that falsely claimed it showed water rushing from a broken dam in the northern Indian state in July 2024, when the region was battered by incessant monsoon rains. The clip has circulated since February 2021, when an avalanche damaged the under-construction Tapovan Vishnugad dam and caused deadly flooding. A state disaster management authority officer told AFP that no dam had been damaged in the current monsoon season.

"Be careful, NTPC dam of Rishi Ganga and Tapovan has broken. By evening the water will cross Chamoli," read part of the Hindi-language caption to a [video](https://perma.cc/T5NU-S6HM) shared on X on July 6, 2024.

The caption is referring to the Tapovan Vishnugad hydropower plant in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand state, operated by the [National Thermal Power Corporation](https://ntpc.co.in/index.php/about-us/our-journey) (NTPC) ([archived link](https://perma.cc/G8QK-QRXZ)).

The video, which was viewed thousands of times, appears to show rushing floodwaters next to a rural road.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2024-07/7520bc64fc5c52e9811ca4cd0df315cd876c6718.jpeg?itok=nlDOVzEl)

Screenshot of the false X post, captured on July 18, 2024

The video was shared with similar captions elsewhere on [X](https://perma.cc/UY78-Q25K) and [Facebook](https://perma.cc/6D79-A3UB?type=image), where it was viewed more than 20,000 times in total.

It circulated after monsoon rains deluged Uttarakhand, with [The Indian Express](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/weather-update-rainfall-uttarakhand-himachal-char-dham-yatra-monsoon-9438270/) newspaper reporting landslides had blocked roads and rivers had swelled to near dangerous levels ([archived link](https://perma.cc/DEB5-Z4AM)).

Monsoon rains across South Asia from June to September offer respite from the summer heat and are crucial to replenishing water supplies, but also bring widespread [death and destruction](https://perma.cc/HP7H-YETN).

The number of fatal floods and landslides has increased in recent years, however, and experts say climate change is exacerbating the problem.

The video circulating online, however, is unrelated to the monsoon season.

### Old video

A reverse image search on Google using keyframes from the video led to the same footage posted on X [here](https://x.com/SmritiSharma_/status/1358349803743105024) and [here](https://x.com/Virenderbabrbjp/status/1358442825256374273) on February 7, 2021 (archived links [here](https://perma.cc/E6DD-GP5U) and [here](https://perma.cc/M2PX-LM84)).

AFP reported at the time that a [flash flood](https://perma.cc/JL26-44QB) in Uttarakhand -- thought to have been caused by a breaking glacier -- sent a barrage of water and debris hurtling down a valley at terrifying speed and with frightening power, sweeping away bridges and roads, and hitting two hydroelectric plants.

Below is a screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (left) and the same clip posted in February 2021 (right):

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2024-07/b3be4959da9a750d267baa1b8d1f773b6d24387e.jpeg?itok=8Fpw_2il)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (left) and the same clip posted in February 2021 (right)

A report by the [National Disaster Management Authority](https://ndma.gov.in/sites/default/files/PDF/Reports/Detalied_report_UK_Disaster.pdf) published in April 2022 said 204 people were killed in the disaster ([archived link](https://perma.cc/VX5D-5ZPF?type=image)).

It also concluded the disaster was caused by a rock and ice avalanche, echoing the findings of [research](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abh4455) published in the journal Science on June 10, 2021 ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20240718062136/https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abh4455)).

The [Chamoli police](https://x.com/chamolipolice/status/1809465290016555486) and the [Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority](https://x.com/chamolipolice/status/1809566180245491729) have also refuted the claim, saying the video was from 2021 (archived links [here](https://perma.cc/2WK4-SSFL) and [here](https://perma.cc/6X33-5PX6)).

Nand Kishor Joshi, a district disaster management officer for Chamoli, told AFP that no dam had been damaged.

"This video is old and has nothing to do with the current monsoon season," he said on July 18, 2024.

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2024-07/b7f3c70aa65fa7548579c1903f881f3498dd80f0.jpeg?itok=Q4Ln_4J1)

# Old video from Italy falsely shared as visuals of the August 2025 Uttarakhand flash flood

![Varun Borugadda](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/77de1408da09a7ec42c70d3d2369e35e27bae0863030d0f1c34b04f3ddce91e2?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Varun Borugadda](https://factly.in/author/varun-borugadda/ "Posts by Varun Borugadda")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/old-video-from-italy-falsely-shared-as-visuals-of-the-august-2025-uttarakhand-flash-flood/#respond)2 Mins Read

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fold-video-from-italy-falsely-shared-as-visuals-of-the-august-2025-uttarakhand-flash-flood%2F "Share on Facebook")   [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fold-video-from-italy-falsely-shared-as-visuals-of-the-august-2025-uttarakhand-flash-flood%2F&text=Old%20video%20from%20Italy%20falsely%20shared%20as%20visuals%20of%20the%20August%202025%20Uttarakhand%20flash%20flood "Share on X (Twitter)")   [Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fold-video-from-italy-falsely-shared-as-visuals-of-the-august-2025-uttarakhand-flash-flood%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F%2F2025%2F08%2FVIsuals-of-the-Uttarakand-Flash-Floods-Thumbnail-.jpg&description=Old%20video%20from%20Italy%20falsely%20shared%20as%20visuals%20of%20the%20August%202025%20Uttarakhand%20flash%20flood "Share on Pinterest")   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fold-video-from-italy-falsely-shared-as-visuals-of-the-august-2025-uttarakhand-flash-flood%2F "Share on LinkedIn")   [Tumblr](https://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fold-video-from-italy-falsely-shared-as-visuals-of-the-august-2025-uttarakhand-flash-flood%2F&name=Old%20video%20from%20Italy%20falsely%20shared%20as%20visuals%20of%20the%20August%202025%20Uttarakhand%20flash%20flood "Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

In the wake of the 5 August 2025 [Uttarakhand flash flood disaster](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c78zjd8xj2xo), a video ([here](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DM-jOqwztN0/) and [h](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DNelmORq2-w/)[e](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DNelmORq2-w/)[re](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DNelmORq2-w/)) showing muddy water rapidly surging through a canal is being shared on social media, with captions claiming the visuals show the recent flash floods in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district (the floods were in [Uttarakashi district](https://www.newindianexpress.com/thesundaystandard/2025/Aug/17/lake-burst-behind-uttarakhand-flash-flood-mha-told)). We will fact-check this claim through this article.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2025/08/VIsuals-of-the-Uttarakand-Flash-Floods-Claim--1024x945.jpg)

An archived version of this post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/43276825?key=b91d0b745d0355ac739e0cd8dceba8d8).

> **Claim:** Visuals of the flash flood occurred in Uttarakhand on 5 August 2025.  
>   
> **Fact:** The video actually depicts a flash flood in Bardonecchia, Italy, not Uttarakhand. Hence, the claim made in the post is **Misleading**.

To verify the claim, we performed a reverse-image search on a few keyframes from the video. The search led us to an older upload of this video on the ‘*The Sun’s*’ YouTube channel and website ([here](https://youtu.be/Nsb9eSzAEgQ?t=7) and [here](https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/35644755/flash-floods-italy-death-trapped/)).

[Uploaded](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nsb9eSzAEgQ) on 1 July 2025, the footage is part of a compilation that shows a devastating flood in Bardonecchia, Italy. The description of this video highlights that ‘*At least one person has been killed in the fierce floods caused by heavy rains, the authorities announced, as extreme weather events become more frequent.*’ Flooding has occurred in the Frejus River.

Apart from this, we also found the viral footage in videos posted ([here](https://x.com/RoyaNewsEnglish/status/1939987349225853402) and [here](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=24835666849354386)) by various media organisations on social media describing it as the visuals of the flooding that occurred in Bardonecchia, Italy.

> Powerful floods hit Italian town of Bardonecchia after heavy rainfall. [pic.twitter.com/QFqVfcDkMM](https://t.co/QFqVfcDkMM)
>
> — Roya News English (@RoyaNewsEnglish) [July 1, 2025](https://x.com/RoyaNewsEnglish/status/1939987349225853402?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Furthermore, we found media reports ([here](https://torinocronaca.it/news/provincia/528788/maltempo-esondazione-a-bardonecchia-si-ripete-il-disastro-di-due-anni-fa-notizia-in-aggiornamento.html), [here](https://tg24.sky.it/cronaca/2025/06/30/maltempo-piemonte-rio-frejus-esondazione-bardonecchia), [here](https://www.virgilio.it/notizie/dirette/live/allerta-maltempo-bardonecchia-esondazione-frejus-diretta-1687823), and [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmpZtFfSMYY)) from 30 June 2025 and 1 July 2025 on this flooding incident, reportedly caused due to torrential rains. According to these reports, the person who lost his life due to these floods is Franco Chiaffrino, a 70-year-old fruit seller.

To sum up, the viral clip of gushing floodwater is from a flood in Bardonecchia, Italy, not Uttarakhand.

# Old Footage From Uttarakhand Linked To Flash Floods In Nepal

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Kushel Madhusoodan

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[News](/fact-check/news/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Aug 27, 2026

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2026/08/Newest-8.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## Claim

A [video](https://archive.ph/6bpzq) showing water and debris rushing down from a mountainous area and sweeping away homes is being shared online as visuals from the recent flash floods in Nepal.

![Old Footage From Uttarakhand Linked To Flash Floods In Nepal](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2026/08/ne1.jpg)

Screengrab from Facebook post by @UpTrend000

**Also Read: [Old, Unrelated Videos Go Viral Amid Flash Floods In Nepal](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/old-unrelated-videos-go-viral-amid-flash-floods-in-nepal)**

## Fact

A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post by [Times of India](https://www.instagram.com/p/DM-HSFMSxmk/), dated August 5, 2025, carrying visuals from the same incident. The post reported that at least four people had died after flash floods swept through Dharali village in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, following a cloudburst in the upper catchment area of the Kheer Ganga river.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2026/08/ne2.jpg)

Screengrab from Instagram post by TOI

A [Dainik Bhaskar](https://www.bhaskarenglish.in/national/news/uncut-video-cloudburst-uttarakhand-debris-buries-dharali-village-on-riverbank-135613681.html) report, also dated August 5, 2025, carried visuals from the same incident and reported that a cloudburst struck Uttarkashi. The resulting floodwaters and debris surged through the Kheer Ganga river and devastated Dharali village.

The incident was also reported by [India Today](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0UIb-JB6gU) on the same day, stating that a cloudburst near Uttarkashi had caused water, debris and silt to flow through Dharali, washing away houses and other structures. At least four people were confirmed dead, while more than 50 were reported missing.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2026/08/ne3-1024x579.jpg)

Screengrab from YouTube video by India Today

**Also Read: [Video From Brazil Falsely Shared To Claim Foreigner Kidnapped, Gang-Raped In India](https://www.newschecker.in/fact-check/video-from-brazil-falsely-shared-to-claim-foreigner-gang-raped-in-india)**

Hence, we could conclude that an old video from the August 2025 cloudburst in Uttarakhand is being falsely linked to the flash floods in Nepal. 

**Sources**   
Report By [Times of India](https://www.instagram.com/p/DM-HSFMSxmk/), Dated August 5, 2025  
Report By [Dainik Bhaskar](https://www.bhaskarenglish.in/national/news/uncut-video-cloudburst-uttarakhand-debris-buries-dharali-village-on-riverbank-135613681.html), Dated August 5, 2025  
Report By [India Today](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0UIb-JB6gU), Dated August 5, 2025
