# Dramatic footage of flash flood in India falsely linked to Pakistan downpours

* This article is more than one year old.
* Published on August 28, 2025 at 11:29
* 2 min read
* By [Rimal FARRUKH](https://factcheck.afp.com/rimal-farrukh),  [Devesh MISHRA](https://factcheck.afp.com/devesh-mishra),  [AFP Pakistan](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-pakistan),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

Intense monsoon downpours have killed hundreds in Pakistan's northwest Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province but dramatic footage of floodwaters sweeping through a hillside village was in fact filmed in Uttarakhand state in neighbouring India. Similar footage also previously circulated in news reports about the flash flood that engulfed the village of Dharali.

"Cloud Burst in Buner, Swat -- A Reminder from Allah," reads superimposed text on a [TikTok video](https://perma.cc/N3LS-JZWJ) viewed more than 78,000 times since it was posted on August 19, 2025.

The caption of the video, showing raging floodwaters sweeping down a valley before smashing into buildings, also says it shows a cloud burst in the Swat district of northwestern Pakistan's mountainous Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

The province has been one of the hardest hit by a torrential spell of [monsoon rains](https://www.barrons.com/news/pakistan-s-monsoon-misery-nature-s-fury-man-s-mistake-7762a387), with more than 450 people killed in flooding and landslides triggered by the downpours ([archived link](https://perma.cc/T2HS-9GNN)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/6dadee89d4ee29dfededeb486d855e57-en.jpeg?itok=SmzJiYzq)

Screenshot of the false TikTok video captured on August 28, 2025, with a red X added by AFP

The same clip was also shared in similar [YouTube](https://perma.cc/AA8P-TTCF) and [TikTok](https://perma.cc/S2BS-9FJH) posts claiming it was filmed in Pakistan.

But the video in fact shows a flash flood in neighbouring India.

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared clip led to similar footage used in an August 5 [BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c78zjd8xj2xo) report titled "Dozens feared trapped as cloudburst triggers flash floods in India" ([archived link](https://perma.cc/Y454-NZM5)).

The footage is credited to the [The Press Trust of India](https://www.ptinews.com/), and the report says it shows Dharali village in Uttarkashi district ([archived link](https://perma.cc/V4EL-2QNB)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/a3e8b761713e649d0aab99abeb2f6094-en.jpeg?itok=qMCzUVdk)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared clip (left) and the footage used by BBC News (right)

A similar video was also shared by video agency [Newsflare](https://www.newsflare.com/video/772892/massive-flood-hits-khir-ganga-river-in-uttarkashi-dharali-village-ravaged-by-debris-and-sludge), where its title reads in part: "Dharali Village Ravaged by Debris and Sludge" ([archived link](https://perma.cc/E6G7-ZV7F)).

Moreover, features visible in the falsely shared clip correspond to Google Maps [clips](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Mukhba+Temple/@31.0442976,78.779374,3a,75y,90t/data=!3m8!1e5!3m6!1sCIHM0ogKEICAgIDxx7TXRQ!2e10!3e10!6shttps:%2F%2Flh3.googleusercontent.com%2Fgps-cs-s%2FAC9h4nroix6UKK9sKFUG2-e6N1IN1EQV7xdsl2pyXZzrbJ2jPuhsQRO_bxSOTd1EuMxFVHWli0qzzIdfg1N7ZEMuEYRGdhCKmP3QpVBeFwEFL3L1IMvrP5iq9cdwiUvrlPFtFnW-sFk%3Dw203-h114-k-no!7i1920!8i1080!4m9!3m8!1s0x39087c0315555555:0x689e58fa86fd14ee!8m2!3d31.0442976!4d78.779374!10e5!14m1!1BCgIgAQ!16s%2Fg%2F11gb4jvpt5!5m1!1e4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDgyNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) and [photos](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Mukhba+Temple/@31.0442976,78.7791549,-38a,25.6y/data=!3m8!1e2!3m6!1sCIABIhB9sTlBOrbvTmbj6-Q6tnvF!2e10!3e12!6shttps:%2F%2Flh3.googleusercontent.com%2Fgps-cs-s%2FAC9h4nrYQNY2zywBjtc9QRrfzIjNZMsnihXAmhAsNCZkNm2cxPUjMHLc_kfvVe9Tpom45sIfQ32qUYolpaDaGpXgRfy3K222kaVgVy-QqvXNHVsla6xlctL2rEO4xnlP-bAiUMTk-D4h9EZ_iTP0%3Dw203-h270-k-no!7i4284!8i5712!4m9!3m8!1s0x39087c0315555555:0x689e58fa86fd14ee!8m2!3d31.0442976!4d78.779374!10e5!14m1!1BCgIgAQ!16s%2Fg%2F11gb4jvpt5!5m1!1e4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDgyNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) of the area (archived [here](https://perma.cc/G8ER-Z6FM?type=image) and [here](https://perma.cc/S7ZL-ZGGC?type=image)).

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-08/8f2ab43a8685a1387ecf85e7b51e732a-en.jpeg?itok=TEYuOLM7)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared clip (left) and a Google Maps photo of the area from June 2025 (right), with corresponding features highlighted by AFP

# Old, Unrelated Videos Falsely Linked To Assam Floods

Written By [Kushel Madhusoodan](/author/kushel/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[News](/fact-check/news/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Jun 10, 2025

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/06/Kushel-One-Rating-Article-Thumbnails-New-Brand-9.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## **Claim**

Two videos claiming to show the devastation caused by the heavy rainfall in Assam, washing away shops and flooding railway tracks.

The archived version of the posts can be seen [here](https://archive.is/goalD) and [here.](https://archive.is/qEVfe)

## **Heavy Rain Wreaks Havoc In Assam**

Over six lakh people were [reportedly](https://www.deccanherald.com/india/assam/flood-dam-water-aggravate-poverty-migration-in-assam-villages-3578037) affected in 21 districts of the northeastern state in the first wave of floods and landslides caused by the torrential rainfall this year, between May 31 and June 6.

## **Fact**

## **Video 1**

Newschecker ran a reverse image search of keyframes, which led us to the [same video uploaded on Instagram on September 8, 2024](https://www.instagram.com/p/C_pHwZgvMXg/), well before the ongoing flood situation in Assam. The caption states the video is from July 9, 2023, with the hashtags #Sainj #valley.

The same video was [uploaded on Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/k95Yfi__4h0) on September 9, 2024, with the description using the hashtags # #sainjvalley #himachal pradesh#flood, along with the same date, “09/07/2023”.

A relevant keyword search led us to this [Indian Express report](https://web.archive.org/web/20230911214827/https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/chandigarh/himachal-pradesh-thunaj-sainj-second-flood-in-11-months-8835254/), dated July 14, 2023, on the devastation caused by the gushing water in Sainj valley of Kullu in Himachal Pradesh. “Sainj, with a total population of around 34,000 people, saw its local market with 200 shops devastated. Of the 200 shops in the markets — including those that were eating joints sold readymade clothes, gifts or stuff of daily needs — nearly 43 were flattened by the floodwater,” read the report, which added that a video of a flooding incident from July 9 had gone viral showing uprooted trees and silted flood water swallowing everything in its path as it cut through a market. A similar report by [The Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/himachal/40-shops-30-houses-washed-away-at-sainj-in-kullu-district-524851/) dated July 12, 2023, stated that as many as 40 shops and 30 houses were washed away because of flooding by the Sainj river.

Although we could not yet independently verify the location of the video, we can confirm that it predates the 2025 Assam floods.

## **Video 2**

Newschecker noticed that one of the train coaches carried the acronym “CR”, which stands for Central Railway that operates the suburban railway system in Mumbai. Also, [we learnt](https://nfr.indianrailways.gov.in/view_section.jsp?fontColor=black&backgroundColor=LIGHTSTEELBLUE&lang=0&id=0,1) that the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) operates trains in Guwahati, contradicting the viral claim that the video is from Guwahati railway station.

We then ran a reverse image search of keyframes, which led us to the [same video on Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qVt-ic-EOW4), dated May 27, 2025, headlined “Mumbai ki Baarish”, while the text on the video reads, “Masjid Mumbai”.

A relevant keyword search led us to multiple news reports, seen [here](https://theprint.in/india/incessant-rainfall-causes-waterlogging-in-parts-of-mumbai-suburban-train-services-hit/2637259/) and [here,](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/trains-crawl-roads-waterlogged-buses-diverted-as-mumbai-reels-under-heavy-rain-yellow-alert-upgraded-to-orange/articleshow/121405638.cms) stating that hours of incessant rainfall caused waterlogging in several low-lying areas of Mumbai and on railway tracks on May 26, 2025, especially at Masjid, Byculla, Dadar, Matunga and Badlapur railway stations.

We also came across this [Pune Mirror post](https://x.com/ThePuneMirror/status/1926915026373197830) on X, dated May 26, 2025, stating that flooding has turned Masjid Bandar station into a stream. We further noticed a board in the background of the viral video reading, “Masjid”, indicating the station’s name and further confirming that the viral claim was false.

# Old video of Buddha statue in floodwaters falsely linked to Nepal-Tibet disaster

* Published on September 3, 2026 at 10:18
* 2 min read
* By [Livia LIU](https://factcheck.afp.com/livia-liu),  [Tolera FIKRU GEMTA](https://factcheck.afp.com/tolera-fikru-gemta),  [AFP Hong Kong](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-hong-kong),  [AFP Ethiopia](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-ethiopia)

Catastrophic flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border in August 2026 killed hundreds of people and left thousands more missing, but a video circulating on social media showing a Buddha statue standing serenely in floodwaters predates the disaster by nearly two years. The statue is located in Bharatpur, Nepal, and the footage was filmed during flooding in September 2024.

The [post](https://perma.cc/SD9S-NYBS) shared on Facebook on August 30, 2026, contains a caption in English that reads: “Nepal flood and Buddha”

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/05eecea78c5fa494579f9988b00a4c6d-en.jpeg?itok=LHX9M4Pp)

Screenshot of the false post, taken on September 1, 2026

The video shows a Buddha statue standing strong against rushing floodwaters.

The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods has [surpassed](https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/9/1/nepal-says-death-toll-rises-to-987-bringing-total-killed-past-1-000-1408) 1,000, as Chinese and Nepali rescuers search for survivors, including people feared trapped in hydropower tunnels (archived [here](https://perma.cc/627D-8U2V)).

More than 4,000 people remain missing after a massive wave of freezing water, rocks and debris swept downstream, destroying settlements across Nepal on August 26, 2026.

However, the circulating video predates the August 2026 disaster.

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared video led to a similar clip posted on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/I_AliFdgNl8) almost two years earlier, on September 28, 2024 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/4R4C-ARKN?type=standard)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/92d6a0e746d61fc634b63987a87e9d84-en.jpeg?itok=eiFiVZld)

Screenshots comparing the original video (left) and the false, taken on September 1, 2026

Nepalese media organisation Republica [published](https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/water-level-of-narayani-river-crosses-danger-mark) a similar image in a September 28, 2024, report about water levels in the Narayani River reaching a dangerous threshold ([archived link](https://perma.cc/GL5D-G2UP)).

At the time, large swathes of Nepal had been inundated with [monsoon downpours](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40324560/) that triggered deadly floods and landslides ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260830031122/https://www.brecorder.com/news/40324560/)).

Features of a [geotagged Google Maps photo](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Vwub9FisgocGtJag8) of the statue on the Narayani River in Bharatpur, in Nepal's Chitwan District, resemble the falsely shared video ([archived link](https://perma.cc/GC7F-B4UC?type=image)).

The statue is more than 110 kilometres (about 68 miles) from the Nepal-Tibet border, where the August 26 disaster occurred.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/004d8e5987094ab0016f25853d1283f0-en.jpeg?itok=BrC6mWC2)

Screenshots comparing the original video (left) and the false, taken on September 1, 2026

An [aerial video](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/drone-footage-shows-debris-along-125209731.html) of the debris-littered banks of the Narayani River in August 26 shows that the water level near the [Buddha statue](https://maps.app.goo.gl/C9bd4oJvatze9S4w9), at around the 30-second mark, was not as high as depicted in the falsely shared video (archived [here](https://perma.cc/5AMN-DFBY) and [here](https://perma.cc/P2LV-46M9?type=image)).

People who live near the statue told AFP Fact Check via WhatsApp on August 28 that flooding there was not as significant as the falsely shared video shows, but it did bring a lot of debris.

AFP Fact Check has debunked other misinformation about the [Nepal-Tibet floods](https://factcheck.afp.com/fact-checking-search-results?search_api_fulltext=Nepal-Tibet).

# 2017 Video of Bihar Bridge Collapse Shared as Recent Visuals From Assam Floods

## The video is from Bihar's Araria, where a bridge collapsed due to flash floods in 2017.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Aa

Large

Edited By :[Ahamad Fuwad](/author/1624194/ahamad-fuwad)

A video, showing a family of three falling down and drowning as a bridge collapses, is being shared on social media with a claim that this incident happened recently in the flood-hit [Assam](https://www.thequint.com/topic/assam-flood).

However, the video dates back to August 2017 when a bridge collapsed in [Bihar’s Araria district](https://www.thequint.com/videos/news-videos/bridge-collapse-due-to-flood-claims-three-lives-in-araria-bihar) due to flash floods. Three people reportedly lost their lives due to the bridge collapse.

The recent flood and landslides in [Assam](https://www.thequint.com/news/breaking-news/assam-floods-18-dead-across-31-districts-nearly-7-lakh-affected) has affected up to 31 out of 33 districts in the state, leaving more than seven lakh people affected.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**CLAIM**

The caption with the video reads, "Present Situation in North East India . #Landslide , #Flood : #Assam #Manipur #Nagaland #Meghalaya."

Similar claims are shared on Facebook and Twitter which can be seen [here](https://perma.cc/9CXR-RGS5), [here](https://perma.cc/T5Q4-JDTM) and [here](https://archive.ph/0dk6E).

**WHAT WE FOUND OUT**

Using InVID, a video verification tool, we divided the video into multiple keyframes and ran a reverse image search on them. This led us to a [YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e1IC4Ld9kkE) posted on **18 August 2017** by news agency Asian News International (ANI)**.**

According to the description of the video, the visual was shot in Araria district in Bihar when the state was hit by heavy floods. It added that three people drowned after a bridge connecting a village collapsed.

Several other news media outlets like *[Deccan Chronicle](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/190817/chasing-life-woman-child-meet-with-death-in-bihar.html), [NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/watch-as-a-bridge-collapses-in-flood-hit-bihar-while-people-cross-it-1739584), [India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/video/bihar-rains-flash-floods-araria-bridge-collapses-3-washed-away-987080-2017-08-17)* and *[Scroll](https://scroll.in/latest/847667/watch-three-die-after-bridge-collapses-over-a-raging-river-in-bihars-araria-district)* also carried this video.

> **[The Quint](https://www.thequint.com/videos/news-videos/bridge-collapse-due-to-flood-claims-three-lives-in-araria-bihar#read-more)** had also reported on the same incident in 2017. The article mentioned that the bridge collapsed because of the heavy flow of the flood water which claimed lives of a man, a woman, and a child.

The [article](https://www.thequint.com/videos/news-videos/bridge-collapse-due-to-flood-claims-three-lives-in-araria-bihar#read-more) also mentioned that the three were trying to cross the bridge when it collapsed. The family got swept away in the water along with the debris.

Evidently, an old video from the Bihar floods is being falsely linked to the recent floods in Assam.

# Old Video Of House Collapsing Into River In Kerala Falsely Linked To 2023 Chennai Floods

Written By [Kushel Madhusoodan](/author/kushel/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Dec 6, 2023

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/12/Kushel-One-Rating-Article-Thumbnails-New-Brand-6.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

**Claim**  
Floodwaters sweep away a house in Chennai following heavy rain triggered by Cyclone Michaung in December 2023.  
  
**Fact**  
Video dates back to October 2021, taken during the flash floods in Kerala.

Several social media users are circulating a video, which shows a house collapsing into a river, claiming that the incident happened in Chennai, where heavy rainfall and floods triggered by Cyclone Michaung in December 2023 has displaced over 18,000 people and killed at least eight.

> Dear friends in Chennai..plz stay safe & secure. Go out only if necessary.Pretty scary visuals. But stay calm. [#ChennaiFloods](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChennaiFloods?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#ChennaiRains2023](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChennaiRains2023?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#ChennaRains](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChennaRains?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#ChennaiCyclone](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChennaiCyclone?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#CycloneMichuang](https://twitter.com/hashtag/CycloneMichuang?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)[#Portalcoin](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Portalcoin?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Portalcoin](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Portalcoin?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)  
>  <https://t.co/CvQCvOY0M7>
>
> — Sachin Pal (@Sachin\_7995) [December 6, 2023](https://twitter.com/Sachin_7995/status/1732233007753544157?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

  

The archived versions of the tweets can be seen [here](https://archive.is/KkX3s) and [here.](https://archive.is/Ri6AR)

## **Fact Check**

Newschecker first ran a reverse image search of keyframes of the video, which led us to this [Youtube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Xfntr7EEbc), dated October 18, 2021, headlined, “Kerala Flood: Dramatic House Collapse in Kottayam”.

We then came across this [Newsminute report,](https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/video-captures-two-storey-house-kerala-completely-collapsing-gushing-river-156607) dated October 17, 2021, sharing the video, stating that the incident happened at Mundakayam, a town located in Kanjirappally taluk of Kerala’s Kottayam district.  According to the report, which identified the river as Manimala, the collapse took place on the morning of October 17. “The two-storey house was located in Koottickal near Mundakayam. The first floor of the house was built at the same level as the road, while the ground floor was below and adjacent to the river. The house seemed to have unhinged from the road after it developed deep cracks on the ground of the first floor. As the floods and the landslide in Koottickal —  triggered by heavy rainfall — washed the soil along with it, the foundation of the house gave way,” read the report.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/CVIaXqXJenK/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
>
> [A post shared by The News Minute (@thenewsminute)](https://www.instagram.com/p/CVIaXqXJenK/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

“Kerala has been witnessing extreme rainfall since Saturday, which caused a series of landslides in various parts of the Kottayam district, including Koottickal and Kokkayar panchayats. The landslide in Koottickal claimed the lives of 12 people, while five died in the Kokkayar landslide,” added the report.

Similar reports can be seen [here](https://www.theguardian.com/world/video/2021/oct/18/india-floodwaters-sweep-away-house-in-kerala-video) and [here](https://www.ndtv.com/kerala-news/video-house-swept-away-as-kerala-witnesses-heavy-rain-2578676), confirming that viral video is from the 2021 flash floods in Kerala.

 

**Also Read:** [Qatar Quashes Death Sentences Of 8 Ex-Indian Navy Personnel? No, Viral Claim Is False](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/qatar-quashes-death-sentences-of-8-ex-indian-navy-personnel-no-viral-claim-is-false/)

## **Conclusion**

Viral video showing house collapsing into a river is old and not related to the 2023 Chennai floods.

## **Result: False**

**Sources**  
[The Newsminute report](https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/video-captures-two-storey-house-kerala-completely-collapsing-gushing-river-156607), October 17, 2021  
[NDTV report,](https://www.ndtv.com/kerala-news/video-house-swept-away-as-kerala-witnesses-heavy-rain-2578676) October 17, 2021

# Fact-Check: Old Video From Pakistan Falsely Linked to Bangladesh Floods

## This video is from Pakistan and predates the floods happening in Bangladesh.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Large

A video of overflowing river is going viral on social media to claim that it is a recent footage from [Bangladesh](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/bangladesh-old-video-jagannath-ratha-yatra-electrocution-not-hindu-muslim-angle-fact-check) floods.

***(Archives of similar claims can be seen [here](https://perma.cc/YQ7T-5E6K)******and [here](https://perma.cc/G3CA-LEG9).)***

**What's the truth?:** This video is from Pakistan and predates the floods happening in Bangladesh.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out the truth?:** We performed a reverse image search on some of the keyframes of the video and this led us to an old YouTube video shared on 8 August, which predates the Bangladesh floods.

* The title stated that the video is from Tala Gang after heavy rains.

* Taking a cue, we performed a relevant keyword search on Google and this led us to video reports about this incident from 8 August.
* Pakistani news channels, *[HUM News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OkgI-d_xN_s&t=19s)* and *[We News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8W2z_QC3N4),* also shared the same video and stated that this video is from Tala Gang, Pakistan where heavy rainfall has caused havoc.
* We reached out Lubna Jerar Naqvi, a fact-checker and a journalist from Pakistan who confirmed to us that this video is from Pakistan.
* Naqvi also forwarded us a video report from *[Dawn](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GlbjFxMUs6U)* that was shared on 1 August.
* The video showed the same bridge as seen in the viral video and the titled stated that this visual of flood situation is from Chitral, Pakistan.

We also found the location on [Google](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/@32.9575294,72.5018721,207m/data=!3m1!1e3!5m1!1e4?entry=ttu) [Maps](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/@32.9575294,72.5018721,207m/data=!3m1!1e3!5m1!1e4?entry=ttu) but no street view was available.

**Conclusion:** An old video from Pakistan showing an overflowing river is being falsely shared as from Bangladesh.

# Cyclone Ditwah: Old Video From Kolkata Shared As Massive Flooding In Chennai

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Kushel Madhusoodan

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Dec 3, 2025

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/12/New-Cover-Vausdha-2025-12-03T173402.913.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## Claim

As the remnants of Cyclone Ditwah lash Chennai and its neighbouring districts with incessant rainfall, a [video](https://archive.ph/PV6fp) showing severe flooding on the roads, where several parked cars can be seen partially submerged, is going viral on social media, with users claiming it depicts the current situation in Tamil Nadu’s capital.

![Cyclone Ditwah: Old Video From Kolkata Shared As Massive Flooding In Chennai](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/12/c1.jpg)

Screengrab from X post by @AnveshkaD

**Also Read:** [Cyclone Ditwah -Old Photo From Hyderabad Shared To Show Flooding In Sri Lanka](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/cyclone-ditwah-old-photo-from-hyderabad-shared-to-show-flooding-in-sri-lanka)

## Fact

A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led Newschecker to a Facebook post by [Kais Kalim](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1841431486754837), dated September 25, 2025. It featured a shorter version of the same video, identifying it to be from Kolkata.

![Cyclone Ditwah: Old Video From Kolkata Shared As Massive Flooding In Chennai](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/12/c4.jpg)

Screengrab from Facebook post by Kais Kalim

Additionally, on closely analysing the viral video, we identified a vehicle with the licence plate WB, indicating West Bengal.

Further, we spotted multiple hoardings such as “Royal Indian Restaurant”, ” Golden Meat shop,” “Reliance Optician” among others. Taking clues from the same, we were able to [locate](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Golden+Meat/@22.5409721,88.3656569,3a,75y,257.31h,91.24t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1syXwgXT_vIhnpR8vXK_-3Zg!2e0!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fcb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile%26w%3D900%26h%3D600%26pitch%3D-1.2376579679707191%26panoid%3DyXwgXT_vIhnpR8vXK_-3Zg%26yaw%3D257.30764747263214!7i13312!8i6656!4m9!3m8!1s0x3a0276e08f3672eb:0x748e0ca6eb47638f!8m2!3d22.5410168!4d88.3653856!10e5!14m1!1BCgIgARICCAI!16s%2Fg%2F11f2b5wjgf?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MTEzMC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) the site seen in the viral footage in Kolkata.

 

(L-R) Screengrabs from viral clip and screengrabs from Google Images

Newschecker was not independently able to confirm when the footage was originally recorded, but our verification confirms that the location is not Chennai and predates the current bout of incessant rainfall in Tamil Nadu. Hence, the viral video claiming to show extensive flooding in Chennai amid incessant rain following Cyclone Ditwah is false.

# Old video of Hurricane Michael shared in false posts about cyclone hitting Bangladesh

* This article is more than five years old.
* Published on June 1, 2021 at 10:33
* 1 min read
* By [AFP Bangladesh](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-bangladesh)

A video has been viewed tens of thousands of times in multiple Facebook posts that claim it shows a cyclone hitting Bangladesh in May 2021. The claim is false: the clip shows a scene of Hurricane Michael battering the US coast in October 2018.

The [video](https://perma.cc/PE6G-YT7N) was shared here on May 24, 2021. It has been viewed more than 35,000 times.

The Facebook post’s Bengali-language caption translates to English as: ‘’Cyclone Yaas started its havoc. Severe storms began in different parts of Bangladesh, people are heading towards shelter.’’

Thousands of people were left homeless on May 27 after Cyclone Yaas hit Covid-ravaged India and neighbouring Bangladesh. AFP reported on the storm [here](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/latest-indian-cyclone-kills-five-051222532.html ).

The same video was also shared [here](https://perma.cc/488B-UMR5) and [here](https://perma.cc/5W3X-PHDP) alongside a similar claim.

The claim is false.

A reverse image search of keyframes extracted from the video clip found, combined with keyword searches, found this video [posted on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kU3Dc6T8Sug) on October 12, 2018.

It is credited to Live Storms Media, a US-based video licensing agency.

The caption reads: “Full video from the full wrath that hurricane Michael unleashed on Panama City Beach, Florida as homes get ripped to shreds and tossed into the air”.

Below is a screenshot comparison of the video in the misleading post (L) and the video on the Live Storms Media channel (R):

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/bangladesh/yaas_2_31may.jpg?itok=AuRAnAsm)

At the YouTube video’s 50-second mark, a sign for “Moby Dick’s” can be seen.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/bangladesh/yaas_3_31may.jpg?itok=CW-Rp2Fr)

This corresponds with this retail business of the same name in [Panama Beach](https://goo.gl/maps/9QTWeTANM9gLJh9D6).

The same video was published here in a CNN [report](https://edition.cnn.com/videos/weather/2018/10/10/hurricane-michael-panama-city-beach-roofs-ripped-off-orig.cnn/video/playlists/hurricane-michael/), credited to Live Storms Media. It was published on October 10, 2018, with the headline: “Michael tears off roofs in Panama City Beach”.

Hurricane Michael slammed into the Florida coast on October 10, 2018, AFP reported [here](https://news.yahoo.com/hurricane-michael-reaches-category-2-threatens-southern-us-131619947.html). It was the most powerful storm to hit the southern US state in more than a century.

**CLAIM**

As Cyclone Fani made landfall in Odisha in early hours of Friday, 3 May, many claims, photos and videos regarding the same also surfaced on social media.

As a result of the cyclone large areas in Puri and other places were submerged as heavy rains battered the entire coastal belt of the state.

A video along the claim “Cyclone Fani continues to strengthen as it tracks over the Bay of Bengal....” was circulated on social media platforms like Facebook and WhatsApp.

>
> Posted by [Abhijit Das Roy](https://www.facebook.com/abhijitdas.roy.31) on [Thursday, May 2, 2019](https://www.facebook.com/abhijitdas.roy.31/videos/613226145859527/)

> Cyclone Fani continues to strengthen as it tracks over the Bay of Bengal....
>
> Posted by [Bong Savage](https://www.facebook.com/TheBongSavage/) on [Thursday, May 2, 2019](https://www.facebook.com/TheBongSavage/videos/2313940705315693/)

The video shows a ship struggling in the sea with high waves during a storm. According to the claim, the ocean is Bay of Bengal and the high waves are caused due to Cyclone Fani.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**FACT**

The claim circulated is false and the video is not of a storm caused by Cyclone Fani.

On conducting a simple reverse image search, **The Quint** found a tweet by [*sever-weather.EU*](https://twitter.com/severeweatherEU/status/1101228686693543937) originally posted in March. The same video was posted in March on Facebook too.

> So, who would be able to stomach this? Ever been in such rough seas? Severe indeed! Video: The Sea Lad via Meteo Reporter Storm [pic.twitter.com/NplM6YB3s3](https://t.co/NplM6YB3s3)
>
> — severe-weather.EU (@severeweatherEU) [February 28, 2019](https://twitter.com/severeweatherEU/status/1101228686693543937?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> So, who would be able to stomach this? Ever been in such rough seas? Severe indeed! Video: The Sea Lad via Meteo Reporter Storm
>
> Posted by [Severe Weather Europe](https://www.facebook.com/severeweatherEU/) on [Thursday, February 28, 2019](https://www.facebook.com/severeweatherEU/videos/585057968635849/)

Further research took us to a YouTube video posted originally in the year 2016. The video might be even older than 2016.

Since the video dates before 3 May, the incident definitely did not occur after Cyclone Fani made landfall.

This claim was earlier debunked by AltNews.

# Old video from Saudi Arabia shared as Cyclone Tauktae’s devastation in Mumbai

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/399cb9e278d29dd4eb8ecba351839b095c6c8018bb34676193b64b2a8d8c69b3?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/archit-mehta/)

[Archit](https://www.altnews.in/author/archit-mehta/)

 ![Old video from Saudi Arabia shared as Cyclone Tauktae’s devastation in Mumbai](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/FI-1-2-1024x536.jpg) 

In the backdrop of India’s west coast region witnessing the devastation of Cyclone Tauktae, several social media users have posted a clip of concrete falling on parked cars during a storm and torrential outpour. It has been claimed this is a recent video from Mumbai’s [Trident Hotel](https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/Mumbai/entity/CgsI7_vn_qeGyfzjARAB?g2lb=2502548%2C2503781%2C2503850%2C4258168%2C4270442%2C4306835%2C4317915%2C4371335%2C4401769%2C4419364%2C4429192%2C4482438%2C4486153%2C4509341%2C4533882%2C4536454%2C4541148%2C4551240%2C4270859%2C4284970%2C4291517&hl=en-IN&gl=in&ssta=1&ap=aAE&&q=Mumbai%27s%20Trident%20Hotel&rp=EO_75_6nhsn84wEQmPa2wcP0u9Z0OAJAAEgCogETTXVtYmFpLCBNYWhhcmFzaHRyYcABA8gBAA&ictx=1&ved=0CAAQ5JsGahcKEwjos5zdk9PwAhUAAAAAHQAAAAAQAg&utm_campaign=sharing&utm_medium=link&utm_source=htls).

Twitter user @HasnaZaruriHai posted the viral video and wrote, “Trident hotel Nariman Point.”

> Trident hotel Nariman Point [pic.twitter.com/hiocEAvU7r](https://t.co/hiocEAvU7r)
>
> — HasnaZarooriHai (@HasnaZaruriHai) [May 17, 2021](https://twitter.com/HasnaZaruriHai/status/1394249271499649029?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The video has been shared by many [Twitter](https://twitter.com/search?q=Trident%20Hotel%2C%20Nariman%20point%20&src=typed_query&f=live) and [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/search/posts?q=Trident%20Hotel%2C%20Nariman%20point&%3D) users. The two posts below cumulatively drew 20,000 views. ([1](https://www.facebook.com/2339898239621646/posts/2974121576199306), [2](https://www.facebook.com/140535406758936/posts/938900233589112))

Alt News has received multiple verification requests for the video on our WhatsApp helpline (76000 11160) and our application. Download our mobile application to send such forwards for verification. ([Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.altnews&hl=en_IN&gl=US), [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/tt/app/alt-news/id1489307805?uo=2))

#### FACT-CHECK: OLD VIDEO FROM SAUDI ARABIA

Alt News analysed the viral video and noticed that the time stamp on the CCTV footage is from July 30, 2020.

A reverse-image search of the video’s keyframes threw up several Arabic posts. This led us to search for ‘car storm video’ in Arabic (فيديو سيارة العاصفة) on Google, restricting the results between July 2020 and August 2020. We were redirected to an August 1, 2020 report by [RT Arabic](https://arabic.rt.com/funny/1140167-%D8%B4%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%AF-%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%B8%D8%A9-%D8%B3%D9%82%D9%88%D8%B7-%D8%AC%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%88-%D9%86%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%A9-%D8%B1%D8%AC%D9%84-%D9%85%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%AA-%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%82/).

As per the article, the incident took place in Saudi Arabia’s Medina. The video shows a section of a house falling on cars due to a storm. The article carries a higher resolution version of the viral video uploaded by a YouTuber on July 31.

[embedyt] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kUKijp-uczM[/embedyt]

The video was also uploaded by [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.net/news/politics/2020/8/1/%D8%A7%D8%A7-79) on August 1, 2020.

A 2020 video from Medina that shows debris crushing parked cars was shared with the false claim that the incident took place in Mumbai’s Trident Hotel due to Cyclone Tauktae.

### *Related*

False

Claim:
> Video of cars being damaged by Tauktae cyclon at Trident Hotel, Mumbai

The content is factually incorrect or fabricated.

# Unrelated Video Falsely Shared as Footage of Cyclone Dana’s Impact in Odisha

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Oct 26, 2024

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/10/Rating-2024-10-26T145735.867.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## Claim

Video shows impact of Cyclone Dana in Odisha.

![Cyclone Dana ](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/10/d1.png)

Screengrab from X post by @CaptainGhazi

Such posts can be seen **[here](https://ghostarchive.org/archive/CUSKA)**, **[here](https://ghostarchive.org/archive/kjUWP)** and **[here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GJr_e_L3-ow)**.

**Also Read: [2021 Photo Of Oil Refinery Fire Falsely Linked To Israeli Attack On Iran](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/2021-photo-of-oil-refinery-fire-falsely-linked-to-israeli-attack-on-iran/)**

## Fact

A [**Google lens**](https://lens.google.com/search?ep=gsbubb&hl=en-IN&re=df&p=AbrfA8rJOJo7FWDtMmtlgu91x6JPmJWpnpslCUzK48wwS6llhJyNWnIQIdWPtH1rSanmj8Ap78E-IOfcM4bsvIS5GeXKkqQXNlj55XMWVuUhqy2l_BYET8MkmtMqOiDJPMVLn6zQZLlhhvhMOkjR7wC0nawlG0eMI8B_WyL3FIGCQle9maHXtJEujtpJ1PynQEQLf1h9DFmk2UCAVEMpSKYqKHqYHGWyadZjTDUmtbogMvAGqKYYuxYoZVrgnafQ_N8rKh21Ab2PxZV2Qn0wjlaa2myRb6uQeV-ZbpR1posw4E_f_L_xAJhjzxFA#) search on the keyframes of the viral clip led us to a YouTube video by **[@BOMBAYBEATSBITES](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=ObSniZmyxr8)**, dated **May 18, 2021**. It featured the same visuals of huge waves washing up on the shore as seen in the viral clip.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/10/d2-1024x693.png)

Screengrab from YouTube video by @BOMBAYBEATSBITES

The same video was also uploaded on YouTube channel **[@ryanbharathedits](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bSkLZSRyRu0)** on **May 15, 2021** to allegedly show Cyclone Tauktae’s effect in Kanyakumari.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/10/d3-1024x682.png)

Screengrab from YouTube video by @ryanbharathedits

A Facebook post by **[@assamHtok](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=312552367151921)**, dated May 15, 2021, featured the same footage that has been shared to show Cyclone Dana “unleashing fury in Odisha.”

Multiple such posts from 2021, such as **[this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=GD0DlWQ3Rrg)**, **[this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HE2lG4-N9rI)** and **[this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CZrCFsQXvA4)**, carried the same footage.

**Also Read: [Viral Posts Falsely Claim ‘Jai Shri Ram’ Chants During Disengagement At India-China Border](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/viral-posts-falsely-claim-jai-shri-ram-chants-during-disengagement-at-india-china-border/)**

We were not independently able to ascertain the exact location seen in the video. However, it dates back to at least May 2021, and does not show the impact of Cyclone Dana in Odisha.

## Result: False

**Sources**  
YouTube Video By **[@BOMBAYBEATSBITES](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=ObSniZmyxr8)**, DatedMay 18, 2021  
YouTube Video By **[@ryanbharathedits](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bSkLZSRyRu0)**, Dated May 15, 2021

# Fact-Check: CGI Video of Tornado Shared as Cyclone Biparjoy At Gujarat Coast

## The animated video was created using Adobe After Effects and Cinema 4D.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Aa

A video showing a tornado emerging from the dark, cloudy sky and forming over a sea surface is going viral on social media to claim that this shows [cyclone Biparjoy](https://www.thequint.com/climate-change/cyclone-biparjoy-people-evacuated-gujarat-landfall) hitting the [Gujarat's](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/tides-hitting-bridge-cyclone-biparjoy-guarat-fact-check) coast.

**About Cyclone [Biparjoy](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/biparjoy-the-changing-character-of-the-arabian-sea-and-its-impact-on-cyclones):** According to the Indian Coast Guard, the landfall is expected to take place between 18:00 to 20:00 hours with powerful winds, storm surges, and lashing rains over a stretch of the coast between Mandvi in [Gujarat](https://www.thequint.com/news/india/cyclone-biparjoy-changes-direction-expected-to-make-landfall-on-gujarat-coast) and [Karachi](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/egypt-sandstorm-video-shared-as-cyclone-biparjoy-gujarat-and-karachi-fact-check) in [Pakistan](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/pakistans-political-chasm-the-armys-staged-move-traps-imran-in-his-own-design).

***(Archives of similar claims can be found [here](https://perma.cc/95HH-SRJX)and [here](https://perma.cc/6UGZ-RVYU).)***

**Is the video real?:** No, this video shows the formation of tornado through Computer-generated imagery (CGI) animation.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out the original video?:** We divided the viral video into multiple keyframes and conducted a reverse image search on some of them on Google.

* On doing this, we came across the [same video](https://www.instagram.com/p/Byax3iGAR-f/) posted by '[orphicframer](https://www.instagram.com/orphicframer/)' on Instagram.
* This video was shared on 7 June 2019 and the caption mentioned hashtags about the video being made on CGI animation.
* The caption read, "#cgi #vfx #visualeffects #digitalart #photoshop".

* We also found the same user's YouTube channel which carried a [longer version](https://perma.cc/HP8J-V7VB) of the same video, and this was shared on 22 December 2018.
* The video's title read, "Tornado in Jersey, Channel Islands (CGI simulation)(TikTok).**"**

* In the description of this YouTube video, the user mentioned that this video was created using Adobe After Effects and Cinema 4D (with TurbulenceFD plugin).

**We also reached out to the creator:** The user running the channel 'orphicframer' confirmed to us that he added the tornado in the original video through CGI in 2018.

* He also stated that the video of the beach was recorded in the same year at Jersey, Channel Islands which is a group of British dependency islands in the English Channel.
* This channel has shared several similar videos of the simulation and can be seen [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TeJ2oCiiKgs) and [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-pnuZVp-HcY).

**Conclusion**: A video of a tornado created by CGI animation is going viral on social media as a real video showing cyclone biparjoy in Gujarat.

*(Note: The story has been updated to add a quote from the artist.)*

# Mumbai Rains: Old Video From Chennai Shared As Waterlogging At Mumbai Airport

Written By [Kushel Madhusoodan](/author/kushel/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Aug 20, 2025

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/08/Copy-of-One-Rating-Article-Thumbnails-Original-16.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## **Claim**

Viral video claiming to show severe waterlogging at Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport amid the intense downpour lashing the city.

The archived version of Republic Media Network’s X post, sharing the video as scenes from the Mumbai airport, can be seen [here](https://archive.is/NePKB).  [Heavy rain has battered](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/mumbai-rain-mayhem-imd-issues-red-alert-local-trains-cancelled-mumbai-university-exam-postponed-10-updates-101755652715204.html) the country’s financial capital for five consecutive days, paralysing life with flooding, suspended trains, flight diversions and evacuation drives in low-lying areas.

We also received the same video from multiple users on our Whatsapp tipline (+91-9999499044), requesting us to fact-check it.

## **Fact**

Newschecker noticed that several users pointed out in the replies to the viral posts that the 25-second video is old and not from Mumbai.

We then ran a reverse image search of keyframes, which led us to this [TimesNow post on X,](https://x.com/TimesNow/status/1731620662182302153) dated December 4, 2023, stating that it showed the flooded runway at Chennai airport following heavy rainfall across the city owing to Cyclone Michaung.

> [#CycloneMichaung](https://twitter.com/hashtag/CycloneMichaung?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw): Runway at Chennai airport flooded amid heavy rainfall across the city.[#ChennaiRains](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChennaiRains?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Chennai](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Chennai?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/6EyGfYt7CI](https://t.co/6EyGfYt7CI)
>
> — TIMES NOW (@TimesNow) [December 4, 2023](https://twitter.com/TimesNow/status/1731620662182302153?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Similar social media posts from December 4, 2023, sharing the video, can be seen [here](https://x.com/LimayeVaibhavi/status/1731570641357418708) and [here](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C0bZNi_vPqV/). According to the posts, several flights at Chennai airport [had been cancelled](https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-shuts-schools-offices-evacuates-thousands-cyclone-michaung-nears-2023-12-04/#:~:text=Chennai%20airport%20runway%20flooded%20as%20Cyclone%20Michaung%20nears%20India,-By%20Praveen%20Paramasivam&text=CHENNAI%2C%20Dec%204%20(Reuters),impact%20of%20a%20severe%20cyclone.) and some diverted owing to the heavy rain and winds [triggered by Cyclone Michaung.](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/cyclone-michaung-chennai-neighbouring-districts-pounded-by-heavy-rains/article67603744.ece)

Although there were several users pointing out that the viral video was even older, allegedly dating back to 2015, we could not yet independently ascertain the exact date. We can, however, confirm that it predates the ongoing extreme rainfall battering Mumbai.

On a close analysis of the video, Newschecker also spotted a yellow board on the flooded runway with black numbering. They are geographical location markers or checkpoint coordinate signs that display latitude and longitude [to verify the current location](https://aviation.stackexchange.com/questions/89813/why-are-lat-lon-coordinates-written-at-parking-bays-in-civil-airports) of the aircraft for navigation purposes.

We entered the latitude and longitude GPS coordinates, written in degrees, minutes, and seconds (DMS) — 12° 59 ‘5.9 ” N 80° 9’ 47.686” E — o[n Google Maps](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/18539?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop), which showed the location as [Chennai, Tamil Nadu](https://www.google.com/maps/place/12%C2%B059'05.9%22N+80%C2%B009'47.7%22E/@12.9849722,80.1606658,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m4!3m3!8m2!3d12.9849722!4d80.1632461?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDgxNy4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D). When we looked for directions to the point, [it showed the destination](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/Tambaram,+Chennai,+Tamil+Nadu/12.9849722,80.1632461/@12.9546355,80.0911948,13z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m8!4m7!1m5!1m1!1s0x3a525f14844aad0f:0xe16d3a66c4ce38d4!2m2!1d80.1000026!2d12.9249308!1m0?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDgxNy4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) as Meenambakkam, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, [which is where](https://www.latlong.net/place/meenambakkam-chennai-tamil-nadu-india-6185.html) the Chennai International Airport (MAA) is situated, further confirming that the viral video is not from Mumbai.

**Also Read**: [India Ditches US Dollar, Pushes BRICS Countries To Trade Only In Rupees? Here’s What We Learnt](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/india-ditches-us-dollar-pushes-brics-countries-to-trade-only-in-rupees-heres-what-we-learnt)

**Sources**  
[X post,](https://x.com/TimesNow/status/1731620662182302153) Times Now, December 4, 2023  
[Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/place/12%C2%B059'05.9%22N+80%C2%B009'47.7%22E/@12.9849722,80.1606658,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m4!3m3!8m2!3d12.9849722!4d80.1632461?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDgxNy4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)

# Fact-Check: Does This Video Show Impact of Cyclone Dana in Odisha? No!

## The video is from May 2021 and is unrelated to Cyclone Dana.

[Abhishek Anand](/author/1685310/abhishek-anand-7)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video of high waves hitting the shore where a house could be seen is going viral on the internet with users linking it to the recent Cyclone Dana that has impacted [Odisha](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/false-claim-about-anti-hindu-play-viral-fact-check) and [West Bengal](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/tmc-rally-west-bengal-muslim-hindu-song-old-video-martyrs-day-fact-check).

**What do viral posts say?:** Those sharing the clip have uploaded it with a caption saying, "Cyclone Dana unleashes its fury on Odisha's coastal regions, bringing: Turbulent waves, Heavy rainfall, Strong gusty winds.

***(You can view archives of similar posts [here](https://archive.is/UvZy7) and [here](https://archive.is/fFWRl).)***

**What is the truth?:** The video could be traced back to May 2021, which predates the recent damage caused in both states by Cyclone Dana.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**What led us to the truth?:** We performed a Google Lens search on the keyframes of the video and found the same visuals on a [Facebook handle](https://perma.cc/LM3S-UUS8) named 'Mo Odisha'.

* The video was posted on **25 May 2021** and its caption said, "Video from Chandipur Balasore. Stay home stay safe."

* We came across similar visuals shared on the official [YouTube channel](https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/TR79k9CyWhw) of *OTV,* which said that they were from Cyclone Yaas.
* It identified the location as 'Digha'. The video was published on 25 May 2021.

**Other sources:** An X user named 'Roxy Koll' had [shared](https://archive.is/gROvc) the same video on **14 May 2021** claiming it to be from Cyclone Tauktae and had identified the location as South Kerala.

> Strong winds from evolving Cyclone [#Tauktae](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Tauktae?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) bring in storm surges south of Kerala. As the Arabian Sea becomes fertile, cyclones, heavy rains, and a rising sea level overlap and create "compound events", resulting in prolonged floods along the coast of India.  
> Video: WeatherGroup [pic.twitter.com/kQgeOfnpV1](https://t.co/kQgeOfnpV1)
>
> — Roxy Koll  (@RockSea) [May 14, 2021](https://twitter.com/RockSea/status/1393201909054382081?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

**Conclusion:** While we could not independently verify the location of the video, it is evident that the clip is old and unrelated to Cyclone Dana.

# Old Video Goes Viral as Elephants Running to Safety Before Landslide Hit Wayanad

## This video predates the Wayanad landslides.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video showing a herd of [elephants](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/wild-life-protection-amendment-bill-trying-to-fix-india-environment-law) stepping out of a jungle is going viral to claim that this scene is from [Wayanad](https://www.thequint.com/news/wayanad-landslide-kerala-floods-amit-shah-pinarayi-vijayan-latest-news), Kerala and shows the animals "running to safety" before the landslides hit the area.

***(Archives of such posts can be found [here](https://perma.cc/VN5A-APB8) and [here](https://perma.cc/GLH9-AS85).)***

**What's the truth?:** This video dates back to at least January and is unrelated to the recent landslides.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out the truth?:** We performed a reverse image search on some of the keyframes of the video on Google and came across a [video](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C2AMQyYpf_f/?igsh=MW51Zjh2dno3Zmk2aQ%3D%3D) shared on Instagram.

This was shared on 12 January, which predates the landslides that happened on 30 July in Wayanad.

* We also noticed '@wayanadan' watermark on the video and taking a cue, we found the same video on this account on [Instagram](https://perma.cc/DE66-RLGV).
* This too, was shared on 12 January and the caption carried hashtags including 'Wayanad'.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C1_Xek4r6GD/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
>
> [A post shared by Wayanadan (444 K + Meta family¤ï¸) (@wayanadan)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C1_Xek4r6GD/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

* We also reached out to the user, who clarified that this video is from a village named Meppadi in Kerala and is unrelated to the Wayanad landslides, as it was recorded in January.
* The user also said that such instances are common and there wasn't anything unusual about elephants crossing the roads.

**Conclusion:** Although the context of the viral video in unclear, it is definitely unrelated to the recent Wayanad landslides.

# Viral Video Showing Dog Rescue In Landslides-Hit Wayanad Is Old & Unrelated

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Aug 2, 2024

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/Rating-2024-08-02T143240.407.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

**Claim**  
Dog and her puppies rescued in landslides-hit Wayanad.  
  
**Fact**  
Old video from Palakkad falsely linked to current situation in Wayanad.

Several social media users shared a one-minute-thirty-second-long-video of a dog and her puppies being rescued from under the mud, claiming it to be a recent incident from the landslides-hit Wayanad. Newschecker, however, found the footage to be old and unrelated to the current situation in the Kerala district.

The video is being widely shared on X and Facebook with users claiming it to be from Wayanad.

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t1-1.png)

Screengrab from X post by @/galexy\_007

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t2-1.png)

Screengrab from Facebook post by @vedahuja.vedahuja.9

 

Such posts can be seen **[here](https://archive.ph/k5cWF)**, **[here](https://archive.ph/tqu2d)**, **[here](https://ghostarchive.org/archive/duMiL)** and **[here](https://ghostarchive.org/archive/a8ZDN)**.

**Also Read: [Wayanad Landslides – Video Of DYFI Relief Efforts Falsely Shared As RSS Aid](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/wayanad-landslides-video-of-dyfi-relief-efforts-falsely-shared-as-rss-aid/)**

## Fact Check/Verification

A [**Google lens**](https://lens.google.com/search?ep=cntpubb&hl=en-US&re=df&s=4&p=AbrfA8qNh30K2eYCFwNKFM2Is_sgB9181InC0WDKHo8sLkdBXfvcd3aE5_DhJntHEnqvDf0dnYSmTgZKMwC7esi3v4Aqmhe_XWvbmCe6Rw1H8b9x9VcHi8d6-GNij8VuTu8lLwlx3FhPG9Q5mDzEBZ-IKyTsTp961PPpZ0NaerTBR5Ut6DecUP-h6t9IFMxFefs_EsKXWe4opda9x3CLJMh_GET0UjOGknJN2Uki2j90Jctyve6dCxNRFzGGvqaszaumvgnzqJiHSB0OsWU-YgC1dfF790L9Ue9kOegi#)search on the keyframes of the viral footage led us to a report by **[Manorama Online](https://www.manoramaonline.com/environment/wild-life/2021/10/14/mama-dog-and-her-puppies-trapped-under-mudslide-rescued.html)**, dated October 19, 2021. Carrying a screengrab from the same video, it stated that a mother dog and her puppies who were trapped under a mudslide in Palakkad were rescued by the locals.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t3.png)

Screengrab from Manorama Online

We then looked up keywords “Palakkad,” “Dog Rescued,” and “Landslide” on [**Google**](https://www.google.com/search?q=Palakkad+Dog+Rescued+Landslide&oq=Palakkad+Dog+Rescued+Landslide+&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUyBggAEEUYOTIJCAEQIRgKGKABMgkIAhAhGAoYoAEyCQgDECEYChigAdIBCjEzNDg1ajBqMTWoAgiwAgE&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8) which led us to a report by **[The News Minute](https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/dog-and-pups-rescued-3-days-after-being-buried-minor-landslide-kerala-156509)** from October, 2021. It featured an image similar to the visuals seen in the viral footage, and stated, “On October 10, Sabitha and Ashraf, a couple who run a shop in a village bordering Palakkad-Malappuram districts of Kerala, heard a dog wailing.”

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t4.png)

Screengrab from TNM website

“They searched but couldn’t find where the wails and whimperings came from. They heard the same cries of a dog for two more days until on October 12, the family decided to undertake a closer inspection. Finally, they found where the wailing came from — beneath a mound of mud. The dog and her two puppies were buried below the mud in a minor landslide in Palakkad district…”

**Also Read: [2001 Image of El Salvador Earthquake Viral As Wayanad Landslide](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/2001-image-of-el-salvador-earthquake-viral-as-wayanad-landslide/)**

The report further quoted Ashraf as saying, “We heard a wailing sound of a dog in this area for three days. There was a minor landslide due to the rains and they were trapped under the mud. We could hear only the muffled sounds. We dug out the mud a bit and saw the dog’s head. When we dug further, we saw six pups. However, only two of the pups survived. Now, the mother dog and her surviving babies have regained health and they are safe.”

It also featured a YouTube video by **[Manorama News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wbCXA6sWlVo&t=4s)** with snippets from the viral footage showing the rescue of the mother dog and her puppies.

![Video Not From Landslides-Hit Wayanad ](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t5-1024x679.png)

Screengrab from YouTube video by Manorama News

Another report on the incident by **[The New Indian Express](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2021/Oct/13/dog-and-two-pups-buried-in-kerala-landslide-rescued-after-three-day-ordeal-2371262.html)** also corroborated that dogs and two pups “survived a minor landslide after lying covered with mud behind a shop for three days” on the Palakkad–Malappuram border and were rescued by the locals.

**Also Read: [Old, Unrelated Images From Idukki Linked To Recent Landslides In Wayanad](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/old-unrelated-images-from-idukki-linked-to-recent-landslides-in-wayanad/)**

## Conclusion

Hence, an old video from Palakkad has been falsely shared to a dog and her puppies being rescued from landslides-hit Wayanad.

## Result: False

**Sources**  
Report By **[Manorama Online](https://www.manoramaonline.com/environment/wild-life/2021/10/14/mama-dog-and-her-puppies-trapped-under-mudslide-rescued.html)**, Dated October 19, 2021  
Report By **[The News Minute](https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/dog-and-pups-rescued-3-days-after-being-buried-minor-landslide-kerala-156509)**, Dated October 14, 2021  
YouTube Video By **[Manorama News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wbCXA6sWlVo&t=4s)**, Dated October 13, 2021

# Old Video of a House Drowning in China Falsely Linked to Wayanad Landslide

## This video predates the Wayanad landslide and is from Guangdong, China.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A timelapse video from a security footage showing a house fully drowning in the flood is going viral as a a video from destructive [landslides](https://www.thequint.com/climate-change/wayanad-landslides-kerala-experts-explain-rainfall-factor-plantations-climate) that happened in [Wayanad](https://www.thequint.com/news/india/kerala-wayanad-landslides-deaths-rescue-operations-climate-disaster-ground-report), Kerala.

***(Archives of similar claims can be seen [here](https://perma.cc/ZW9Q-3YM3) and [here](https://perma.cc/6CF7-4MCX).)***

**Where is the video from?:** This video predates the Wayanad landslide that happened on 30 July 2024.

* This video was recorded on 16 June 2024 and is from Guangdong, China.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out the truth?:** We performed a reverse image search on Google using some of the keyframes from the viral video.

* This led us to several YouTube videos from 26 June 2024 which predates the Wayanad landslide. These can be seen [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-UBuGHH_pIo), [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qO8SM9AXcNc) and [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yc2Qdesy7Y4).
* The title of these videos stated that this video dates back to 16 June 2024 and is from Meizhou, Guangdong, China.
* Moreover, we also noticed the date as 16 June 2024 on the left top corner of all these videos including the viral clip.

* Taking a cue, we performed a reverse image search on Google along with some relevant keywords this time and this led us to reports from Chinese websites.
* These reports shared by *[Jinrizhiyi](http://jinrizhiyi.vip/index.php/product/4925)* and *[Sohcradio](https://sohcradio.com/175852.html)*which carried screenshots from the viral video and stated that floods hit the city of Meizhou in China on 16 June 2024.
* It also stated that this flood led to 38 deaths.

**Conclusion:** An old video of a flooded area in China is going viral as a visuals from Wayanad landslide.

# Indian landslide clip misrepresented as Nepal-Tibet flood

* Published on August 29, 2026 at 13:29
* Updated on August 29, 2026 at 13:36
* 2 min read
* By [Chelsea CHAN](https://factcheck.afp.com/chelsea-chan),  [AFP Hong Kong](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-hong-kong)

A deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Nepal-Tibet border region in August 2026, but footage online of muddy floodwater barrelling through a road is actually from India. The clip previously circulated in July 2026, when a landslide destroyed a construction site in India's southern Kerala state. AFP confirmed that the footage was recorded at a restaurant near the site.

"A moment of life and death in Nepal," reads part of the Chinese-language caption of an [X post](https://perma.cc/PG7R-AE4M) shared on August 27.

```
Warning: Distressing visuals
```

The video -- which racked up over three million views -- shows what appears to be CCTV footage of a heavy mudslide eroding a highway before slamming into a truck and sweeping away several people.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/1d52575640ba48cd01c3aca62c4a03e8-en.jpeg?itok=frGnb4XD)

Screenshot of false X post taken on August 28, 2026, with red cross added by AFP

The [clip](https://perma.cc/Y8YN-ANX5) surfaced in similar English language [posts](https://perma.cc/LH33-JTRR) after [devastating floods](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260828-fresh-flood-warnings-for-disaster-hit-nepal-and-tibet-1-400-still-missing) in the Nepal-Tibet border region [killed](https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/news/number-of-missing-in-nepal-china-floods-soars-past-2-400/ar-AA2b9lu5?ocid=BingNewsSerp) at least 586 people, with the number of missing soaring past 2,400 on August 28 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/RX2P-7VZ2)).

The trauma of the catastrophe has been "enormous", and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.

The [US Geological Survey](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/landslide-hazards/science/2026-nepal-debris-avalanche-and-flash-flood) said the disaster was likely caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris downstream ([archived link](https://perma.cc/5DNF-35JV)). The surge of water hit villages and towns on path of rivers Bhote Koshi and Trishuli in Nepal.

But the video shows a massive landslide that hit southern India in July 2026, not Nepal.

A [reverse image search](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.36RH9NT) on Google using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) found the same footage [shared](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DafoQ6vAJCR/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsi=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ==) on Instagram on July 7, 2026 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7UFU-3EZW)).

The post's Marathi-language caption reads in part, "Massive landslide near tunnel construction site in Wayanad, Kerala."

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/35a7c30e247739105df62773d36809a9-en.jpeg?itok=KSUv-1oi)

Screenshot comparison of the false post (L) and the Instagram post

Media organisations [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/7/7/deadly-landslide-buries-tunnel-construction-site-in-india) and [The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/seconds-before-disaster-cctv-shows-wayanad-landslide-sweeping-away-fuel-tanker-2-dead-7-missing/articleshow/132236627.cms) also published the footage and reported that the landslide was triggered by continuous monsoon rain, killing at least [eight](https://english.deshabhimani.com/deshabhimani-english-/kerala-news/kalladi-landslide-last-missing-body-recovered-wayanad-47326#google_vignette) people (archived [here,](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/7/7/deadly-landslide-buries-tunnel-construction-site-in-india) [here](https://perma.cc/GKD3-8MRX) and [here](https://web.archive.org/web/20260829110527/https://english.deshabhimani.com/deshabhimani-english-/kerala-news/kalladi-landslide-last-missing-body-recovered-wayanad-47326)).

Timestamp in the top-left corner of the CCTV footage shared in false post shows the video was filmed on July 7, 2026.

Screenshot of the false post taken on August 28, 2026, with the timestamp highlighted by AFP

---

Visual details in the footage correspond to images of a [restaurant](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Grilax+Restaurant/@11.5229485,76.1339068,3a,75y,90t/data=!3m7!1e2!3m5!1sCIABIhADycKzdCflJGfgc5MADhc4!2e10!3e12!7i4032!8i2268!4m7!3m6!1s0x3ba61393a492b717:0xd4acfb4f0bda0c9b!8m2!3d11.5229485!4d76.1339068!10e5!16s%2Fg%2F11rrsb07yy!5m1!1e4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDgyNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) near the site of the landslide in Wayanad, which were uploaded to Google Maps ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7ZVA-MW86)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/687472a0f0f26e846923115bd3650f3a-en.jpeg?itok=1fV05QWl)

Screenshot of the false post (L) and the photo uploaded on Google Maps

AFP contacted the restaurant, whose owner confirmed the video was recorded in their CCTV camera on July 7.

"This is our restaurant in the background, from where the video is recorded," the restaurant owner told AFP via a phone call on August 28.

AFP has [previously debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6M39WH) false claims swirling around the Nepal-Tibet floods.

# Elephants Running To Safety Before Landslides Hit Wayanad? No, Viral Video Is Old

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Chayan Kundu

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Aug 5, 2024

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/Rating-2024-08-05T140924.292.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

**Claim**  
Herd of elephants seen running to safety an hour before landslides hit Wayanad.  
  
**Fact**  
Video dates back to at least January 2024, not linked to recent landslides.

Over 370 people were dead and several others injured after landslides hit multiple areas of **[Wayanad](https://www.ndtv.com/video/wayanad-landslides-death-count-rises-to-373-search-underway-for-those-missing-822085)** district during the early hours on July 30. The rescue operations, and the search for the missing are currently underway.  In this backdrop, several social media users, including verified handles, shared a video claiming to show a herd of elephants “running to safety” an hour before the landslides hit Wayanad district last week. Newschecker, however, found the video to be old, and unrelated to the recent disaster in Kerala.

The 27-second-long-video is being circulated on Facebook and X with users claiming, “Elephants running to safety 1 hour before the landslide in Wayanad, Kerala. Animals have subtle vision.”

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t1-2.png)

Screengrab from X post by @unenews9

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t2-3.png)

Screengrab from Facebook post by @vipinsham

 

Such posts can be seen **[here](https://archive.ph/KVO1Q)**, **[here](https://archive.ph/O6s4C)**, **[here](https://www.facebook.com/amitabh.chaudhary/videos/7959494194171331)** and **[here](https://www.facebook.com/reel/342380208944316)**.

**Also Read: [Old, Unrelated Images From Idukki Linked To Recent Landslides In Wayanad](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/old-unrelated-images-from-idukki-linked-to-recent-landslides-in-wayanad/)**

## Fact Check/Verification

A [**Google lens**](https://lens.google.com/search?ep=subb&hl=en-IN&re=df&p=AbrfA8o_lFT3MWgrEDHnz9PARZ_0PN_3ChUhmMvgshnciifhfQrjpZud1DO-hlNmKb4c35P78YVBHZi0FP_IL-hCBf2-_m2eILmEz07JAMXj87Itw4gfyPZxa0yhBFftB_1x4xrd8ipl-extqANE_t7g6LHNuQLj30qFchA833pfnQzxqV2HUgXieNNy9IEbnvoptZlZvKN5zytYJ3skF6GxnVdn-TEJGKqO7TOcWp1A0zfbUJ-t1OEKJDN9ctIOwVTRzD5yIWiaalfVeCK-b6a4L3kPWEVOTxDlsAa9XZKTO9j-muJR2g%3D%3D#) search on the keyframes of the viral footage led us to a YouTube video by **[@TravelwithAJ96](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f7vkQkkrBvY)**, dated April 3, 2024. It featured the same visuals of a herd of elephants crossing the road.

![Elephants Running To Safety Before Landslides Hit Wayanad? No, Viral Video Is Old](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t3-1-1024x753.png)

Screengrab from YouTube video by @TravelwithAJ96

We also found a slightly different version of the viral footage shared on Instagram by **[@yathrakarude\_sradhakku](https://www.instagram.com/p/C2AMQyYpf_f/)** on January 12, 2024. “Just 900 Kandi things…,” the post stated.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t4-1.png)

Screengrab from Instagram post by @yathrakarude\_sradhakku

A comparison between the keyframes of the viral footage and the Instagram video can be seen below.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/a2.png)

(L-R) Screengrabs from viral video and screengrabs from Instagram video

Furthermore, we noticed a watermark of “@wayanadan” on the Instagram video. Taking a clue, we skimmed through the Instagram account of **[@wayanadan](https://instagram.com/p/C1_Xek4r6GD/)**, and found a post from January carrying the same video.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/t6.png)

Screengrab from Instagram post by @wayanadan

We were independently not able to ascertain the exact location of the video. However, it dates back to at least January 2024 and does not show elephants running to safety 1 hour before the Wayanad landslides.

**Also Read: [2001 Image of El Salvador Earthquake Viral As Wayanad Landslide](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/2001-image-of-el-salvador-earthquake-viral-as-wayanad-landslide/)**

## Conclusion

Hence, an old video has been falsely shared to show a herd of elephants running to safety an hour before the landslide hit Wayanad.

## Result: False

# 2001 Image of El Salvador Earthquake Viral As Wayanad Landslide

Written By [Kushel Madhusoodan](/author/kushel/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Aug 1, 2024

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/08/Kushel-One-Rating-Article-Thumbnails-New-Brand.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## **Claim**

Photo of Mundakkai village after over 200 people died in massive landslides that struck the hilly areas near Meppadi in Wayanad, Kerala, on Tuesday (July 30).

The archived version of the tweet can be seen [here.](https://archive.is/qNXz0)

## **Fact**

Newschecker ran a reverse image search, which led us to this [Wikimedia Commons picture](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ElSalvadorslide.jpg), stating that it shows the landslide that happened during the 2001 El Salvador earthquake.

A further search led us to the same photo featured in a [NASA write-up](https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/learn/sensing-our-planet/gridding-the-risks-of-natural-disasters) on the world’s natural disaster hotspots, dated February 2006. “The 2001 El Salvador earthquake-induced landslide, located in a neighbourhood near Santa Tecla, El Salvador, buried numerous homes under tons of earth. The Hotspots report identified El Salvador as being at high risk for landslides, earthquakes, floods, and cyclones,” read the caption of the photo. Similar articles can be seen [here](https://www.rockngem.com/rockin-rewind-wednesday-earthquake-in-el-salvador/) and [here](https://www.encyclopedie-environnement.org/en/soil/why-earthquakes-trigger-catastrophic-landslides/), confirming the viral image is not related to the July 2024 landslides in Wayanad, Kerala.

 

“During the earthquake of 13 January 2001 in El Salvador, for example, the Las Colinas landslide claimed the lives of more than 500 people, nearly two thirds of the victims associated with the earthquake,” read an entry in the Encyclopaedia of the Environment, dated January 15, 2021, pointing to the same photo.

**Also Read**: [Muttiah Muralitharan Grooving To ‘Tauba Tauba’? No, Video Viral With False Claim](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/muttiah-muralitharan-grooving-to-tauba-tauba-no-video-viral-with-false-claim/)

## **Result: False**

**Sources**  
[Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ElSalvadorslide.jpg)  
[NASA write-up](https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/learn/sensing-our-planet/gridding-the-risks-of-natural-disasters), February 13, 2006

# Old & Unrelated Video Shared as Dog Rescued from Landslides in Wayanad

## BOOM found that the viral video is not recent but actually dates back to a landslide that occurred in Palakkad, Kerala, in 2021

By - [Nidhi Jacob |](/author/nidhi-jacob) 

Published -

[![Boomlive](https://www.boomlive.in/h-upload/2026/10/08/1058459-google.webp)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=boomlive.in)

Listen to this Article

![](/theme_phoenix/images/claim-icon.png) CLAIMA dog and her puppied are rescued by the NDRF following the massive landslides in Wayanad. The claim states "Big salute to the NDRF team. A dog and her two puppies rescued from Landslide in Wayanad."

![](/theme_phoenix/images/factcheck-icon.png) FACT CHECKBOOM found that the viral video is not recent but actually dates back to a landslide that occurred in Palakkad, Kerala, in 2021.

Numerous social media users have falsely claimed that a video showing the rescue of a dog and her two puppies by the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is related to the massive landslide that struck Wayanad, Kerala, on July 30.

The claim states "Big salute to the NDRF team. A dog and her two puppies rescued from Landslide in Wayanad."

> Big salute to the NDRF team  
>   
> A dog and her two puppies rescued from Landslide in Wayanad [#WayanadDisaster](https://twitter.com/hashtag/WayanadDisaster?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc^tfw) [#WaynadLandslide](https://twitter.com/hashtag/WaynadLandslide?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc^tfw) [#DisasterRelief](https://twitter.com/hashtag/DisasterRelief?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc^tfw)[#WayanadDisaster](https://twitter.com/hashtag/WayanadDisaster?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc^tfw) [pic.twitter.com/eshPIaXSkU](https://t.co/eshPIaXSkU)
>
> — Praveen Singh (@galexy\_007) [August 2, 2024](https://twitter.com/galexy_007/status/1819238153699426546?ref_src=twsrc^tfw)

BOOM found that the viral video is not recent but actually dates back to a landslide that occurred in Palakkad, Kerala, in 2021.

Search operations are currently underway across six zones in the landslide-affected areas to locate missing persons. According to news [reports](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/wayanad-landslide-live-updates-9492176/), over 300 people have died, and approximately 218 are suspected to be missing.

Fact-check

BOOM conducted a reverse image search on Google which led us to news reports regarding the rescue of the dog and her puppies by the [Manorama Online](https://www.manoramaonline.com/environment/wild-life/2021/10/14/mama-dog-and-her-puppies-trapped-under-mudslide-rescued.html) on October 13, 2021, [The News Minute](https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/dog-and-pups-rescued-3-days-after-being-buried-minor-landslide-kerala-156509) and the [New Indian Express](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2021/Oct/13/dog-and-two-pups-buried-in-kerala-landslide-rescued-after-three-day-ordeal-2371262.html) on October 14, 2021.

Further, the same video was also uploaded on [Newsflare](https://www.newsflare.com/video/459359/dog-and-her-two-pups-were-rescued-after-48-hours-as-they-were-struck-in-a-landslide-south-india), a news video uploading platform on October 15, 2021.

The incident took place in a border village of Palakkad-Malappuram districts near Kanjirathani of Kumaranelloor, per news reports.

According to a couple's account reported by the media, the dog and her two puppies were buried under the mud in a minor landslide in Palakkad district. They were rescued three days later with the help of an animal rescuer who assisted in freeing them from the mud.

In the video shared by local residents, the mother dog is seen poking her head out as soon as a small portion of the mud was cleared. She then started wailing desperately. Her puppies were lying close to her. The residents pulled them out, cleaned them, and provided food and water.

"We heard a wailing sound of a dog in this area for three days. There was a minor landslide due to the rains and they were trapped under the mud. We could hear only the muffled sounds. We dug out the mud a bit and saw the dog's head. When we dug further, we saw six pups. However, only two of the pups survived. Now, the mother dog and her surviving babies have regained health and they are safe," Ashraf, who runs a shop in a village bordering the Palakkad-Malappuram districts of Kerala told the media.
