# Old, Unrelated Images From Idukki Linked To Recent Landslides In Wayanad

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[News](/fact-check/news/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Jul 30, 2024

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/Rating-2024-07-30T152658.437.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

**Claim**  
Images linked to the recent landslides in Wayanad.  
  
**Fact**  
Old images showing rescue operations in Idukki

At least 84 people were killed and several others injured after **[landslides](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/wayanad-landslides-live-updates-chooralmala-rescue-operation-death-count-kerala-rain-latest-news-today-101722315714355.html)** hit multiple areas of [**Wayanad**](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/massive-landslides-hit-keralas-wayanad/article68462894.ece) district, including Meppadi, Mundakkal and Chooralmala towns, during the early hours of Tuesday. While rescue operations are underway, social media platforms continue to flood with unverified visuals claiming to show the recent tragedy in Kerala. Newschecker investigated two such images, and found them to be unrelated to the landslides in Wayanad.

Several social media users, including verified handles, shared an image *(hereafter referred as image 1)* of a rescue operation linking it to the landslides in Wayanad.

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/t1-16.png)

Screengrab from X post by @manwith\_noidea

 ![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/t2-15.png)

Screengrab from X post by @iam\_pky/

 

Such posts can be seen [**here**](https://archive.ph/d1zrm), [**here**](https://archive.ph/0Ubak) and [**here**](https://archive.ph/ZRv9D).

Tamil Nadu unit of the Congress also shared an image *(hereafter referred as image 2)* on X in a [**post**](https://archive.ph/pFnTV) on Wayanad*,* stating*, “*Deeply distressed by the devastating landslides near Meppadi in Wayanad. Our heartfelt condolences to the families who have lost loved ones. Praying for the safe rescue of those still trapped*.”*

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/Tamil-Nadu-Cong.png)

Screengrab from X post by @INCTamilNadu

**Also Read: [Old, Unrelated Videos Shared As Protests In Paris Over ‘Satanic’ Olympics Opening Ceremony](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/old-unrelated-videos-shared-as-protests-in-paris-over-satanic-olympics-opening-ceremony/)**

## Fact Check/Verification

A [**Google lens**](https://lens.google.com/search?p=AbrfA8rkRlHAmNqdXlJFK90MPgZxP2DG8eQ-TGnCSNL5tSOJ9B7CnpqE6h4cXri9tsnIZ7z3y1ERQTx283YCntzrLHQlXqhI6TY3a484We1msTsc6EgCAehS3cOd2CR7-7LvLv92x2Cg2TuJdIqPn13hEoMIcpIhKjBDd8lLIr9nDmj-FAlfXHU29_lq2fqrZt0Z5HU1nBvswBVjpYmopQGbcaUmuB3aVGUnVwUb-LkTP9s5valhJVG1vU9ODHBIIaH3-y4TOsUyycm3ZHI7bi7W2Vingy0R60XAmmQF60BVIPg%3D#) search on image 1 led us to a **[PTI](https://theprint.in/india/20-bodies-recovered-from-idukki-landslide-debris-in-kerala/477668/)** report, dated August 8, 2020, on a landslide in Kerala’s Idukki. Carrying the same image, it stated, “At least 20 bodies have been recovered so far from the debris of the landslides that flattened a row of 20 houses of tea estate workers in the high range Idukki district in Kerala, as efforts were underway amid continuing rains to locate those missing.”

Notably, the viral image 1 was captioned “Landslide in Idukki district of Kerala,” and was credited to news agency PTI itself.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/e1-11-1024x615.png)

Screengrab from The Print website

We also found a report by **[The News Minute](https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/kerala-landslide-pinarayi-govt-declares-rs-5-lakh-each-kin-deceased-130300)** from August 2020 featuring the same photo, captioned “Pettimudi, Rajamala, Idukki.” “The Kerala government has declared Rs 5 lakh each as ex-gratia to the families of those who lost their lives in a huge landslide in Rajamalai in the state’s Idukki district…,” it stated.

![Landslides In Wayanad ?](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/e2-11.png)

Screengrab from TNM website

It further quoted CM Pinarayi as saying, ““It’s understood that the landslide in Rajamala had occurred early in the morning. Electricity and communication facilities were cut off due to heavy rains. Hence, the outside world came to know about the tragedy late…”

A photo feature by **[Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/photos/india-news/photos-landslide-in-idukki-kills-15-people-ndrf-to-the-rescue/photo-gwLBkyB5B1qG65kASmhiyK-5.html)** on the August 2020 landslide in Idukki district also carried the same image. “Debris lies on the ground after a landslide in Idukki on August 7. Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had sounded a red alert for Idukki on August 7, indicating extremely heavy rains of over 20 centimetres in the coming days, PTI reported. (PTI),” its caption stated.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/e3-15.png)

Screengrab from HT website

Furthermore, we [**found**](https://lens.google.com/search?p=AbrfA8otWOQZ2l-DNEX-f_33jTkco0XGvwJA0pEqxplAB-eV1W7KmP-ImE3FqtU5iQCt5A1AV6i2HC7D1Ho7Kk1-SOs18UTJuR8UhUTqbSlIxzeXo54ese_zcZoiF5mFqQolXy_xKkhkILgeSYv9tmmqwjUM_oxtELMaJqU1E-kr3uNM1LT0Uga0CE8aD29BCqm_ckwVSB6YIXGq2NjeflDRdlgy7kbSqraE8BYu_VkcGLOw3CqfwfaR6yvMFEBGoFk_m-u3cB_udIE8hrO1u_hTndedP6-cqJsj8tk7ji9R0C8%3D#) the image 2 to be from the 2020 Idukki landslide as well.

**Also Read: [Video Of Indian Men’s Relay Team Qualifying For 2023 World Athletics Finals Falsely Linked To Paris Olympics](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/video-of-indian-mens-relay-team-qualifying-for-2023-world-athletics-finals-falsely-linked-to-paris-olympics/)**

Displaying the viral image 2, a **[PTI](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/death-toll-in-landslide-in-idukki-district-rises-to-28-11596962841684.html)** report on the landslide stated, “Incessant rains induced landslides in Kerala’s Idukki seems to be claiming more lives as death toll nears 30 mark while the authorities say that 78 people were residing at the spot of landslide Now NDRF is carrying out the rescue work with sniffer dogs to bring more missing people out from the debris”

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/e4-8.png)

Screengrab from Live Mint website

A video report by **[The Tribune](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h6qE34SySyw)** on the landslide in Idukki district, dated August 9, 2020, also carried both the images.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2024/07/e5-5.png)

Screengrabs from YouTube video by The Tribune

**Also Read:** [**AI-Generated Image Of Kamala Harris With Jeffrey Epstein Goes Viral**](https://newschecker.in/ai-deepfake/ai-generated-image-of-kamala-harris-with-jeffrey-epstein-goes-viral/)

## Conclusion

Hence, old images from Idukki have been falsely shared to show rescue work after the recent landslides in Wayanad.

## Result: False

**Sources**  
Report By **[PTI](https://theprint.in/india/20-bodies-recovered-from-idukki-landslide-debris-in-kerala/477668/)**, Dated August 8, 2020

# Old & Unrelated Visuals Falsely Linked to Rescue Work in Wayanad by RSS

## These images are not from the recent Wayanad tragedy while the video is recent but is unrelated to RSS.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A collage of four images and are video showing people rescuing others stuck in flood are going viral online to claim that it shows members of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ([RSS](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/2024-elections-mohan-bhagwat-speech-confirms-that-rss-open-license-to-bjp-modi-under-review)) helping people in Wayanad, Kerala after the area was hit by landslides.

***(Archives of similar claims can be seen [here](https://perma.cc/5KH4-WR65) , [here](https://perma.cc/T52Y-R6TC) and [here](https://perma.cc/KEY3-SUWX).)***

**What's the truth?:**Although the collage containing four images actually shows the RSS team conducting rescue work, they are all old images.

* The video showing people collecting important items at relief camps and cooking food is unrelated to RSS. It shows members of NGO, Deseeya Seva Bharati Kerala, working to help people stuck in Wayanad landslide.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out the truth?:** We performed a reverse image search on each of the image on Google and this led us to old reports and posts. Let's take a look.

**IMAGE 1 & 2**

* These two images showing men in khaki short walking in water-filled roads is actually from 2018 and shows RSS members carrying relief activities after devastating floods hit Kerala.
* We came across Facebook [post](https://perma.cc/93QV-DVPL) shared by RSS Rengali, Sambalpur on 18 August 2018 and along with other images, it included the viral images too.

* According to the [reports](https://www.undp.org/publications/post-disaster-needs-assessment-kerala), Kerala witnessed heavy flooding from 1 June to 18 August 2018 with incessant rains triggering several landslides and forced the release of excess water from 37 dams.
* This had displaced 1.4 million people and took 433 lives.

**IMAGE 3**

On performing a reverse image search, we came across a website called *[VSK Tamil Nadu](https://vsktamilnadu.org/rss/keralafloods-2018-relief-activities/)* which had posted several images of relief activities in Kerala after the 2018 floods.

This was shared in August 2018.

**IMAGE 4**

* A reverse image search on Google led us to a Facebook post from 21 August 2019.
* The viral image can be spotted at 0:13 timestamp of the video.

RSS [website](https://www.rss.org/Many%20More.html) also carries this image as RSS workers carrying relief work but does not specify the date or location.

**VIRAL VIDEO**

* We noticed 'Vallatholinte Kavipada' watermark on the video and looked at their Facebook [page](https://www.facebook.com/vkkeralam/videos/788443379844707) where this video was shared on 30 July.
* We also performed reverse image search on Google on some of the keyframes of the video but it did not return any old results.
* The results also included the video shared by Vallatholinte Kavipada's page and some on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C-DfVY9MOQz/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==).
* All the captions of these posts mentioned that the video shows Sevabharathi activists helping with food from Pazhassi Balamandir, an orphanage, to the disaster ground in Wayanad.

* Taking a cue, we then checked Deseeya Seva Bharati Kerala's social media platforms, where they had shared this video on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/sevakeralam/) story.
* We also figured out through the NGO's [website](https://www.sevabharathikeralam.in/about) that this organisation is not linked to RSS at all.

Team WebQoof reached out to Seva Bharati Kerala who clarified to us that the video only shows volunteers in Wayanad who are linked with their NGO.

**Conclusion:** Clearly, old and unrelated visuals are being linked to RSS workers helping out people in Wayanad, Kerala.

# Video shows cloudburst over Austrian lake, not rainfall before flood in India's Sikkim state

* This article is more than three years old.
* Published on October 17, 2023 at 10:22
* 2 min read
* By [Devesh MISHRA](https://factcheck.afp.com/devesh-mishra),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

A video of a cloudburst has been viewed thousands of times in social media posts falsely claiming it shows the cause of a deadly flash flood in northeast India in early October 2023. But the video in fact shows time-lapse footage taken near Austria's Lake Millstatt in June 2018.

"A sudden cloudburst in Sikkim led to the downpour of 15 feet of water. Around 24 deaths reported so far," reads the Hindi-language caption of a Facebook post shared [here](https://perma.cc/ASD8-UMGT) on October 6, 2023.

The 15-second video, viewed more than 970,000 times, shows a cloudburst over a body of water nestled in the mountains.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2023-10/0db917a40617bba3b205af5d4b735e8c.jpeg?itok=qfgUJYrM)

Screenshot of the false Facebook post, taken on October 10, 2023

The video was shared as Sikkim, a hilly state in northeast India, was hit by a torrential [flash flood](https://perma.cc/7UKK-NZLY).

AFP reported on October 8 that the water surge came after intense rainfall burst the high-altitude Lhonak Lake, which sits at the base of a glacier in peaks surrounding the world's third-highest mountain, Kangchenjunga.

Water powered downstream, adding to a river already swollen by monsoon rains, damaging a dam and sweeping away houses. At least 77 people have been confirmed dead.

The video was also shared with similar claims elsewhere on Facebook [here](https://perma.cc/MSZ6-K3FE) and [here](https://perma.cc/ABG9-G6AX).

While heavy rain contributed to the sudden lake burst that flooded Sikkim, the video was in fact filmed more than five years earlier in Austria.

### Rainfall in Austria

A combination of reverse image searches and keyword searches on Google found longer versions of the video uploaded on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ObYRYF3d38Y) on June 12, 2018 and on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/pietflossee/videos/183284345664805) on June 13, 2018 by Peter Maier (archived links [here](https://perma.cc/6R3T-FPMT) and [here](https://perma.cc/T7WJ-WAF6)).

The YouTube video is titled, "Tsunami from Heaven / Amazing Rainstorm Timelapse / Downburst / Microburst".

According to the US National Weather Service, a [microburst](https://www.weather.gov/bmx/outreach_microbursts) is a localised downdraft within a thunderstorm ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7M9G-3CJX)). Wet microbursts are accompanied by a significant amount of rain or snow.

The Facebook post's German-language caption reads: "Here is some original footage with original sound, for all who still think that it was a fake." The post also links to the YouTube time-lapse video.

Below is a screenshot comparison of the video used in the false posts (left) and the video uploaded to Maier's YouTube channel (right). The false posts appear to have changed the original video's aspect ratio, but AFP has highlighted matching features in the landscape.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2023-10/0116f75b55746a1e1c8a02b11b70f8a5.jpeg?itok=bxWYAfz3)

Screenshot comparison of the video used in the false posts (left) and the video uploaded to Maier's YouTube channel (right)

The footage corresponds to Google Street View imagery of Lake Millstatt [here](https://maps.app.goo.gl/DHdP3RZY5p1gZfn27).

Further keyword searches found the video was used in a Washington Post [article](https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/capital-weather-gang/wp/2018/06/19/watch-this-incredible-rain-storm-explode-over-a-lake-in-austria/) on June 19, 2018 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/RU89-W5KL)).

The headline of the article reads, "Watch this incredible rainstorm explode over a lake in Austria". It also attributes the footage to Maier.

The same video was shared in other news articles from 2018 [here](https://www.europapress.es/desconecta/curiosity/noticia-espectacular-video-timelapse-muestra-tsunami-cielo-descargo-tormenta-lago-20180618132508.html) and [here](https://www.insider.com/mountaineer-captures-stunning-timelapse-of-tsunami-from-heaven-2018-6) (archived links [here](https://perma.cc/N5C8-PUTM) and [here](https://perma.cc/8VGJ-CVZC)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2023-10/5d62fc25cc06b9c731c693da43ea5b78.jpeg?itok=V5dZXnbz)

# Sikkim Floods: 'Saw My Pregnant Wife and Baby Being Washed Away, Was Helpless'

## At least 14 people lost their lives and 102 others, including 22 army personnel, are missing due to the disaster.

[Madhusree Goswami](/author/1685998/madhusree-goswami)

Published:

[India](https://www.thequint.com/news/india)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

***Do your bit to support our journalism. [Become a member](https://www.thequint.com/plan-selection?utm_source=article&utm_medium=hyperlink) – and help us stay on top of the most important stories.***

"*Hamile Teesta nadi ko esto nisthur rup kaile dekheko thiyena* (We had never seen Teesta river's angry form up until now)," Meena Tamang, a resident of Singtam in [Sikkim](https://www.thequint.com/topic/sikkim), told **The Quint** in Nepali. Her voice was trembling as she spoke over phone on Thursday, 5 October.

Meena had to flee her home with just her clothes on her back on 4 October, at midnight, when floodwaters started gushing into her two-storey house, situated on the banks of Teesta in Singtam.

"The police began alerting citizens by blowing whistles at around 1 am. We initially did not pay much heed to it, as we thought it was a routine affair. But half hour later, the cops were at our doorstep, frantically pleading with us to evacuate since the water level of the Teesta river was rising," she said.

> "Just then, we heard an ominous sound and saw a bridge being washed away and the water rapidly advancing towards our house. We didn't have time to collect any of our belongings, so we fled. I put my life's entire savings into building the house brick by brick, and now the river has engulfed my home."

Meena Tamang

Meena fled along with her son, daughter-in-law, and two toddler grandchildren.

> Her story is the story of many other families in Sikkim that witnessed a flash flood in the Teesta basin after a cloudburst over Lhonak Lake in north Sikkim, according to officials.

Up until 12 pm on 5 October, at least 14 people lost their lives, and 102 others, including 22 army personnel, are missing due to the disaster.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

## 'Saw My Pregnant Wife and Baby Being Washed Away'

Nishant Gupta, a driver and a resident of [Rangpo](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/teesta-hydropower-project-running-losses-harming-environment) West in Pakyong district of Sikkim, lost his entire family – his pregnant wife and a four-year-old son – to the disaster.

> "The police began alerting us at around 2 am to evacuate. I planned to drive up my family to higher reaches till the floodwaters would subside. I helped my wife and son to get to the car and even started the engine. I quickly rushed back home to fetch for my father who is old but by the time I got back I saw waters gushing into the car and slowly surrounding us," he narrated to **The Quint.**

"My father and I climbed up a tree to seek shelter. Within minutes, the car with my wife and son was washed away right in front of my eyes. I wanted to save them, but there was no way I could do so. The last thing I could hear was my son screaming, '*Baba molai bachaunu* (Please save me, father). It will haunt me till my last breath," he told **The Quint.**

Gupta said his wife's delivery was due in just 10 days.

"We were so excited to welcome a new member into the family. It would be the perfect gift for *dasain* ([Dusshera)](https://www.thequint.com/topic/dussehra). But life had other plans," he added.

## 'Could Save My Brother But Not His Wife or Kid'

Similarly, Brijkumar Sahu, a 32-year-old daily wage earner and a resident of Melli, a town on the [West Bengal](https://www.thequint.com/topic/west-bengal) and Sikkim border, lost his family to the gushing waters.

"I was fast asleep when, around 3 am, I felt my bed getting wet. I got up and saw that water was gushing into my house. I immediately bolted upstairs to help my family members out. I could get my brother and elderly father out. But my sister-in-law, who was pregnant, and my 5-year-old nephew were stuck in another part of the house. None of us could reach it since the water was flowing in so fast," he told **The Quint.**

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

## 'Rescue Efforts Proving to Be Difficult'

Arun Subba, a resident of Singtam and a local volunteer involved in the rescue efforts in town, underlined the challenges rescuing.

"From the building where I used to stay, we have been able to rescue seven people. The main problem we are facing in our rescue efforts is that the buildings are covered in 10-15 feet of slit and mud. Many people are trapped on the upper floors. But then in many cases, there is no way we can reach them since the access route to these buildings or the staircases have been washed off," he told **The Quint.**

Officials at the disaster management control room in Gangtok said roads and communication lines in Chungthang have been snapped, and they were in the dark about the situation.

"We have absolutely no communication with Chungthang where the flash flood washed away a dam. The town has also been affected. People were evacuated soon after the water level in the Teesta started rising in the early hours of Wednesday. The casualties have not been many. The town has been hit, though," a second official told *Hindustan Times.*

Another official said three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) companies flown to Bagdogra in neighboring West Bengal remained stranded as choppers could not take off for Sikkim.

"As soon as the weather clears, one company will be flown to the worst-hit Chungthang in the Mangan district. The remaining two companies would be stationed at [Gangtok](https://www.thequint.com/news/hot-news/gangtok-seeks-a-solutions-to-mounting-traffic-woes) and Pakyong,” he noted.

# Fact-Check: Old Video From Indore Shared as Family Being Swept Away in Pakistan

## The 2011 video showed five people of a family being swept away near the Patalpani waterfall in Indore.

[Abhilash Mallick](/author/58713/abhilash-mallick)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

Edited By :[Garima Sadhwani](/author/1686850/garima-sadhwani)

A video showing five people getting swept away near what looks like a waterfall has been shared on the internet with a claim that it is from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in [Pakistan](https://www.thequint.com/explainers/explained-pakistan-floods-what-is-causing-it-and-why-so-severe).

The claim comes while Pakistan is experiencing its worst floods in a decade [triggered by torrential rains](https://www.thequint.com/news/world/flood-struck-pakistan-deploy-army-rescue-relief-operations) since 14 June. More than 1,300 people have been killed due to the floods and several thousand have been injured and displaced.

However, we found that the video, which dates back to 2011, was from Indore in Madhya Pradesh. According to news reports, five members of a family were swept away in the waterfall at Patalpani after the water level rose due to a flood after a sudden bout of rainfall.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

## CLAIM

The video was shared with a caption written in Urdu, which, when translated to English, read, "Flood in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa swept away the whole family."

The video was also shared on [Twitter](https://web.archive.org/web/20220830055038/https://twitter.com/PrateekPratap5/status/1564490445522358272) by connecting it to the floods in Pakistan.

## WHAT WE FOUND

We used the [InVID WeVerify Google Chrome extension](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/how-to-verify-viral-videos) to extract keyframes from the viral video and conducted a reverse image search Google. While going through the search results, we came across a [YouTube video posted in 2011](https://perma.cc/KHU9-KWC3) that carried an extended version of the video.

The caption of the video, which was captured on 17 July 2011, said, "Patalpani Accident Indore Full Video."

Taking a cue from the video's caption, we conducted a keyword search on Google for the incident in Indore and found several news reports.

An article published in *[NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/cities/rain-tragedy-in-indore-family-washed-away-at-waterfall-461845)* on 18 July 2011 had clips from the viral video. The article said that "five members of a family were swept away in the waterfall at Patalpani after the water level rose suddenly." The report added that two people managed to swim away while the remaining three drowned.

We also found similar reports published in other news publications such as *[The Indian Express](http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/mp-body-of-girl-swept-away-at-patalpani-waterfall-recovered/819623/)* and *[India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/north/story/mp-3-family-members-drown-in-indore-waterfalls-137741-2011-07-18)*.

We then conducted another keyword search and found reports about a similar incident that happened in Kohistan, which falls under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province. Five brothers were swept and a video of the same was available on news portals.

Evidently, an old video from Indore was shared by social media users to claim that it shows a family being swept away in the Pakistan floods.

# Old Video From Karachi Falsely Shared as Recent Visuals of Kerala Floods

## We found out that the video is unrelated to the current Kerala floods and dates back to 2025.

[Anika K](/author/2434387/anika-k)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video is going viral on the internet, falsely claiming to show visuals of the [Kerala](https://www.thequint.com/news/breaking-news/kerala-heavy-rains-landslides-floods-fatalities-rescue-operations) floods.

* The video shows a man falling off a bike and being carried away by the water.

***(Archived versions of similar claims can be found [here](https://archive.ph/HqyiU) and [here.](https://archive.ph/czUP5))***

**Is it true?:** No, the video dates back to 2025 and is from Karachi, Pakistan. It does not show recent visuals of the Kerala floods.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out?:** We ran a reverse image search on the video using Google Lens and found videosuploaded in 2025 that shared the same visuals.

* One of the [videos](https://archive.ph/ppCGk), uploaded on 22 August 2025, mentions the location as Karachi, Pakistan.

* We found two [other](https://www.instagram.com/inspirednationofficial1/reel/DNk5Kc-oGSg/) [video](https://archive.ph/Q8g64)s, uploaded on 20 August 2025, where the locations were mentined as Shahrah-e-Faisal and Gulshan-e-Iqbal, which are both locations in Karachi, Pakistan.

* We then looked for more videos showing flooding in Karachi from August 2025 and found a video on YouTube that showed on of the hoardings seen in the viral video.

**Conclusion:** The video is from 2025 and does not show recent visuals of the Kerala floods but shows flooding in Karachi, Pakistan.

# Widespread video compilations misrepresent old visuals as Texas flood scenes

* This article is more than one year old.
* Published on July 10, 2025 at 20:55
* 11 min read
* By [Bill MCCARTHY](https://factcheck.afp.com/bill-mccarthy),  [AFP USA](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-usa)

Social media is littered with misrepresented visuals said to show the deadly floodwaters that swept through Texas, in the latest example of misinformation trailing an extreme weather event. Fourteen clips shared in two widespread video compilations are not from the July 4, 2025 floods, as claimed online, but instead depict prior disasters that hit other US states and countries such as China, Indonesia, Mexico, Belgium and Spain.

"July 4, 2025. Catastrophic flooding occurring across portions of the Texas Hill Country," says text over a [TikTok video](https://perma.cc/Q3J6-XMCD) shared [July 5, 2025 to X](https://perma.cc/8UFH-AP3E).

The post, which claims to show the Guadalupe River, cuts between dramatic videos of surging waters barrelling across landscapes and cities, washing away cars and rushing into buildings.

A second [TikTok video](https://perma.cc/FD9F-FEHZ) shared [by the same X user](https://perma.cc/CTC6-UE9H) shows several similar clips, with a text overlay saying they are also scenes from the "floods in Texas."

The [video compilations](https://perma.cc/5RAG-ZRXV) -- and the clips contained within them -- [rocketed](https://perma.cc/HTE5-2MQY) across [platforms](https://perma.cc/P6LM-79PB) after more than 120 people, including at least 27 girls and counselors from a youth summer camp, were [killed](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250710-scrutiny-over-texas-flood-response-mounts-as-death-toll-tops-120) as [catastrophic floods](https://www.communitynewspapergroup.com/news/nation/texas-floods-how-geography-climate-and-policy-failures-collided/article_381ec02a-3a73-5503-9c2d-aa4a1516417b.html) tore through Texas during the 2025 Fourth of July holiday.

But the 14 videos are old and unrelated to the disaster in the southern border state, AFP determined using a combination of [reverse image searches](https://factcheck.afp.com/how-do-reverse-image-search), [keyword searches](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVAKQqO2BE4) and [geolocation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DJuaIsiEYMo). Several of them were also flipped horizontally or sped up.

### China, September 2024

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-07/6dbb98747b582c5f1dec5e14bd2bf7cc-en.jpeg?itok=81aFWwwg)

Screenshot from X taken July 9, 2025

Reverse image searches surfaced the first video from the compilation on the video-licensing websites [ViralBear](https://viralbear.media/library/9787) and [Newsflare](https://www.newsflare.com/video/692896/video-shows-people-fleeing-overflowing-river-in-zhejiang-china) (archived [here](https://perma.cc/EKS8-JWC7) and [here](https://perma.cc/U5VB-39TS)).

The two sites described the footage as showing people fleeing the overflowing Qiantang River -- known for its powerful tidal bore -- in China's Zhejiang province on September 25, 2024.

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-07/d014c889d16d7ac0ae7720df29589c73-en.jpeg?itok=PB5KPUNB)

Screenshot from X taken July 9, 2025

The second video has been online since at least July 19, 2024, when a [Facebook user](https://www.facebook.com/reel/881920030425920) posted it alongside a caption saying it showed a valley in Chitral, Pakistan, an area prone to monsoons (archived [here](https://web.archive.org/web/20250707170806/http:/web.archive.org/screenshot/https:/www.facebook.com/reel/881920030425920)).

### Indonesia, March 2025

Screenshot from X taken July 9, 2025

The third video is a mirrored version of footage that shows a flash flood near the Puncak mountain pass of Bogor Regency, Indonesia, according the TikTok user who originally [uploaded it](https://www.tiktok.com/@wasky134/video/7477229172822117637) March 2, 2025 (archived [here](https://perma.cc/3DGR-MGFC)). The user's caption also mentions the Ciliwung River, a prominent waterway in the area.

A separate video available via [Newsflare](https://www.newsflare.com/video/725581/indonesia-flash-floods-hit-cisarua-puncak-bogor-area) and [CNN Indonesia](https://www.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20250303192942-24-1204582/video-penampakan-banjir-dan-longsor-di-puncak-bogor) shows additional angles of the floodwaters rushing past the same building -- identifiable by its unique black and yellow railings (archived [here](https://perma.cc/LW2W-Q4FG) and [here](https://perma.cc/7JAF-3TYX)). Newsflare's description further specifies that the footage was captured in the town of Cisarua.

AFP [reporting from March 4](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250304-hundreds-evacuated-as-torrential-rains-flood-indonesia-capital) said rain caused the Ciliwung river to overflow, affecting 1,446 people from 224 houses in one village alone, according to Indonesia's National Disaster Mitigation Agency.

The eighth video -- the first in the second compilation analyzed by AFP -- pulls from footage of a wave crashing through the Outrigger Bar & Grill on Roi-Namur, an island of the Marshall Islands, on January 20, 2024.

The original video, which was sped-up and flipped in the compilation online, appeared on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/szNpjdnP_Rw) and was later reposted by [Newsflare](https://www.newsflare.com/video/621852/terrifying-flood-wave-engulfs-bar-outrigger-in-roi-namur-kwajalein-atoll) and [ViralBear](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GZW8YMFJsXk) (archived [here](https://perma.cc/P75P-9WSH), [here](https://perma.cc/T22L-HTMU) and [here](https://perma.cc/H3QT-M3N9)).

### Indonesia, April 2021

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-07/34cf08e04d0aedef137b32014141b5d9-en.jpeg?itok=P7gcSN1T)

The tenth video is a mirrored and sped-up version of a clip [shared](https://archive.ph/OPs3t) to Instagram as early as April 4, 2021 in a since-deleted post that said it shows a flood toppling the Kambaniru bridge in Waingapu, Indonesia. ### Indiana, February 2019

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-07/44d7834d0c7beab358ae1152f1ee5313-en.jpeg?itok=lBgoCtYo)

Screenshot from X taken July 9, 2025

The 12th clip misappropriates -- and sped up and flipped -- a February 7, 2019 video [posted to YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEPBUchMD30) by ViralHog (archived [here](https://perma.cc/QC8G-KH8Y)).

The clip's description says a family's camper was whisked away by a nearby creek's rising waters in Lawrence County, Indiana. Hannah Lee, the mother of the family who captured the video, told [local news](https://www.whas11.com/article/news/local/indiana/ind-family-devastated-after-vacation-camper-swept-away-in-flood/417-23391183-6793-4627-8b04-021104f1b85a) the camper was destroyed when the family found it on a neighbor's farm.

Keyword searches turned up the original clip on Lee's [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/hannah.voorhies/videos/2055027961271651), where she wrote in a comment that it took place on Popcorn Church Road in Springville, Indiana (archived [here](https://web.archive.org/web/20250710163055/https://www.facebook.com/hannah.voorhies/videos/2055027961271651)).

A [National Weather Service](https://www.weather.gov/ind/feb72019severe) storm report for February 7, 2019 recounts a "creek severely out of banks ... flooding peoples yards and flooding vehicles away" in Springville (archived [here](https://perma.cc/3X4W-JV35)).

# Footage of disasters filmed outside Nepal falsely linked to deadly August 2026 floods

* Published on September 2, 2026 at 10:00
* Updated on September 2, 2026 at 11:26
* 3 min read
* By [Yusra JABEEN](https://factcheck.afp.com/yusra-jabeen),  [AFP Pakistan](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-pakistan)

In the aftermath of the deadly floods in Nepal that have killed at least 1,000 people, old videos of flooding and mudslides filmed outside the Himalayan nation have circulated in social media posts that falsely link them to the disaster. The latest includes a compilation that incorporates footage from past disasters in Russia, Japan, Indonesia and Argentina. Searches for the original clips and geolocation show they in fact are not linked to the deadly flooding in August 2026.

"Natural disaster in Nepal, hundreds of tourists go missing," reads an Urdu-language X post [shared](https://perma.cc/PF5L-MBX4) by an account with more than 722,000 followers on August 27.

The attached 46-second montage shows mudslides crashing through buildings and bridges, with superimposed Urdu-language text saying more than 270 people had been killed and 1,500 were missing at the time.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/71a7f6d8c084dddcea683974379f2f61-en.jpeg?itok=-iEEKHIs)

Screenshot of the false post taken on August 28 with red X added by AFP

The death toll from the devastating Himalayan glacial floods [crossed](https://www.dawn.com/news/2026786/toll-from-himalayan-floods-crosses-1000-mark) the grim 1,000 mark on September 1, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels ([archived link](https://perma.cc/YTA9-L4V6)).

Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris triggered by a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on August 26, wiping out entire settlements and carving a path of destruction across Nepal.

The US Geological Survey said the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream.

AFP [has](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6PE9G3) fact-checked [other](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6PM6WF) pictures and videos falsely linked to the Nepal-Tibet floods after the disaster.

The circulating footage has [spread](https://perma.cc/4JDM-RS5R) on Pakistan-based accounts [on X](https://perma.cc/7QNE-ERMB) and on India-based [Facebook accounts](https://perma.cc/4CD5-M34D), where it has racked up more than 551,000 views.

But the clips in the compilation in fact do not show the disaster in Nepal.

## 2025 mudslide in Russia

A Google [reverse image search](https://factcheck.afp.com/how-do-reverse-image-search) found a mirrored version of the first clip showing a mudslide shared on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DMyHLRKsuV7/) on July 31, 2025, with a caption saying it was filmed in Tyrnyauz in Russia's Caucasus region on the day ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260902045625/https://www.instagram.com/reels/DMyHLRKsuV7/)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/b7887ad7fcc25005ed7eca7f04fc513b-en.jpeg?itok=wEhuCwui)

Screenshot comparison of the false post (left) and the Instagram video

A [keyword search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVAKQqO2BE4) also found a video filmed from a different angle [shared](https://t.me/StormSouthRU/1648) on the Telegram messaging app on the day showing the same scene ([archived link](https://perma.cc/9B8W-FC7U)).

Russian state-owned news service RIA [reported](https://ria.ru/20250802/chp-2032994040.html) that heavy rain caused a mudslide that day in the region, and authorities have evacuated local residents in some areas of the town ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20250802150142/https://ria.ru/20250802/chp-2032994040.html)).

## 2021 Japan floods

Another reverse image search using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the clip showing floodwaters rushing down from a hill led to the same footage shared by Japanese outlet [Sankei News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5LWNIhMBNYw) on YouTube on July 3, 2021 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/EPN2-SL7V)).

AFP was able to geolocate the area shown in the video using [Google Street View images](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Izusan+Port/@35.1143778,139.0812425,143a,75y,270.33h,78.59t/data=!3m8!1e1!3m6!1sxiYJBAFhxBkloIWsaoX7_g!2e0!5s20180701T000000!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fcb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile%26w%3D900%26h%3D600%26pitch%3D11.413360065640333%26panoid%3DxiYJBAFhxBkloIWsaoX7_g%26yaw%3D270.32987728120924!7i13312!8i6656!4m7!3m6!1s0x6019be86868828d9:0x6a09f54f29249e17!8m2!3d35.1102062!4d139.0863997!10e5!16s%2Fg%2F11b7yq5v_9?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDgzMS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260902025030/https://www.google.com/maps/place/Izusan+Port/@35.1143778,139.0812425,143a,75y,270.33h,78.59t/data=!3m8!1e1!3m6!1sxiYJBAFhxBkloIWsaoX7_g!2e0!5s20180701T000000!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fcb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile%26w%3D900%26h%3D600%26pitch%3D11.413360065640333%26panoid%3DxiYJBAFhxBkloIWsaoX7_g%26yaw%3D270.32987728120924!7i13312!8i6656!4m7!3m6!1s0x6019be86868828d9:0x6a09f54f29249e17!8m2!3d35.1102062!4d139.0863997!10e5!16s%2Fg%2F11b7yq5v_9?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDgzMS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)).

Torrents of mud [crashed](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/world/article/204425/One-dead-two-missing-in-Japan-after-heavy-rain#:~:text=Strong%20rain%20in%202021%20triggered%20a%20devastating%20landslide%20in%20the%20central%20resort%20town%20of%20Atami%20that%20killed%2027%20people) through part of the town following days of heavy rain at the time and killed 27 people ([archived link](https://perma.cc/RHS6-N5P8)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/b0ca903b27c20dda8e200db679cbb4cf-en.jpeg?itok=lpQUkgZC)

Screenshot comparison of the false video (left) and the report from Sankei News

The same clip has circulated in other false [claims](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.33VN99Y) previously [debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.69TY3NQ) by AFP.

## 2020 Indonesia deluge

A separate reverse image search found the video of a current battering a bridge was [published](https://www.newsflare.com/video/361931/bridge-collapses-into-flooded-river-after-heavy-rain-in-indonesia) by British news agency Newsflare on June 11, 2020, with a caption saying it shows the Molintogupo Bridge in the Gorontalo province in Indonesia collapsing ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260902025638/https://www.newsflare.com/video/361931/bridge-collapses-into-flooded-river-after-heavy-rain-in-indonesia)).

The clip in the circulating posts had been mirrored. The state-owned news agency Antara [published](https://sulteng.antaranews.com/berita/129632/jembatan-molintogupo-bone-bolango-ambruk-diterjang-banjir) a picture of the bridge days after it collapsed ([archived link](https://perma.cc/98A9-QPBA)).

The outlet also [reported](https://en.antaranews.com/news/150596/flash-flood-inundates-homes-in-gorontalo-impacts-1150-residents) at the time that flooding in some parts of the province affected some 1,150 people, with floodwater reaching nearly 1.5 metres (4.9 feet) ([archived link](https://perma.cc/9JNG-ZHCK)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/d44dc66d62f63f24e1ef844c5ec5c261-en.jpeg?itok=CGOQwMuy)

Screenshot comparison of the false post (left) and the Newsflare video

## 2023 Argentina bridge collapse

AFP traced the clip in the montage showing a bridge collapse to a TikTok post that [shared](https://www.tiktok.com/@arielberrondo/video/7316553942773976325) a longer version on December 25, 2023, with a caption saying it shows a bridge in the Poman Department in the Catamarca province in Argentina ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260902053803/https://www.tiktok.com/@arielberrondo/video/7316553942773976325)).

Local media [reported](https://www.pagina12.com.ar/698397-video-la-feroz-crecida-de-un-rio-que-arraso-con-un-puente-en/) that heavy rains in the region caused a landslide that swept away the footbridge, which was completed just over a month before it was destroyed ([archived link](https://perma.cc/N9HB-VWKP)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/ec7755b6bcbc25d1e7eb4fa61d457416-en.jpeg?itok=aidBqvcu)

Screenshot comparison of the false post (left) and the original video uploaded to TikTok

The provincial government [published](https://www.facebook.com/Catamarca.Gob/posts/pfbid02hhe6iBfadxQ7maUcxQuNJ2fH1rjhqvH3JRiukzMCv6Y26CTinfcPq96oJJVBZZQzl) a picture on its Facebook account on November 6, 2023 showing the same bridge after it was completed ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260902034515/https://www.facebook.com/Catamarca.Gob/posts/pfbid02hhe6iBfadxQ7maUcxQuNJ2fH1rjhqvH3JRiukzMCv6Y26CTinfcPq96oJJVBZZQzl)).

# Old India disaster footage misrepresented as Nepal-Tibet floods

After deadly floods tore through the Nepal-Tibet border in August 2026, social media posts recirculated footage claiming it showed the disaster unfolding. However, this is false; the unrelated video depicts flash floods that struck India's northern state of Uttarakhand in August 2025.

"Terrifying moment as floodwaters sweep through Nepal," reads part of an English Facebook [post](https://perma.cc/RF5H-Y7JA?type=image) published on August 29, 2026, by a Mauritian account.

"Absolutely terrifying footage appears to show hydropower workers watching from their camp as a massive surge of water and debris approaches," the post adds. "The workers reportedly knew something was coming, but the speed and sheer force of the flood were far beyond what they expected."

The post contains a video of a flash flood tearing through a valley, destroying properties and infrastructure.

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/a3f783e4f260a0edf74fa219ec11ad35-en.jpeg?itok=WbqloEug)

Similar posts spread in [Bengali](https://perma.cc/U4KT-2PRC?type=image) and [English](https://perma.cc/YNK2-CWP8?type=image) on [Facebook](https://perma.cc/R7MK-FFLE?type=image), [Instagram](https://perma.cc/G3YX-P2MG?type=image)and [X](https://perma.cc/2RYF-7TTQ?type=image).

The videos surfaced after catastrophic flooding and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed waves of water and debris that [killed](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/pilgrims-seeking-peace-caught-deadly-032632593.html) more than 470 people and left upwards of 1,400 missing ([archived here](https://perma.cc/9YZX-T45J?type=image)).

The surge of water hit villages and towns on the path of two rivers -- Bhote Koshi and Trishuli in Nepal.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including trekkers in the Himalayan nation, as well as scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet's sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.

According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.

Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.

However, the video is unrelated and was filmed in India.

## Uttarakhand floods

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google of the video using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8), followed by [keyword searches](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FfugMVf5WuY), surfaced an [Instagram video](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DM-rGp0Jcx8/) published by the weather platform AccuWeather on August 5, 2025 ([archived here](https://perma.cc/LU8W-8M68?type=standard)).

"Dharali, India," its caption says -- referring to a village in the Uttarakhand state -- with the footage credited to visual licensing platform [Reuters Connect](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/india-flood-in-kheerganga-river-in-uttarkashi-district-of-uttarakhand-after-cloudburst/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX09XU0hCQzEwNjUxMDg) ([archived here](https://perma.cc/Z7D3-CP5F)).

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/ace8eae396b434e1aa1364582a4ba54a-en.jpeg?itok=_WZA0M4K)

The falsely shared footage also corresponds to [Google Earth Satellite imagery](https://earth.google.com/web/@31.03996082,78.78123668,2544.08357388a,225.87785082d,35y,165.1222457h,59.99621745t,359.99999895r/data=CgRCAggBOgMKATBCAggASg0I____________ARAA?authuser=0) of India's Dharali ([archived here](https://perma.cc/N4KZ-TVB6)).

Indian officials say at least 70 people were [killed](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250812-toll-of-india-himalayan-flood-likely-to-be-at-least-70) in August 2025 after a deadly wall of icy water swept away the Himalayan town and buried it in mud ([archived here](https://web.archive.org/web/20260828045842/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250812-toll-of-india-himalayan-flood-likely-to-be-at-least-70)).

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/fbc2889383375b29215a84d1d8d63fd8-en.jpeg?itok=mgBjNp1P)

AFP Fact Check has [debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6M39WH) other [false claims](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6PE9G3) related to the flooding in Nepal.

# None of these visuals are related to the Nepal floods in August 2026

![Nitish Kumar Dhonge](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/aa25bd8a70a5f0525e72675022ac12d97edc4861706554b09fe2739a0fbce6af?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Nitish Kumar Dhonge](https://factly.in/author/nitish-kumar-dhonge/ "Posts by Nitish Kumar Dhonge")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/none-of-these-visuals-are-related-to-the-nepal-floods-in-august-2026/#respond)6 Mins Read

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fnone-of-these-visuals-are-related-to-the-nepal-floods-in-august-2026%2F "Share on Facebook")   [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fnone-of-these-visuals-are-related-to-the-nepal-floods-in-august-2026%2F&text=None%20of%20these%20visuals%20are%20related%20to%20the%20Nepal%20floods%20in%20August%202026 "Share on X (Twitter)")   [Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fnone-of-these-visuals-are-related-to-the-nepal-floods-in-august-2026%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F%2F2026%2F08%2FAugust-2026-Nepal-floods-Thumbnail.jpg&description=None%20of%20these%20visuals%20are%20related%20to%20the%20Nepal%20floods%20in%20August%202026 "Share on Pinterest")   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fnone-of-these-visuals-are-related-to-the-nepal-floods-in-august-2026%2F "Share on LinkedIn")   [Tumblr](https://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fnone-of-these-visuals-are-related-to-the-nepal-floods-in-august-2026%2F&name=None%20of%20these%20visuals%20are%20related%20to%20the%20Nepal%20floods%20in%20August%202026 "Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

On 26 August 2026, massive flash floods struck parts of Nepal and Tibet, causing widespread destruction as rivers including the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli overflowed and swept away homes, roads, bridges, and other infrastructure. Experts said the disaster was likely triggered by the collapse of a glacier and a massive ice-and-rock avalanche in the Himalayas, which sent huge amounts of debris and water into the river systems. As of 28 August 2026, the death toll in Nepal had risen to 469, according to Nepal Police, while nearly 1,000 people remained missing as search and rescue operations continued ([here](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cr0qxd1y219kt), [here](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/nepal-flash-floods-death-toll-surges-nearly-1500-missing-fresh-flood-threat-glacier-collapse-live-updates-august-28-2026/article71398953.ece), and [here](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/26/world/asia/flood-nepal-tibet.html)).

Amid the disaster, multiple visuals are being shared on social media with the claim that they show visuals of the August 2026 Nepal floods. Let’s verify the truth behind these visuals in this article.

> **Claim:** The visuals show the August 2026 Nepal floods.
>
> **Fact**: None of the videos are related to the Nepal floods in August 2026. They are either old videos from other locations or AI-generated videos that are being shared as visuals of the disaster. Hence, the claim made in the post is **Misleading**.

**Video 1**

This [video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1105755468678770) is being shared on social media with the claim that it shows a Chinese helicopter reaching the site where a glacier had broken, causing a massive amount of water to be released and resulting in widespread destruction in Nepal.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-1-828x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55978410?key=aa0b1f66cf1b2657adf7871770ddaa67).

In our investigation, we found that the video was originally [uploaded](https://www.instagram.com/p/DcUFQZhvGzS/) ([archived](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55978796?key=2de7af393e7d47eec1f34b011d31ea12)) on the Instagram account of Leigh Coates, an American commercial helicopter pilot based in Valdez, Alaska. She posted the video on 22 August 2026 and specifically identified the location as Columbia Glacier in Alaska. She explained that a Jökulhlaup, also known as a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF), occurs when water trapped by glacier ice suddenly finds a way out, causing the water to drain rapidly beneath the glacier and rush downhill with immense force. She further stated that such events have been occurring annually at Columbia Glacier since 2014, although they are rarely captured because they generally occur in remote areas.

**Video 2**

The [video](https://x.com/dmuppavarapu/status/2092846095751905510) is being shared on social media with claims that it shows the largest lake in the mountains whose embankment breached, causing the massive Nepal-Tibet floods.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-2.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55980143?key=da4702b6b3c6b98f286c870f9ce4f605).

We found that the [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E5TOaoetGDo) was uploaded by Leigh Coates on her official YouTube channel on 16 August 2026, before the Nepal floods. The video is titled “Before and After a Jökulhlaup Glacial Outburst Flood” and shows an example of the glacial outburst flood that occurred in Juneau, Alaska. This confirms that the video is unrelated to the August 2026 Nepal-Tibet floods.

**Video 3**

The video ([here](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/1oT56HbSnVI), [here](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1771313084066281), and [here](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1771313084066281)) is being shared with claims on social media that it shows vehicles and buildings being swept away by flash floods in Nepal.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-3-595x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55980977?key=7a0c97a0275edfc5bf2737d7f965b8de).

However, we [found](https://www.facebook.com/reel/4679277042293724/) ([archived](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55950933?key=1464962bd6490be94d8ca59f3d841dca)) that this video has been available on the internet since 04 August 2026, at least 22 days before the Nepal floods. Moreover, upon examining the video, we noticed that the movement of the water and vehicles appeared unnatural.

We also analysed the video using AI detection tools such as [Hive](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/image/63057823?key=e5da3f3985f4d79c22fd02c46a8413f6), which indicated that the video was AI-generated.

**Video 4**

This [video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1677583674374727) is being shared with the claim that it shows vehicles being swept away by heavy floods during the August 2026 Nepal disaster.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-4.png)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55951159?key=5bb71ac2765dd6639d0425daf194313f).

We [found](https://youtu.be/20wbqiDdBf4?si=3wlPQjCnlrCQhnIT&t=21) that this video is related to the flash floods that occurred in the Chamoli region of Uttarakhand on 10 August 2026. Media reports ([here](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/uttarakhand-rainfall-weather-watch-flash-flood-in-uttarakhand-niti-valley-washes-away-vehicles-after-bridge-collapse-11893823), [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0_L9vUm8Ris)) from the time also carried the same visuals and reported that vehicles were swept away after a bridge collapsed amid the flooding.

**Video 5**

This [video](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/IEca8tTqorQ) is being shared with the claim that it shows a mudslide rapidly turning into a torrent of muddy floodwater during the August 2026 Nepal floods.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-5-575x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55981737?key=207ea61ca90a06c4bc499bdc6358d4c8).

We [found](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_z2_IEqOBNg&t=3s) that the video is not related to the August 2026 Nepal floods. The video was actually recorded in Hpakant, Myanmar, in January 2024 ([here](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DaLtKtjzTtq/), [here](https://www.geoengineer.org/news/mine-waste-dam-failure-in-myanmar-caught-on-video)).

**Video 6**

This [video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1574705387436469) is being shared with the claim that it shows water and debris rushing down from a mountainous area and sweeping away homes during the August 2026 flash floods in Nepal.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-6-798x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55982118?key=30867de1e2d408490f3090bdc7ac4318).

We found ([here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0UIb-JB6gU), [here](https://www.bhaskarenglish.in/national/news/uncut-video-cloudburst-uttarakhand-debris-buries-dharali-village-on-riverbank-135613681.html), and [here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DM-HSFMSxmk/)) that this video is from Dharali village in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, and dates back to August 2025. It shows flash floods that occurred following a cloudburst in the upper catchment area of the Kheer Ganga River. The resulting floodwaters, debris and silt surged through Dharali, washing away houses and other structures. At least four people were confirmed dead, while more than 50 others were reported missing.

**Video 7**

This [video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1696933708042592) is being shared with the claim that it shows a massive landslide occurring during the August 2026 Nepal floods.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-7.png)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55951421?key=ce3091a0f204c5a07959d22f2a4b9e7f).

We found ([here](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=3253185424883859), [here](https://www.threads.com/@luo256245/post/Db5BK29ikmo)) that this video has been available on the internet since at least 11 August 2026, predating the recent Nepal floods. Several users have [claimed](https://www.reddit.com/r/DisasterUpdate/comments/1vljtms/this_massive_mountain_collapse_was_captured_on/) that the landslide was triggered by an earthquake that struck Colombia on 10 August 2026.

**Video 8**

This [video](https://x.com/warsurv/status/2092592456734785723?s=20) is being shared with the claim that it shows a power plant being devastated amid the August 2026 Nepal floods. News outlets like [**NDTV**](https://archive.ph/wdqOj), [**Dainik Bhaskar**](https://archive.ph/ojlAK), and [**Divya Bhaskar**](https://archive.ph/bNpsq) also shared the video, claiming it was from Nepal.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-8-774x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55983208?key=ec4a4147c47538e1f942234e2fac501b).

We found  ([here](https://www.thefridaytimes.com/16-Feb-2023/how-the-devastating-2022-flood-still-impacts-lower-kohistan#google_vignette), [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CsK22QjQTQs), and [here](https://mvau.lt/media/489433f8-eaa7-4274-bec5-d9ee722ccc82)) that this video has been available online since at least 2022 and is not related to the August 2026 Nepal floods.

**Video 9**

This [video](https://x.com/SantaniSubhajit/status/2092588667957342691) is being shared with the claim that it shows people in Nepal running ahead of fast-moving floodwaters during the severe floods on 26 August 2026. [Dainik Bhaskar](https://archive.is/ByVBc), [Punjab Kesari TV](https://mvau.lt/media/2c8faa0d-34b5-4e97-a4e8-498b8853c063), and [News18 Tamil Nadu](https://mvau.lt/media/4a027f0e-035d-43cf-a935-7fec6e2e2610) also shared the video in the context of the Nepal floods.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-9-616x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55983988?key=3e2cb7aea163431202b8ad683c5ae988).

We [found](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1815380632791412) that the video was available online as early as 04 August 2026, well before the 26 August 2026 Nepal floods, and therefore predates the disaster. The original post stated that the video showed rainfall in Yafa, a mountainous region of Yemen ([here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wsoKJydaZos), [here](https://www.adngad.net/news/871062)).

**Video 10**

The video ([here](https://www.facebook.com/watch?v=1101722282294182), [here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DciyFL-AYrh/)) shows an elephant rescuing a man during the August 2026 Nepal floods.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/08/August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-10-1024x423.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55984698?key=560e10de72d93b55da2dc9934e0ff46f).

We [found](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2btkPB-1zL0) that the video shows an elephant rescuing a man in Assam, India. The video was filmed several weeks before the August 2026 Nepal floods and is therefore unrelated to the disaster.

To sum up, none of these visuals are related to the Nepal floods in August 2026.

# Old video from Pakistan misrepresented as deadly Nepal-Tibet flood

* Published on August 28, 2026 at 09:42
* 2 min read
* By [Devesh MISHRA](https://factcheck.afp.com/devesh-mishra),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

Devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border in August 2026 killed hundreds of people, disrupted power supplies and damaged hydropower infrastructure, but a video circulating online showing floodwaters is not linked to the recent catastrophe. The footage predates the disaster and shows the Ranolia Hydropower Plant in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province during catastrophic floods in August 2022.

"Several power projects were swept away along with debris during the devastating floods in Nepal. Reports from Nepal say 13 riverside power projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts have been affected. Sixty-five people working on the Langtang Hydropower Project are missing," reads a Hindi-language X post [shared](https://perma.cc/G9RG-P942) on August 26, 2026.

The attached nine-second video shows a fast-flowing river eroding the embankment of a power plant before washing away a substantial portion of the site.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/a33bfff8a003ae4a48befe087f8a2948-en.jpeg?itok=8F_hWp_R)

Screenshot of the false X post taken on August 27, with a red X added by AFP

[Devastating floods](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260827-desperate-families-search-for-missing-after-nepal-floods) struck the Nepal-Tibet border region on August 26, with a tsunami-like wall of water and mud sweeping through villages and towns along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers ([archived link](https://perma.cc/NME4-7U5T)).

At least 469 people have been killed, Nepali police [said](https://en.prothomalo.com/international/south-asia/umwwgxycf6) on August 28, while Chinese state media had earlier confirmed three dead. More than 1,400 people are missing, including hundreds of foreigners ([archived link](https://perma.cc/G2YW-TVXL)).

Nepali army helicopter rescue teams were also [working](https://english.aawsat.com/world/5311947-nepal-army-trying-save-100-people-trapped-tunnel-hydropower-project) on the day to rescue around 100 people trapped inside a tunnel at a hydropower project swamped by the devastating flood ([archived link](https://perma.cc/M5S6-C8CV)).

The Nepalese prime minister's office said in a statement that the army had been working in tough conditions. It did not give further details about the nationalities of those rescued or trapped.

The clip circulated with similar claims elsewhere on [X](https://perma.cc/5DGE-4HFF) and [Instagram](https://perma.cc/FR74-LT4S), but it was actually filmed in 2022 and shows floods that ravaged Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

## 2022 Pakistan flood

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google found the same video [uploaded](https://www.instagram.com/p/ChzTcCQsZj-/) on a Pakistan-based Instagram account on August 28, 2022 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/BQN6-2K8H)).

Its caption reads: "Flood in Dubair", referring to Pakistan's [Dubair](https://www.dawn.com/news/2005921) valley -- a flood-prone area in the lower Kohistan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260609064045/https://www.dawn.com/news/2005921)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-08/b438801821f522748d81c174623b1609-en.jpeg?itok=5irT3q4k)

Screenshot comparison of the false video (L) and the 2022 Instagram post

AFP reached out to the account owner, Saeed Anwar, a travel photographer and data analyst with the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government, who confirmed the video was filmed in Pakistan.

"I captured this video in August 2022 in Dubair, a village in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province," Anwar told AFP on August 27. "It shows the Ranolia hydropower project being swept away by heavy floodwaters."

Monsoon rains and flash floods [devastated](https://www.geo.tv/latest/436401-pakistan-orders-thousands-to-evacuate-near-flood-swollen-rivers) large parts of Pakistan at the time, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The floods killed more than 1,700 people and affected millions, [according](https://news.un.org/en/story/2022/10/1129337) to UN figures (archived [here](https://perma.cc/4S4D-XV7Z) and [here](https://web.archive.org/web/20250909014901/https://news.un.org/en/story/2022/10/1129337)).

Local media also [reported](https://www.thefridaytimes.com/16-Feb-2023/how-the-devastating-2022-flood-still-impacts-lower-kohistan) the flooding severely damaged the Ranolia Hydropower Project, and it remained out of service six months after the disaster ([archived link](https://perma.cc/87HL-JR8X)).

Another user [shared](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1199662810607261) a clip of the flooding showing the same scene in a video comparing the area before and after the disaster ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20260828051828/https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1199662810607261)).

Anwar [reshared](https://www.instagram.com/p/DciGbUSoIN5/) the footage on his Instagram account after the Nepal floods, with a clarification that he filmed the clip in 2022 in Pakistan ([archived link](https://perma.cc/GG55-VYD8)).

AFP has [debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.C6PE9G3) other false claims related to the flooding in Nepal.

# Glacier burst video from Alaska falsely viral as Nepal flash flood trigger

Footage of a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood or GLOF phenomenon happening over Alaska’s Columbia Glacier was falsely shared by social media users as the cause behind the devastating August 26 floods in Nepal

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/a4a0477ebec4d5590fdb727dbcaa04b3cec9f6db79e9eea09829393dcc4032a6?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/prantikali/)

[Prantik Ali](https://www.altnews.in/author/prantikali/)

 ![Glacier burst video from Alaska falsely viral as Nepal flash flood trigger](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Copy-of-Feature-Image-Template-1-1024x576.png) 

Following the devasting flash floods in Nepal on August 26, which claimed over [1,200 lives](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/nepal-flash-floods-live-updates-rescue-operations-relief-death-toll-missing-persons-news-september-2-2026/article71417912.ece) and caused massive destruction, a video has gone viral on social media, purporting to show the Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) phenomenon. It displays footage from a search helicopter, ostensibly showing the breach of a glacial lake in China. Users on social media have widely shared the clip, claiming that this was the immediate trigger to the Nepal floods.

X user Bhavesh Mane ([@iambmane](https://x.com/iambmane/status/2092696500640022649)) posted the clip on August 27, with the hashtag #NepalFloods. At the time of this article being written, the post garnered 2 million views, and was reshared close to 2,000 times. ([Archive](https://archive.is/lhxEa))

> A Glacial Lake Outburst Flood [#GLOF](https://x.com/hashtag/GLOF?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) can happen when a glacier-dammed lake suddenly breaches. 🌊🧊
>
> Pressure and fractures create a pathway for the trapped water to escape, sending a massive surge of water and debris downhill at terrifying speed[#GlacialFlood](https://x.com/hashtag/GlacialFlood?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#NepalFloods](https://x.com/hashtag/NepalFloods?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Nepal](https://x.com/hashtag/Nepal?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/0zrw0SIEqO](https://t.co/0zrw0SIEqO)
>
> — Bhavesh Mane (@iambmane) [August 26, 2026](https://x.com/iambmane/status/2092696500640022649?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

**Also Read: [Nepal floods: Unrelated videos of past disasters, AI visuals falsely viral](https://www.altnews.in/nepal-floods-unrelated-videos-of-past-disasters-ai-visuals-falsely-viral/)**

A journalist with Dainik Bhaskar, Ashish Rai ([@journorai](https://x.com/journorai/status/2092786304606257522)) also posted the clip on X, which received 2 million views and close to 4,000 reshares. ([Archive](https://archive.is/bRO4P)) 

Several other X users, like former MLA Rajpal Singh Sekhawat ([@Rajpal\_BJP](https://x.com/Rajpal_BJP/status/2092812385795125484)), Dr. Kiran J Patel ([@kiranpatel1977](https://x.com/kiranpatel1977/status/2092869660589056372?s=20)), Pradhyumn Sharma ([@pradhyu78651514](https://x.com/pradhyu78651514/status/2093224955425222991?lang=ar-x-fm)), AH Siddiqui ([@anwar0262](https://x.com/anwar0262/status/2092854571182002620?s=20)) and ([@greatandhranews](https://x.com/greatandhranews/status/2093051138329411752)) posted the clip with the same claim. (Archives: [1](https://archive.is/UzMK1), [2](https://archive.is/9tLY5), [3](https://archive.is/qs5ex), [4](https://archive.is/GpJti), [5](https://archive.is/KAnv4))

This slideshow requires JavaScript.

#### Fact Check

To check whether the claims surrounding this viral clip are authentic, we broke it down into keyframes, then ran reverse image searches on the keyframes. This led us to an Instagram reel, uploaded by an user with the handle ([@helipilotleigh](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcUFQZhvGzS/)), on August 22. It contains the exact same footage as the viral clip.

> View this post on Instagram
>
> [A post shared by Leigh Coates (@helipilotleigh)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcUFQZhvGzS/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

In the caption, the user, whose name is Leigh Coates, explains what a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood, or GLOF is, and mentions that the video shows one happening over the Columbia Glacier in Alaska.

The description on [her YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@HeliPilotLeigh/videos) states that she is a helicopter pilot based in the United States, who specialises in ferry flights and advanced training for mountain flying, as well as airport landings.

We noticed that she had uploaded similar videos of glacial outbursts on her Instagram profile, and her YouTube channel.

In conclusion, the video that went viral recently in the context of the Nepal flash flood, showing a glacial outburst — purportedly in China — is actually from the Columbia Glacier in Alaska. It was uploaded by a helicopter pilot named Leigh Coates on her Instagram handle, a few days before the flash flood in Nepal. Thus, the claim that the phenomenon shown in this video was a direct trigger for the August 26 Nepal floods is false and misleading.

# This viral photo does not show children affected by the August 2026 Nepal floods; it was taken in Vietnam in 2007

![Nitish Kumar Dhonge](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/aa25bd8a70a5f0525e72675022ac12d97edc4861706554b09fe2739a0fbce6af?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Nitish Kumar Dhonge](https://factly.in/author/nitish-kumar-dhonge/ "Posts by Nitish Kumar Dhonge")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/this-viral-photo-does-not-show-children-affected-by-the-august-2026-nepal-floods-it-was-taken-in-vietnam-in-2007/#respond)3 Mins Read

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fthis-viral-photo-does-not-show-children-affected-by-the-august-2026-nepal-floods-it-was-taken-in-vietnam-in-2007%2F "Share on Facebook")   [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fthis-viral-photo-does-not-show-children-affected-by-the-august-2026-nepal-floods-it-was-taken-in-vietnam-in-2007%2F&text=This%20viral%20photo%20does%20not%20show%20children%20affected%20by%20the%20August%202026%20Nepal%20floods%3B%20it%20was%20taken%20in%20Vietnam%20in%202007 "Share on X (Twitter)")   [Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fthis-viral-photo-does-not-show-children-affected-by-the-august-2026-nepal-floods-it-was-taken-in-vietnam-in-2007%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F%2F2026%2F09%2FChildren-affected-by-the-August-2026-Nepal-floods-Thumbnail.jpg&description=This%20viral%20photo%20does%20not%20show%20children%20affected%20by%20the%20August%202026%20Nepal%20floods%3B%20it%20was%20taken%20in%20Vietnam%20in%202007 "Share on Pinterest")   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fthis-viral-photo-does-not-show-children-affected-by-the-august-2026-nepal-floods-it-was-taken-in-vietnam-in-2007%2F "Share on LinkedIn")   [Tumblr](https://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fthis-viral-photo-does-not-show-children-affected-by-the-august-2026-nepal-floods-it-was-taken-in-vietnam-in-2007%2F&name=This%20viral%20photo%20does%20not%20show%20children%20affected%20by%20the%20August%202026%20Nepal%20floods%3B%20it%20was%20taken%20in%20Vietnam%20in%202007 "Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

On 26 August 2026, massive flash floods struck parts of Nepal and Tibet after an ice-and-rock avalanche triggered a surge of water and debris through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems. The disaster destroyed homes, roads, bridges, hydropower projects and other infrastructure. As of 04 September, at least 1,252 people have died in Nepal, and more than 4,200 remain missing. Search and rescue operations are continuing, with two hydropower workers rescued alive from a tunnel on 4 September, nine days after the disaster ([here](https://mofa.gov.np/content/1874/sixth-press-briefing-on-bhote-koshi-floods/), [here](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/one-person-rescued-alive-tunnel-nepal-lawmaker-says-2026-09-04/), [here](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cr0qxd1y219kt), and [here](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/nepal-flash-floods-death-toll-surges-nearly-1500-missing-fresh-flood-threat-glacier-collapse-live-updates-august-28-2026/article71398953.ece)).

Amid this, a photo is being widely shared on social media ([here](https://www.facebook.com/rakhi.dutta.902/posts/pfbid0VBWEDaFYrpoRdKkJgtf3kbtcw49U3Z9mw4cDZZkg1FMEyPYvRZJMCBMQ7d5vcRkjl), [here](https://www.facebook.com/drjayadev/posts/pfbid07hRAR8j4AEoCDgAyjkWtTDXZwshvCeh4BmhptEHkZGgUtN4SAwWw9fSVC55bdo3nl), and [here](https://www.facebook.com/search/top/?q=%E0%B4%B6%E0%B5%81%E0%B4%AD%F0%9F%98%8A%E0%B4%A6%E0%B4%BF%E0%B4%A8%E0%B4%82%20%20A%20two%20and%20a%20half%20year%20old%20sister%20being%20protected%20by%20four%20year%20old%20brother.%20%23Nepal%20%23Flood)) with the claim that it shows a young girl being protected by her brother, who were victims of the Nepal floods. Let’s verify the truth behind the photo in this article.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/09/Children-affected-by-the-August-2026-Nepal-floods-Claim-846x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/image/63286742?key=2acec767ff92169b65222c4dd75392d6).

> **Claim:** The photo shows a young girl being protected by her brother, who are victims of the August 2026 Nepal floods.
>
> **Fact**: The photo is not related to the August 2026 Nepal floods. Vietnamese photojournalist Na Son Nguyen took it in October 2007 in Can Ty, a remote village in Hà Giang province, Vietnam. The photo shows two Hmong siblings, with the boy comforting his younger sister while their parents were away working in the fields. Hence, the claim made in the post is **Misleading**.

A Google Lens search of the viral photo led us to a [BBC report](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-32579598) ([archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20260904061030/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-32579598)) dated 4 May 2015 featuring the same photo, confirming that it predates the 2026 Nepal floods. According to the report, Vietnamese photographer Na Son Nguyen took the photo in October 2007 in Can Ty, a remote village in Ha Giang province, Vietnam. Talking to the BBC, he said the photo shows two Hmong siblings, with the boy comforting his crying sister while their parents were away working in the fields. He also said this was his most-shared photo, but unfortunately, it was repeatedly circulated online in the wrong context.

We also [found](https://www.instagram.com/nasonphoto/p/0-4mXgketu/?hl=en) ([archived](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/image/63287724?key=bed38ea6b06ba6f8594fc5c6bb5c7b63)) an Instagram post by Vietnam-based photojournalist Na Son Nguyen featuring the same photo, published on 2 April 2015. The post states that Nguyen captured the photo in October 2007 in a mountainous village in Hà Giang province, Vietnam. He said the photo shows a young boy comforting his younger sister while their parents were away working in the fields. This confirms that the viral photo is unrelated to the recent floods in Nepal.

To sum up, this viral photo does not show children affected by the August 2026 Nepal floods; it was taken in Vietnam in 2007.
