# Image of India disaster misrepresented as glacial floods at Nepal-Tibet border

* Published on September 1, 2026 at 08:38
* 2 min read
* By [Vishesh SINGH](https://factcheck.afp.com/vishesh-singh),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india),  [AFP Australia](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-australia)

In the wake of glacial floods in Nepal in August 2026 that have killed hundreds, social media posts questioning the cause used an old image that was misrepresented as a scene from the disaster. The picture was in fact taken from a video which depicts flash floods that struck India's Uttarakhand in August 2025.

"More than 150 people are dead and hundreds more missing after an enormous wave of water, ice, mud and rock cascaded more than 170 kilometres down the Bhote Koshi River valley in Nepal," reads an [August 28 post](https://perma.cc/68ZZ-MXYV) from a Melbourne-based Facebook page which says it shares "news, analysis and opinions from Australia focused on multicultural communities and the Indian subcontinent".

The post included a blurry photo of muddy waters and debris cascading down a valley near red-roofed houses.

"Tsunami of dirt: what caused Nepal’s deadly glacial flood?" was embedded in the image, a question that was echoed in the post.

"At least 34 Australians are missing. There was little warning," the post says, calling on Facebook users to click through to a [news article](https://web.archive.org/web/20260901042750/https://www.theaustraliatoday.com.au/tsunami-of-dirt-what-caused-nepals-deadly-glacial-flood/) in the comments.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/e7a7ba223fab084818874eb5ee6affbf-en.jpeg?itok=rVc1w2mP)

Screenshot of the false Facebook post taken on September 1, 2026, with the red X added by AFP

A similar post with the same image also appeared on [X](https://perma.cc/F34H-XQ4M), shared by the same outlet.

The image surfaced after catastrophic flooding and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed waves of water and debris, [killing](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260831-nepal-buries-dead-as-rescuers-seek-thousands-missing) more than 900 people and leaving upwards of 4,500 missing ([archived link](https://perma.cc/2KSN-JR9H)).

Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including trekkers in the Himalayan nation, as well as scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet's sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.

The US Geological Survey (USGS) said the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.

Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.

But the photo shown in the Australian posts was in fact from a video taken in India a year earlier.

## Uttarakhand floods

A [Google reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) of the photo, followed by [keyword searches](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FfugMVf5WuY), surfaced an [Instagram video](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DM-rGp0Jcx8/) published by the weather platform AccuWeather on August 5, 2025 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/LU8W-8M68?type=standard)).

"Dharali, India," its caption says -- referring to a village in the Uttarakhand state -- with the footage credited to visual licensing platform [Reuters Connect](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/india-flood-in-kheerganga-river-in-uttarkashi-district-of-uttarakhand-after-cloudburst/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX09XU0hCQzEwNjUxMDg) ([archived link](https://perma.cc/Z7D3-CP5F)).

Image

# Log-filled river in India misrepresented as showing flooding from Nepal-Tibet disaster

* Published on September 3, 2026 at 06:10
* 2 min read
* By [Najmi MAMAT](https://factcheck.afp.com/najmi-mamat),  [AFP Malaysia](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-malaysia)

A high-altitude glacial collapse in the Himalayas unleashed a destructive wall of freezing water and debris that carved a path of destruction across Nepal, but footage showing a raging river seemingly filled with tree logs was not filmed after the disaster. The clip previously circulated a year earlier during flooding in India's Himachal Pradesh state.

"God is great. Pray for Nepal," says part of the Malay-language caption of a [Facebook video](https://perma.cc/ZCF9-WZUG) shared on August 27, 2026.

The video, which appears to have been filmed from an elevated vantage point overlooking a valley, shows a river filled with tree trunks and logs rushing beneath a bridge.

The caption adds: "17 Malaysians among hundreds missing after flash floods in Nepal. Floods caused by the overflow of the Bhote Koshi River swept away many villages and destroyed roads, buildings, and hydropower projects in the Rasuwagadhi–Timure area."

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/19e39fcf431540883039fc889b11bf79-en.jpeg?itok=UyRp8Lna)

Screenshot of the false post captured on September 2, 2026, with a red X added by AFP

The same footage was also used in similar [Facebook](https://perma.cc/9VWD-FR7A) and [TikTok](https://perma.cc/38RU-BWXY) posts in [multiple languages](https://perma.cc/ZS2L-ZS8D), including [Spanish](https://perma.cc/W7KB-D9ZJ) and [Bengali](https://perma.cc/WG95-HGWX), after a tsunami-like [glacial flood](https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/9/2/funerals-in-nepal-for-missing-a-week-after-deadly-floods-1254) ripped through a valley on the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, wiping out entire settlements ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7AYN-NGYG)).

Among the more than 1,200 people killed and nearly 4,800 missing are [scores of pilgrims](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260828-pilgrims-seeking-peace-caught-in-deadly-nepal-tibet-floods) who come to the Himalayas seeking spiritual renewal, drawn by Tibet's sacred, snow-capped Mount Kailash ([archived link](https://perma.cc/95UL-Q3H4)).

Thousands of devotees, including dozens from [Malaysia](https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1523907/families-cling-hope-51-malaysians-remain-unreachable-after-nepal), are reported to have made the pilgrimage this year and are among those listed as uncontactable following the disaster ([archived link](https://perma.cc/25NX-BLL7)).

The circulating video, however, was not filmed during the disaster.

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared video led to the same footage that was published in an [X post](https://x.com/gohimachal_/status/1961452121401987436?s=46&t=sl_FYSMkcnclkYVQoneaDg) on August 29, 2025 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/XKS9-NXN6)).

Its caption indicates it shows the logs in the Ravi River in the town of Chamba, in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh.

Local media [reported](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/shimla/floating-logs-in-ravi-stir-buzz-officials-say-its-just-driftwood-uprooted-trees/articleshow/123654366.cms) a "heavy cloudburst and flash flood" in the upper catchment areas of Chamba between August 24 and August 26, 2025, which led to extensive flooding ([archived link](https://perma.cc/XDQ8-GL7X)).

The Ravi River's swollen currents caused [extensive damage](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1081891437347351), carrying away logs, debris and property along the riverbank ([archived link](https://perma.cc/XTS9-TV9E)). Officials said the rising waters had also damaged several houses and bridges in Chamba and adjoining areas.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/4ca6f820fb107193962fb9ad5051f86d-en.jpeg?itok=Ew0Y939J)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (L) and the August 2025 X clip

The footage matches imagery of the Shitla Bridge in Chamba available on [Google Maps](https://maps.app.goo.gl/KrbyQ28U3S1JD5657) ([archived link](https://perma.cc/6HQQ-9ZKQ?type=image)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/7f32f822e76ae84ba696b22717b5a30e-en.jpeg?itok=9yietRbT)

Screenshot comparison of the X video (L) and the photo shared on Google Maps, with matching elements highlighted by AFP

# Old Clip of Fish Flopping Around in Georgia Falsely Linked to Chennai Floods

## This video dates back to 2018 and is from Tbilisi, Georgia.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video showing several [fish](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/fish-video-old-from-us-doesnt-show-beas-near-manali-fact-check) flopping and wriggling around on the floor of a [supermarket](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/flooding-videos-subway-supermarket-not-from-new-york-united-states-fact-check) is being linked to [Chennai floods](https://www.thequint.com/quintlab/chennai-rain-floods-parched-climate-change/).

***(You can view archives of similar claims [here](https://perma.cc/T86M-H3PN) and [here](https://perma.cc/43YK-5EZH).)***

**What's the truth?:** This video is being falsely linked to Chennai floods.

* It dates back to 2018 and is from a supermarket located in Tbilisi, Georgia.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find out the truth?:** We performed a reverse image search on some of the keyframes of the viral video and this led us to a [YouTube video.](https://perma.cc/4XDR-EBME)

* This was shared by a channel named 'ViralHog' on **5 February 2018.**
* According to the description of the video, this incident happened in Georgia.

* Further, we came across news reports by *[Mirror](https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/dozens-live-fish-left-flopping-12008160)*and *[Daily Mail](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-5380435/Aisle-Fish-wriggle-flap-supermarket.html)* from 11 and 12 February 2018, respectively.
* Both reports carried the same video and stated that an aquarium tank shattered in a supermarket named Carrefour in Tbilisi, Georgia.
* Following which, several fish from the tank fell out on the ground and wriggled around in shallow water.

**More about Chennai [floods](https://www.thequint.com/explainers/cyclone-michaung-bay-of-bengal-hotbed-storms-explained):** Cyclone [Michaung](https://www.thequint.com/videos/news-videos/cyclone-michaung-andhra-pradesh-heavy-rain-chennai-deaths) is the latest cyclone to have struck the Bay of Bengal, wreaking havoc in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh since since 4 December.

* At least 12 people are said to have died in Chennai, amid heavy rainfall induced by the cyclone.
* According to the state government, Tamil Nadu witnessed three months of rain within just two days.

**Conclusion:** An old video showing several fish wriggling around in a Georgian supermarket is being falsely linked to the recent floods in Chennai.

# Old Video From Chennai Falsely Shared as Recent Visuals of Mumbai Airport’s T2

## The visuals date back to December 2023 and show Chennai Airport.

[Aishwarya Varma](/author/1562223/aishwarya-varma)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Aa

Aa

Small

Aa

Medium

Aa

Large

A video showing a waterlogged runway with people surrounding the front wheel of an [aeroplane](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/bangladesh-video-falsely-shared-as-bihar-teen-building-plane-fact-check) is being widely shared on social media, where users have claimed that it shows visuals from Terminal 2 of [Mumbai](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/monsoon-in-mumbai-is-infrastructure-failure-on-loop) [Airport](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/delhi-airport-monsoon-submerged-water-fact-check).

* The claim comes against the backdrop of the city seeing torrential downpour, with the Meteorological Department issuing a 'red alert' for Mumbai from 18-20 August.

***(Archived versions of more posts sharing this claim can be seen [here](https://archive.ph/rAHqE), [here](https://archive.ph/n9Zkd), [here](https://archive.is/HxlFp), and [here](https://archive.ph/Iz0F6).)***

**Is it true?:** No, the claim is false as the video is old.

* It shows the condition of Chennai Airport in December 2023, when Cyclone Michaung impacted parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**How did we find this out?:** A simple reverse image search on the video using Google Lens led us to news reports from **December 2023**.

* This report by *[The New Indian Express](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/tamil-nadu/2023/Dec/05/cyclone-michaung-chennai-airport-resumes-operations-after-shutdown-on-monday-2638821.html)*, dated 5 December 2023, carried a screenshot of the viral video, with the caption that it showed visuals from Chennai Airport due to "incessant rains" triggered by Cyclone Michaung.

* It noted that the cyclone had inundated Chennai Airport's runway, causing operations to be shut down for a full day.
* Other reports by *[The Telegraph](https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/chennai-airfield-open-after-rains-airlines-intimated-airport-officials/cid/1984700#goog_rewarded), [South First](https://thesouthfirst.com/pti/several-flights-cancelled-diverted-from-chennai-to-bengaluru-due-to-cyclone-michaung-impact/),* and *[Moneycontrol](https://hindi.moneycontrol.com/news/photos/india/trends/cyclone-michaung-water-logged-chennai-airport-see-the-devastationg-images-1638561-3.html)* about Cyclone Michaung's impact on Chennai Airport also included screengrabs from this video.
* The clip was also uploaded by *The Times of India* on their YouTube channel.

**Was Mumbai Airport flooded?:** Amid heavy rainfall, Mumbai Airport's T2, which is called the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, saw several delays and diversions, as per *[The Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/heavy-rains-disrupt-flights-at-mumbai-airport/articleshow/123414055.cms?from=mdr).*

* While rains and low visibility hindered operations, there were no credible reports about runways being flooded or operations stopping.
* In light of the red alert, the airport's official X account issued a passenger advisory, telling people to "check their flight status" and "allow extra travel time to reach the airport."

> In view of the heavy rain forecast in Mumbai, passengers are advised to check their flight status with their respective airlines and allow extra travel time to reach the airport.[#CSMIA](https://twitter.com/hashtag/CSMIA?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#PassengerAdvisory](https://twitter.com/hashtag/PassengerAdvisory?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#MumbaiAirport](https://twitter.com/hashtag/MumbaiAirport?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#WeatherUpdate](https://twitter.com/hashtag/WeatherUpdate?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/AILp023cun](https://t.co/AILp023cun)
>
> — Mumbai Airport (@CSMIA\_Official) [August 18, 2025](https://twitter.com/CSMIA_Official/status/1957321528955019477?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Airlines such as [IndiGo](https://x.com/IndiGo6E/status/1957969684914917693), [SpiceJet](https://x.com/flyspicejet/status/1957890472837591249), [Air India](https://x.com/airindia/status/1957694969591841225), and [Akasa Air](https://x.com/AkasaAir/status/1958007188364095787) also issued similar notices for flyers.

**Conclusion:** An old video from Chennai is being shared to falsely claim that it shows recent visuals from Mumbai Airport.

# Digitally Altered Video Shared As Cyclone Biparjoy Off Gujarat Coast

Written By [Pankaj Menon](/author/pankaj-menon/1), Edited By Ruby Dhingra

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[News](/fact-check/news/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Jun 13, 2023

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/06/Cyclone-Biparjoy-off-Guajrat-coast.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## Claim

Video of Cyclone Biparjoy off Gujarat coast near Dwarka

Newschecker received the claim on our WhatsApp tipline (+91-9999499044) to be fact checked.

![Digitally Altered Video From 2022 Shared As Cyclone Biparjoy Off Gujarat Coast Near Dwarka](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/06/Cyclone-Biparjoy-WA-request.jpg)

Screengrab of video shared with Newschecker on our WhatsApp tipline requesting it to be fact checked

**Also Read: [Adipurush Screening: Seat Next To Lord Hanuman To Cost Double?](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/adipurush-screening-seat-next-to-lord-hanuman-to-cost-double)**

## Fact

Newschecker began by carefully analysing the footage claiming to show cyclone Biparjoy off the Gujarat coast near Dwaraka and noticed that the tornado appears to be edited into the video.

This was confirmed by the observation that the sea in the viral video appears to be calm and placid, while the tornado, with raging winds, is seen really close. This would have ideally caused huge waves, and a disturbed surface of the sea, as opposed to how it can be seen in the video.

We then conducted a reverse image search on the keyframes of the video which led us to a YouTube post by channel @rtsarovvideo that posts real and edited footages of extreme weather events.

The video was posted in August 2022. This helps us to infer that the video is neither recent and is most likely edited. Hence the claim made is false.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2023/06/iNTRO-TO-rs-VIDEOS.jpg)

Screengrab of the description of the YouTube page stating that they post both real and edited videos of extreme weather events

We also reached out to the creator of the page for further clarification. Rostyslav Tsarov, the creator of the page confirmed that the video was not that of cyclone Biparjoy. “This video was created by me using CGI and I am the owner of this video. It is edited and it is not Cyclone Biparjoy,” he told Newschecker.

**Also Read: [Old Video Of Tree Swaying Fiercely Falsely Linked To Cyclone Biparjoy](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/old-video-of-tree-swaying-fiercely-falsely-linked-to-cyclone-biparjoy)**

## **Result: Altered Media**

# Old, Unrelated Videos Falsely Linked To Nepal Flash Floods

## BOOM found that the videos are unrelated to the flash flood that hit Nepal on August 26, 2026.

By -  [Srijit Das](/srijit-das) 

Published -

[![Boomlive](https://www.boomlive.in/h-upload/2026/10/08/1058459-google.webp)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=boomlive.in)

Listen to this Article

As Nepal grapples with the devastating impact of flash floods, a wave of old and unrelated visuals has surfaced on social media, falsely claiming to show the disaster that struck the country on August 26, 2026.

BOOM found that the videos, which have garnered millions of views online, actually depict different incidents and were recorded before the disaster struck Nepal.

Massive landslides and flash floods struck the Nepal-Tibet border on the morning of August 26, causing widespread destruction across the Himalayan region. Official figures state that hundreds of people, including Indian tourists, went missing and several were killed in the incident. Rescue operations are currently underway in the affected areas, amid fears of another flood following China's warning of a [possible lake outburst](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd948kn02e5o).

While several videos showing the unfolding disaster are being shared on social media, BOOM found that the videos below went viral with false claims that they were from Nepal, when they actually depict different incidents.

**Claim 1: Video captures the moment a flash flood swept through Nepal**

When we performed a reverse search on a keyframe from the [video claimed to show the Nepal disaster](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1574705387436469), we found several news reports from 2025 identifying the footage as visuals of the flash floods that hit Uttarkashi in August 2025. The Times of India [reported](https://www.instagram.com/p/DM-HSFMSxmk/) on the video, stating that the flash flood, triggered by a cloudburst in the upper catchment area of the Kheer Ganga river, caused large-scale destruction in Dharali village in Uttarkashi district on August 5, 2025.

Another video report by The Indian Express covering the incident can be seen below.

**Claim 2: Video recorded from a Chinese helicopter shows the site where a glacier broke, causing destruction in Nepal**

> Shocking scary but fascinating video from Chinese.   
> \*The Chinese helicopter reached the place where the glacier was broken and the water that came out of it caused a lot of destruction in Nepal. This phenomenon is called GLOF!\*  
>   
>  \*A glacial lake outburst flood can occur when the… [pic.twitter.com/703nBWc8Qg](https://t.co/703nBWc8Qg)
>
> — Ratan Sharda 🇮🇳 रतन शारदा (@RatanSharda55) [August 27, 2026](https://x.com/RatanSharda55/status/2092998101305016578?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Several users shared a video recorded from a helicopter showing an aerial view of a broken glacier, falsely claiming that it captured the cause of the Nepal disaster on August 26. ABP News also [published a report](https://archive.is/IfIzG) based on the same claim. However, BOOM traced the video to the Instagram profile of commercial helicopter pilot Leigh Coates, who [shared](https://archive.is/4aS2n) it on August 22, 2026.

Coates said the video captures a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) at Columbia Glacier in Alaska. She added that the phenomenon has been occurring annually since 2014.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcUFQZhvGzS/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
>
> [A post shared by Leigh Coates (@helipilotleigh)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcUFQZhvGzS/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

**Claim 3: Video captured by a Chinese man shows the moments when a flash flood struck Tibet and Nepal**

> A man from China recorded the frightening moments as a flash flood struck Tibet and Nepal, showing the sheer force and speed of the rushing water [pic.twitter.com/z7BPKPaeIv](https://t.co/z7BPKPaeIv)
>
> — Surajit (@surajit\_ghosh2) [August 26, 2026](https://x.com/surajit_ghosh2/status/2092633696939733473?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

When we searched for the video, we found that news agency ANI’s UP and Uttarakhand X handle had posted the same video on August 10, 2026. The report stated that the video shows a sudden flash flood in Chamoli’s Niti Valley, where strong currents swept away the Valley Bridge, along with a dozer and a vehicle, near Tamak Valley on the Niti-Malari road.

The video was credited to Chamoli Police.

> [#WATCH](https://x.com/hashtag/WATCH?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) | Uttarakhand: Tamak drain in Chamoli’s border area of Niti Valley witnessed a sudden flash flood today, with a strong current sweeping away the Valley Bridge, along with a dozer and a vehicle, near Tamak Valley on the Niti-Malari road.  
>   
> (Source: Chamoli Police) <https://t.co/j86HPpA116> [pic.twitter.com/eMMbop035P](https://t.co/eMMbop035P)
>
> — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) [August 10, 2026](https://x.com/ANINewsUP/status/2086817688001871924?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

# Uttarkashi Cloudburst: Old Video of Men Being Rescued From Flooded River In Himachal Falsely Shared as Dharali

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1), Edited By Pankaj Menon

[Fact Check](/fact-check/1)[News](/fact-check/news/1)[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

Aug 7, 2025

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/08/New-Cover-Vausdha-64.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

## Claim

![image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/main/img/cross.svg?quality=71&format=webp&w=64)

Video showing individuals being rescued from an overflowing river in Uttarkashi’s Dharali amid recent flash floods.

## Fact

![image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/main/img/tick.svg?quality=71&format=webp&w=64)

Old video from Himachal Pradesh's Solan shared in a false context.

A video showing a group of men using ropes to rescue youths stranded in the middle of a raging river is being widely shared on social media platforms, with several users linking it to the recent flash floods in Uttarakhand’s Uttarkashi district following a cloudburst on Tuesday (August 5, 2025).  
  
Multiple X, Facebook and YouTube users shared the over-two-minute-long-footage with a Hindi text overlay reading, “New video of Dharali village.”

Newschecker’s investigation, however, revealed that the video was not related to the recent Uttarkashi cloudburst.

![Uttarkashi Cloudburst: Old Video of Men Being Rescued From Flooded River In Himachal Falsely Shared as Dharali](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/08/d1.jpg)

Screengrab from X post by @anitaklab

Such posts can be seen [**here**](https://archive.ph/xbRfE), [**here**](https://archive.ph/bJaS4) and [**here**](https://archive.ph/FPSpy).

**Also Read: [Viral Image Showing Aftermath Of Uttarkashi Cloudburst Is AI Generated](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/viral-image-showing-aftermath-of-uttarkashi-cloudburst-ai-generated)**

### **Rescue & Relief Work In Uttarkashi**

The NDRF, SDRF, Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), police and other related agencies are involved in the relief and rescue work in [**Uttarkashi**](https://www.thehindu.com/elections/uttarakhand-assembly/uttarakhand-uttarkashi-cloudburst-flash-flood-rescue-operation-live-updates-august-7-2025/article69904013.ece) district hit by flash floods. The teams rescued 190 people from Dharali on Wednesday (August 6, 2025) and around 65  others have been airlifted to Matli so far on Thursday (August 7, 2025). Visuals from the rescue operations can be seen [**here**](https://x.com/uksdrf/status/1953026949569487096), [**here**](https://x.com/uttarakhandcops/status/1953045483263275249) and [**here**](https://x.com/uttarakhandcops/status/1953071070275412406).

## Fact Check/Verification

A reverse image search on the keyframes of the viral clip led us to a report by [**The Indian Express**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gG8y--iMl04), dated July 29, 2022, detailing an incident in Himachal Pradesh’s Solan where five youths were rescued by locals after they were trapped in the river in Nalagarh. The report featured snippets of the viral footage, confirming that it was unrelated to the recent calamity in Uttarkashi.

![Uttarkashi Cloudburst: Old Video of Men Being Rescued From Flooded River In Himachal Falsely Shared as Dharali](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2025/08/d2.jpg)

Screengrab from YouTube video by The Indian Express

Another report by [**The Tribune**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBLVrGHbJAc), published on July 29, 2022, also carried visuals showing the same incident, corroborated that it shows the rescue of the youths who were stuck in a river in Solan’s Nalagarh, adding that they had gone into the river to take photos.

**Also Read:[PM Modi-Led Govt Offering ₹5,000 I-Day Cash Gifts To Citizens? No, Viral Link Is A Scam](https://newschecker.in/fact-check/pm-modi-led-govt-offering-%e2%82%b95000-i-day-cash-gifts-to-citizens-no-viral-link-is-a-scam)**

Detailing the effects of incessant rainfall across states, an [**Aaj Tak**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X6tqMkl5mQc) report from July 2022, too, featured the snippets from the now viral footage to show locals rescuing youths stuck in a river in Himachal Pradesh’s Solan.

Screengrab from YouTube video by Aaj Tak

The **[Uttarakhand Police](https://x.com/uttarakhandcops/status/1952998484430471622/photo/1)** also flagged the viral clip, clarifying that it was unrelated to the recent disaster in Dharali.

## Conclusion

Hence, we find that the viral posts, claiming to show the rescue of men stranded in a river in Dharali following the recent cloudburst, are false.

# A 2022 flood rescue video from Himachal Pradesh is falsely shared as from the recent Uttarkashi cloudburst

![Murshid M](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/2b5d3083d5fe47f4d0fb287cddce5f7a6c44a7ce911a1556e93aae85def15b6e?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Murshid M](https://factly.in/author/murshid-m/ "Posts by Murshid M")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/a-2022-flood-rescue-video-from-himachal-pradesh-is-falsely-shared-as-from-the-recent-uttarkashi-cloudburst/#respond)3 Mins Read

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-2022-flood-rescue-video-from-himachal-pradesh-is-falsely-shared-as-from-the-recent-uttarkashi-cloudburst%2F "Share on Facebook")   [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-2022-flood-rescue-video-from-himachal-pradesh-is-falsely-shared-as-from-the-recent-uttarkashi-cloudburst%2F&text=A%202022%20flood%20rescue%20video%20from%20Himachal%20Pradesh%20is%20falsely%20shared%20as%20from%20the%20recent%20Uttarkashi%20cloudburst "Share on X (Twitter)")   [Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-2022-flood-rescue-video-from-himachal-pradesh-is-falsely-shared-as-from-the-recent-uttarkashi-cloudburst%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F%2F2025%2F08%2FRescue-video-from-Uttarkashi-Thumbnail-scaled.jpg&description=A%202022%20flood%20rescue%20video%20from%20Himachal%20Pradesh%20is%20falsely%20shared%20as%20from%20the%20recent%20Uttarkashi%20cloudburst "Share on Pinterest")   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-2022-flood-rescue-video-from-himachal-pradesh-is-falsely-shared-as-from-the-recent-uttarkashi-cloudburst%2F "Share on LinkedIn")   [Tumblr](https://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-2022-flood-rescue-video-from-himachal-pradesh-is-falsely-shared-as-from-the-recent-uttarkashi-cloudburst%2F&name=A%202022%20flood%20rescue%20video%20from%20Himachal%20Pradesh%20is%20falsely%20shared%20as%20from%20the%20recent%20Uttarkashi%20cloudburst "Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

The recent cloudburst in Uttarakhand’s Uttarkashi district on 05 August 2025 triggered severe flash floods, particularly in Dharali village. The intense and sudden rainfall caused rivers like the Kheer Ganga to overflow, leading to large-scale destruction of homes and infrastructure. At least five people lost their lives, several remain missing, and around 190 people have been rescued so far ([here](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/uttarakhand-flash-floods-live-updates-himachal-pradesh-uttarkashi-cloudburst-deaths-rescue-operations-latest-news-9027948), [here](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/uttarakhand-cloudburst-uttarkashi-flash-floods-missing-dead-damage-rescue-2766598-2025-08-05), and [here](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttarakhand/uttarakhand-uttarkashi-cloudburst-flash-floods-highlights-august-6-2025/article69896766.ece)).

In this context, a video ([here](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1411184333326320), [here](https://x.com/PRABHATROY22/status/1953192508957331568) and [here](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Uly-XbejfpA)) is going viral on social media showing a few people stranded in the middle of fast-flowing water being rescued. It is being widely shared with the claim that it shows scenes from the recent Uttarkashi cloudburst. Let’s verify the truth behind this video.

> **Claim**: The viral video shows people being rescued during the recent August 2025 Uttarkashi cloudburst.
>
> **Fact**: The video is unrelated to the Uttarkashi cloudburst. It shows a 2022 incident from Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh, where five youths were trapped in the Chikli river while taking selfies during a flash flood. The Uttarakhand Police also clarified that the video has no connection to the Dharali disaster. Hence the claim is **FASLE**.

To verify the truth, we performed a reverse image search on Google, which led us to the same video uploaded by [The Indian Express](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gG8y--iMl04) on their YouTube channel on 29 July 2022. The video was titled, “*Nalagarh: Five Migrants Land In River To Take Photo, Stuck In Flash Flood Due To Heavy Rains*.”

According to the description, the incident occurred in Nalagarh, Solan district, Himachal Pradesh. Due to heavy rains, rivers in the area were in full spate. On that day, five youths entered the Chikli River to take a selfie when a sudden flash flood struck. They clung to rocks in the middle of the river to save themselves. Locals, upon noticing the situation, launched a rescue operation and eventually pulled them out using ropes.

Several media outlets also reported on the same incident shown in the viral video, some using the original footage and others using still images ([here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBLVrGHbJAc), [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D3KfLuafYbU), and [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fJiPBbq_n_w)). The Uttarakhand Police issued a clarification on 06 August 2025, through their official X handle, [stating](https://x.com/uttarakhandcops/status/1952998484430471622) that the viral video being linked to the recent Harshil, Dharali disaster is completely false and misleading, and urged the public not to spread confusion by sharing such misinformation.

> [#FactCheck](https://x.com/hashtag/FactCheck?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)  
>   
> सोशल मीडिया पर उक्त वीडियो को कुछ लोगों द्वारा प्रसारित कर हर्षिल, धराली आपदा से जोड़ा जा रहा है, जो कि पूर्णतः असत्य व भ्रामक है। वीडियो का धराली आपदा से कोई सम्बन्ध नहीं है।   
> कृपया सोशल मीडिया पर गलत जानकारी डालकर भ्रम न फैलाएं । [pic.twitter.com/kDyd7E2sxb](https://t.co/kDyd7E2sxb)
>
> — Uttarakhand Police (@uttarakhandcops) [August 6, 2025](https://x.com/uttarakhandcops/status/1952998484430471622?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

While the rescue operations are still ongoing in Uttarkashi, with efforts continuing across the affected regions, including Dharali, where advanced equipment like ground-penetrating radars and sniffer dogs are being used to locate the missing  ([here](https://www.thehindu.com/elections/uttarakhand-assembly/uttarakhand-uttarkashi-cloudburst-flash-flood-rescue-operation-highlights-august-7-2025/article69904013.ece) and [here](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c78zjd8xj2xo)), the viral video has no connection to the recent Uttarkashi cloudburst.

To sum up, an old video of a flood rescue in Himachal Pradesh is falsely shared as footage from the recent Uttarkashi cloudburst in Uttarakhand.

# Nepal floods: Unrelated videos of past disasters, AI visuals falsely viral

Alt News found that several widely shared videos and compilation clips claiming to show the August 26 flash floods in Nepal are either old footage from other disasters from different parts of the world or even AI-generated

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/a4a0477ebec4d5590fdb727dbcaa04b3cec9f6db79e9eea09829393dcc4032a6?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/prantikali/)

[Prantik Ali](https://www.altnews.in/author/prantikali/)

 ![Nepal floods: Unrelated videos of past disasters, AI visuals falsely viral](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Copy-of-FI-Kit-2026-08-31T210438.215-1024x536.png) 

A devastating flash flood on Wednesday, August 26, near the Nepal-Tibet border, resulted in massive destruction in several districts of Nepal, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Gorkha, with over [700 dead](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/nepal-flash-floods-live-updates-death-toll-rescue-operation-missing-person-tibet-border-glacier-collapse-news/article71406948.ece) and over 2,500 people still missing. [Reportedly](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/27/what-caused-the-catastrophic-flash-flood-in-nepal-and-tibet-and-how-does-a-glacier-collapse), a glacial landslide of ice and rock caused the flash floods, which destroyed homes roads, bridges and power plants.

In the days following the catastrophe, social media was rife with video clips showing the extent of devastation — from gigantic waves of floodwater gushing through entire villages, to buildings collapsing, and people being swept away under the debris.

However, Alt News found that a large number of these videos circulating on social media were not authentic. Several of these videos were not from Nepal at all, but drawn from various other calamities which occurred across the world in the last few years.

#### Clip From 2025 Uttarakhand Floods

An X user, Said Ercan ([@saidercan](https://x.com/saidercan/status/2092720077468577799)), posted a compilation clip on August 27 showing the havoc wreaked by large flood waves. The first clip shows a torrential river flowing through a mountainous area, and eventually sweeping through the houses on the banks, destroying them in an instant. The post has garnered over 5.8 million views and been reshared over 5,000 times  at the time of publishing. ([Archive](https://archive.is/iOMbP))

To verify whether the video is of the Nepal floods, we broke it down into keyframes and ran a reverse image search. This led us to an Instagram post uploaded by [The Times of India](https://www.instagram.com/p/DM-HSFMSxmk/), on August 5, 2025, featuring the same footage.

> View this post on Instagram
>
> [A post shared by The Times of India (@timesofindia)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DM-HSFMSxmk/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

The caption states that the footage is of the Uttarakhand cloudburst havoc. “At least four people have died and many are feared missing after a devastating flash flood triggered by a cloudburst in the upper catchment area of the Kheer Ganga river caused large-scale destruction in Dharali village in Uttarkashi district…,” read the caption.

A [Dainik Bhaskar](https://www.bhaskarenglish.in/national/news/uncut-video-cloudburst-uttarakhand-debris-buries-dharali-village-on-riverbank-135613681.html) report also features the same video to show the scale of damage caused by the cloudburst in Uttarkashi. We ran relevant keyword searches, and found news reports from sources like [Reuters](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/india-flood-in-kheerganga-river-in-uttarkashi-district-of-uttarakhand-after-cloudburst/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX09XU0hCQzEwNjUxMDg), [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c87eyx1v039o), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/6/indian-village-swallowed-by-mudslide-what-happened-and-why), [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttarakhand/uttarakhand-uttarkashi-cloudburst-flash-floods-highlights-august-6-2025/article69896766.ece), and others, that corroborated this finding. Thus, the video footage shared by the X user is actually of the 2025 Uttarakhand flash floods, and not of the recent Nepal havoc.

#### AI-generated Clip

In another instance, X user Ayesha Khan ([@Ayesha0Khaan](https://x.com/Ayesha0Khaan/status/2092834184595443813)) posted a video clip, of huge waves sweeping away cars, building structures, and people. The clip received over 1 million views. ([Archive](https://archive.is/Y6Vjb))

X user Ravi Shankar Singh ([@Ravishanka34381](https://archive.is/cFwsc)) also posted the clip with the same claim. However, we noticed some discrepancies in the video — for instance, around the 0:05 timestamp, a tree log appears out of nowhere in the debris flowing through the floodwater, indicating that the clip could be AI-generated.

We ran the video through [Hive’s AI detection tool](https://hivemoderation.com/ai-generated-content-detection), which confirmed our suspicion, showing a 99.9% possibility of the video containing AI-generated content.

#### Clip From 2024 China Incident

News outlet Medya Post ([@medya\_post](https://x.com/medya_post/status/2092902851269824874)) uploaded a clip on X, which showed around 15 people getting swept away by powerful flood waves. The caption stated: “Tourists who wanted to take videos and photos during the flood disaster that occurred in Nepal were swept away by the current and disappeared.” The post had seen massive traction on social media, with over 1.5 million views. ([Archive](https://archive.is/EYOiF)) 

Two other X users with the handles ([@JMNewsNetwork\_](https://archive.is/s3nyW#selection-195.0-195.15)) and ([@redpillmd](https://archive.is/1cfkz)) had uploaded the same video, with the former having deleted it after it had been viewed over 45,000 times.

To verify the clip’s authencity, we ran a reverse image search, which led us to an X post, originally uploaded by an user with the handle ([@Arab\_Storms](https://x.com/Arab_Storms/status/1832699678208459068/)) on September 8, 2024. 

> التصوير اصبح اهم من الحياة [#شاهد](https://x.com/hashtag/%D8%B4%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%AF?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) ❗️[#الصين](https://x.com/hashtag/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%8A%D9%86?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) جرف المد القوي لنهر تشيانتانج العديد من الزوار الذين كانوا يحاولون التقاط صورة ،،،[#Yagi](https://x.com/hashtag/Yagi?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/bdiEj7fk9b](https://t.co/bdiEj7fk9b)
>
> — طقس\_العالم ⚡️ (@Arab\_Storms) [September 8, 2024](https://x.com/Arab_Storms/status/1832699678208459068?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

According to the caption, the video had been taken in China, showing the powerful waves of the Qiantang River overpowering tourists on the shore who were clicking photos. The incident, which occured in the days following Asia’s most powerful storm in 2024, the Super Typhoon Yagi, had also been reported on by [The Indian Express](https://indianexpress.com/article/trending/trending-globally/china-qiantang-river-tourists-being-swept-away-while-taking-selfies-super-typhoon-yagi-viral-video-9557691/), and [Newsflare](https://www.newsflare.com/video/680428/tidal-bore-ripped-phones-out-of-tourists-hands-as-they-watch-from-river-banks-in-china).

#### Video From West Bengal Landslide

A news outlet TNT Media ([@TNT\_Media1](https://x.com/TNT_Media1/status/2092715499004289094)) posted a clip which showed a mudslide from a vantage point. It also features the narrow escape of some vehicles and people gathered at the spot. The caption, written in Arabic, claims that horrifying scenes correspond to the recent Nepal flash floods. ([Archive](https://archive.is/FqPTD)) 

> مشاهد مروعة من نيبال.. 😯😯 [pic.twitter.com/N7f5jBl4i6](https://t.co/N7f5jBl4i6)
>
> — 𝐓𝐍𝐓 (@TNT\_Media1) [August 26, 2026](https://x.com/TNT_Media1/status/2092715499004289094?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

We noticed that the car, visible in parts of the video, bears a number plate whose state code (WB) corresponds with that of West Bengal. Moreover, the recorder of the video, while shooting the clip, speaks in Bengali to warn people to get away from the waves.

A reverse image search on several keyframes of the video led us to [this X post](https://x.com/TheDailyJagran/status/2089340271117127832), uploaded by The Daily Jagran on August 17.

> A biker had a narrow escape after a massive landslide struck the Bindu area of West Bengal’s Kalimpong district. Huge rocks, soil and debris suddenly came crashing onto the road as vehicles passed through.[#Kalimpong](https://x.com/hashtag/Kalimpong?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Landslide](https://x.com/hashtag/Landslide?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#WestBengal](https://x.com/hashtag/WestBengal?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Biker](https://x.com/hashtag/Biker?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#ViralVideo](https://x.com/hashtag/ViralVideo?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Monsoon](https://x.com/hashtag/Monsoon?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/HgFLY7Dhjy](https://t.co/HgFLY7Dhjy)
>
> — The Daily Jagran (@TheDailyJagran) [August 17, 2026](https://x.com/TheDailyJagran/status/2089340271117127832?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The caption states that the video shows a landslide in the Bindu area of West Bengal’s Kalimpong district, thereby proving that this video clip is not related to the Nepal flash floods.

#### Compilation Clip From Various Calamities

An X user named “Leonard Sardua $TOR” ([@lsardua](https://x.com/lsardua/status/2093019047382098031)) posted a compilation of clips showing structures collapsing under the deluge, claiming they showed the devastation caused by the flash flood in Nepal. The clip garnered over 3.3 million views and 3,700 reshares. ([Archive](https://archive.is/47WTA))

Two more users, “HadY Azmy” ([@HadYAzmy1](https://archive.is/20H10)) and Ahmad Ansari ([@Ahmadansari2233](https://x.com/Ahmadansari2233/status/2092793193339453860)), amplified the same clip on August 27. The former video, which has now been deleted, had garnered over than 2.5 million views and over 3,000 reshares. 

On running a reverse image search on one keyframe from the viral clip, we were led to an article published by [The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/srinagar/j-k-floods-terrifying-video-shows-shopping-complex-swallowed-by-raging-floodwaters-near-kashmir/articleshow/132540535.cms) on July 21. The report shows the same building structure collapse under the force of floodwater, and states that the video was from the Budgam district of Jammu and Kashmir.

![](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Screenshot_54.jpg)

Another segment of the compilation shows a red building being engulfed by the gushing floodwater, sweeping away cars and other structures amid the debris.

Running a reverse image search on this keyframe, we found that the clip could be traced back to a mudslide in Japan’s Atami city from July 2021. An X user with the handle [@d\_t\_dcg\_sdh](https://x.com/d_t_dcg_sdh/status/1411176638277033988) had uploaded several clips showing the mudslide sweeping away houses and vehicles. We also found news reports from [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/3/japan-torrential-rains-unleash-landslides-20-missing-report) and Spanish news outlet [La Nacion](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/el-mundo/video-el-impactante-alud-de-barro-en-japon-que-dejo-dos-muertos-y-al-menos-20-desaparecidos-nid03072021/), corroborating that the clip was recorded during a mudslide in Japan in 2021.

This slideshow requires JavaScript.

The same compilation video also included a segment which showed a bridge being torn down by the raging floodwater.

This, we found, was in fact from an incident in Indonesia, showing the collapse of the wooden Molintogupo Bridge, owing to the overflowing of the Bone River. [A video uploaded by Newsflare on Dailymotion](https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x7ufni4), notes that the incident occurred on June 11, 2020. It was also reported on by [VGTV](https://tv.vg.no/nyheter/her-raser-broen-i-vannmassene?id=198386).

Another segment of the same clip shows two men watching a bridge being dismantled and swept away by floodwater.

We found that this video was from Argentina. A reverse image search on a keyframe led us to [this X post by AccuWeather](https://x.com/accuweather/status/1740029286801920509) on December 25, 2023, which shows a bridge in Argentina’s Catamarca being blown away by the turbulent floodwater.

> A bridge was swept away in Catamarca, Argentina, on Christmas Day, leaving a city completely isolated. ⁣ [pic.twitter.com/hVdwxmQ7QU](https://t.co/hVdwxmQ7QU)
>
> — AccuWeather (@accuweather) [December 27, 2023](https://x.com/accuweather/status/1740029286801920509?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Another video, showing a white car being dragged along by the torrential flow of mud water, was also part of this compilation.

This, Alt News found, was originally from Islamabad, in Pakistan, dating back to a devastating [flood](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/7/22/rains-flash-floods-kill-21-in-pakistan-tourists-rescued-in-hilly-north1&_rdr#) that took place in July 2025.

Similarly, a segment showing a woman overlooking a building structure being swept away by flood water, was also part of this compilation, alleging that it was from Nepal.

A reverse image search proved that the image has existed on X since at least [September 2024](https://x.com/MattWallace888/status/1840107271520694464). On further investigation, we [found](https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/government-making-hurricanes-conspiracy-theory) that it showed the damage caused by Hurricane Helene in  North Carolina, United States.

> Don’t worry guys, weather modification isn’t real! It’s just a coincidence that Hurricane Helene is one of the most devastating “inland damage storms” in history and that hundreds of pro-Trump counties are being massively impacted during the most important election of our… [pic.twitter.com/lyi8YZXB8A](https://t.co/lyi8YZXB8A)
>
> — Matt Wallace (@MattWallace888) [September 28, 2024](https://x.com/MattWallace888/status/1840107271520694464?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Another clip showing a submerged bus making its way through the floodwater was also featured in the compilation.

We found that this video was shot during a downpour in Pakistan’s Karachi, which left the city flooded and resulted in at least 16 deaths. Pakistani news media outlet [24 News HD, in their report on the flood](https://www.24newshd.tv/19-Mar-2026/rain-emergency-declared-karachi-downpour-storm-leaves-19-dead) dated March 19, used the same clip of the submerged bus.

Thus, the compilation clip uploaded by users “Leonard Sardua $TOR”, “HadY Azmy”, and Ahmad Ansari, with the claim that the footage depicts the havoc in Nepal is fake and misleading. The entire compilation stitches together footage from real calamities, occuring in various other parts of the world in the past few years, to wrongly claim that they are visuals from the Nepal flash floods on August 26.

# Old and unrelated videos are falsely being attributed to the 2024 Assam floods.

![Varun Borugadda](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/77de1408da09a7ec42c70d3d2369e35e27bae0863030d0f1c34b04f3ddce91e2?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Varun Borugadda](https://factly.in/author/varun-borugadda/ "Posts by Varun Borugadda")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/old-and-unrelated-videos-are-falsely-being-attributed-to-the-2024-assam-floods/#respond)3 Mins Read

"Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

In the wake of the recent (July 2024) devastating floods in Assam ([here](https://www.telegraphindia.com/north-east/assam-flood-situation-continues-to-improve-significantly/cid/2033785) and [here](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/3-more-deaths-take-assam-floods-toll-to-96/articleshow/111766560.cms)), a [video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1852037095288972) containing two clips allegedly related to the floods has gone viral. The first clip in this video features a bridge collapsing and washing away in flood water, and the second one shows a flooded railway track with a train getting toppled by the water. We fact-check this claim through this article.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2024/07/Assam-Flood-videos-Claim--577x1024.jpg)

An archived version of this can be seen [here](https://perma.cc/3S36-9H6Z).

> **Claim:** These video clips show the devastating effect the 2024 Assam floods on a bridge and a parked train.
>
> **Fact:** Both video clips are old and unrelated to the 2024 Assam floods. The bridge collapse video was filmed in Indonesia in April 2021 during a flood in the Kambaniru River. The second clip featuring a train getting overturned by flood water was filmed in 2022 at the New Haflong Railway Station in the Dima Hasao district of Assam. Hence, the claim made in the post is **False**.

To check the veracity of the [viral claim,](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1852037095288972) we performed a reverse image search on a few of the first clips’ keyframes, leading us to a [2021 news report](https://news-indozone-id.translate.goog/news/911535321/banjir-bandang-terjang-ntt-jembatan-bersejarah-yang-diresmikan-jenderal-ahmad-yani-ambruk?_x_tr_sl=auto&_x_tr_tl=en&_x_tr_hl=en-US&_x_tr_pto=wapp) on the clip.

Reportedly, this was filmed in Indonesia. It shows a historical bridge named ‘Ahmad Yani Bridge’/ ‘Old Kambaniru Bridge’ collapsing due to a flash flood that occurred in the Kambaniru River. This incident occurred on 4 April 2021 in Indonesia’s East Sumba Regency, NTT.

A further search yielded news reports from [Tibunenews](https://youtu.be/GdjYm9cyujc?t=83) and [SBS News](https://twitter.com/SBSNews/status/1378911766046855168) from 2021, which also featured the [clip](https://youtu.be/GdjYm9cyujc?t=83) of ‘Old Kambaniru bridge’ collapsing and getting washed away by floodwaters.

> Video shows homes and bridges being swept away in Indonesia and East Timor as torrential rain brought landslides and floods to the region, leaving dozens dead. [pic.twitter.com/VlJ7Hl0oOb](https://t.co/VlJ7Hl0oOb)
>
> — SBS News (@SBSNews) [April 5, 2021](https://x.com/SBSNews/status/1378911766046855168?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

To learn details about the second clip in the [viral video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1852037095288972), we performed a reverse image search on a few of its keyframes online. This search led us to multiple social media posts ([here](https://twitter.com/HannanAhmed_/status/1526281037407391745), [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fevoZj3JGeY), and [here](https://youtu.be/ghcr9DFbUYY?t=29)) from 2022 that shared the same video clip. According to these posts, the video shows a flood situation in Assam’s ‘New Haflong Railway Station.’

https://twitter.com/HannanAhmed\_/status/1526281037407391745

We also found news reports ([here](https://www.india.com/news/india/assam-flood-news-today-passenger-train-in-haflong-station-topples-as-flash-flood-wreaks-havoc-in-assam-disturbing-visuals-emerge-watch-5399203/), [here](https://news.abplive.com/videos/news/india-assam-floods-wreck-havoc-at-new-haflong-railway-station-abp-news-ground-report-1532624), and [here](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/assam-floods-indian-railways-cancels-these-trains-till-end-of-next-month-full-list-11652933396867.html)) on this incident from May 2022.

As per the reports, the Haflong railway station in the Dima Hasao District was flooded with water due to heavy rainfall, which caused a train parked on the tracks to [topple](https://www.newsflare.com/video/494912/watch-devastating-videos-shows-passenger-train-toppled-at-haflong-railway-station-in-assam-flash-floods). This evidence makes it clear that the video clips featured in the viral video are old and unrelated to the 2024 Assam floods.

To sum up, the viral clips claiming to show the devastating effects of the 2024 Assam floods are old and unrelated to the recent floods.

# A staged video is falsely shared as showing the dead bodies of 2026 Assam flood victims

![Nitish Kumar Dhonge](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/aa25bd8a70a5f0525e72675022ac12d97edc4861706554b09fe2739a0fbce6af?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Nitish Kumar Dhonge](https://factly.in/author/nitish-kumar-dhonge/ "Posts by Nitish Kumar Dhonge")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/a-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims/#respond)2 Mins Read

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims%2F "Share on Facebook")   [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims%2F&text=A%20staged%20video%20is%20falsely%20shared%20as%20showing%20the%20dead%20bodies%20of%202026%20Assam%20flood%20victims "Share on X (Twitter)")   [Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F%2F2026%2F07%2FBodies-of-people-died-in-the-Assam-floods-Thumbnail-1.jpg&description=A%20staged%20video%20is%20falsely%20shared%20as%20showing%20the%20dead%20bodies%20of%202026%20Assam%20flood%20victims "Share on Pinterest")   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims%2F "Share on LinkedIn")   [Tumblr](https://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fa-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims%2F&name=A%20staged%20video%20is%20falsely%20shared%20as%20showing%20the%20dead%20bodies%20of%202026%20Assam%20flood%20victims "Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

The major flood wave in Assam began around 19–20 July 2026, following several days of heavy rainfall that caused rivers such as the Dikhow, Disang, and Dhansiri to overflow in Upper Assam. The flooding inundated villages, damaged infrastructure, disrupted transport across districts including Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, and Golaghat, and prompted extensive rescue and relief operations. As of 31 July 2026, official reports indicate that the floods have claimed 80 lives ([here](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/assam-floods-upper-assam-water-levels-himanta-biswa-sarma-evacuations-simalguri-trains-10796438/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), [here](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/guwahati/assam-flood-toll-rises-to-80-over-2-12-lakh-affected-kartik-aaryan-gives-rs-1-crore-relief-aid/articleshow/132746661.cms), [here](https://www.indiatodayne.in/assam/story/heavy-rain-inundates-guwahati-roads-localities-as-assam-floods-affect-over-17-lakh-people-1427073-2026-07-20), and [here](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/assam/2026/Jul/24/25-of-flood-hit-areas-in-assams-sivasagar-charaideo-inaccessible-cm-himanta-says-situation-dangerous)).

In this context, a video is being shared on social media ([here](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1012186845041304), [here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DbV8d7ZPT_d/), and [here](https://www.facebook.com/search/top/?q=%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%80%20%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%82%20%E0%A4%AC%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A2%E0%A4%BC%20%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%20%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%B5%20%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%82%20%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%80%20%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%20%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%88%20%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%B8-%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%B8%20%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%AE%20%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%87%20%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B2%20%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%88%20%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A4)) with the claim that it shows the dead bodies of victims of the 2026 Assam floods. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/07/Bodies-of-people-died-in-the-Assam-floods-Claim-873x1024.jpg)

The archived post can be found here.

> **Claim:** The video shows the dead bodies of people who died in the Assam floods.
>
> **Fact**: The video is staged and does not show a real incident. It is unrelated to the Assam floods and was uploaded by an Instagram creator named Simran SK on 03 July 2026, more than two weeks before the floods began in Assam. Hence, the claim made in the post is **Misleading.**

A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the [same video](https://www.instagram.com/p/DaVcoN2u698/) ([archived](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55121014?key=abe4c90c32ba5aa26b0bccec75eb96a6)) uploaded by Instagram creator Simran SK on 03 July 2026. According to reports ([here](https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-climate/assam-floods-2026-causes-explained-10802845/), [here](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqlx61p3wz0o)), the incessant rainfall that triggered the Assam floods began on 19 July 2026, more than two weeks after the video was uploaded. This clearly establishes that the video predates the Assam floods and is unrelated to the disaster.

Upon reviewing the [Instagram account](https://www.instagram.com/simransk944/), we found [another video](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dac5eVcqU9S/) ([archived](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55122130?key=b1fa10a02b94e0d711a383124c434e69)) showing similar visuals of people lying motionless on the ground as if they were dead bodies. In the [second part](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dap0shIKjfl/) ([archived](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55122101?key=05684e33f251eb4d42d2eb4147d5f9b0)) of the same video uploaded on the account, the same individuals seen acting as dead bodies in the first part can be seen getting up after it is announced that the video shoot is over. This clearly confirms that the scene was staged and created for entertainment purposes, not as footage of a real incident.

To sum up, a staged video is falsely shared as showing the dead bodies of 2026 Assam flood victims.

# Posts misrepresent old flooding footage as monsoon rains lash India

* This article is more than one year old.
* Published on June 19, 2025 at 05:07
* 2 min read
* By [Sachin BAGHEL](https://factcheck.afp.com/sachin-baghel),  [AFP India](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-india)

As torrential monsoon rains in India's northeast triggered landslides and deadly floods, a video was shared in social media posts falsely claiming it showed the destruction caused by a deluge in Assam's state capital Guwahati. The video in fact shows flooding in a different state, Himachal Pradesh, in July 2023.

"Scary Scenes at Gauhati, Pray for Assam," reads the caption of a [Facebook video](https://perma.cc/2KV5-GS63) shared on June 3, 2025, using an alternative spelling for Assam's state capital Guwahati.

"Guwahati" is also superimposed over the video, which shows a raging torrent ripping down street-side stalls.

It surfaced after [flash floods and landslides](https://www.barrons.com/news/india-s-monsoon-rains-kill-at-least-30-in-northeast-8d95aa02) triggered by annual monsoon rains in India's northeast states killed at least 30 people, including eight in Assam ([archived link](https://perma.cc/V4YX-RQEL?type=image)).

India's annual monsoon season from June to September offers respite from the intense summer heat and is crucial for replenishing water supplies, but also brings widespread death and destruction.

Scores of people die each year during the rainy season due to flash floods and landslides across the country of 1.4 billion people.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-06/1576669803a083e1c9c4ddd81fbeb3a5-en.jpeg?itok=aUtlzVA4)

Screenshot of the false Facebook post, captured on June 15, 2025

The same video was also shared in similar [Instagram](https://perma.cc/MST9-5EC3) and [X posts](https://perma.cc/Z8FW-9YNF).

Several low-lying areas of Guwahati were [recently flooded](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250531-india-monsoon-floods-kill-five-in-northeast), with hundreds of families forced to abandon homes to seek shelter elsewhere, but the video circulating online was filmed nearly two years earlier ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20250608010515/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250531-india-monsoon-floods-kill-five-in-northeast)).

A [reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on Google using [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHNimjTpxd8) from the falsely shared video led to the same [footage](https://www.instagram.com/p/C_pHwZgvMXg/) posted on Instagram on September 8, 2024 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/KNB2-ZRMD)).

Its caption reads, "Sainj valley flood 09/07/2023". The [Sainj valley](https://maps.app.goo.gl/7VUEEztrGN64LTJz8) is in Himachal Pradesh state's Kullu district ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7KUH-UTCY)).

AFP reported in July 2023 that [torrential downpours](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-environment/20230712-death-toll-rises-to-66-in-india-s-monsoon-mayhem) washed away vehicles, demolished buildings and tore down bridges in Himachal Pradesh, the state worst affected by relentless monsoon rains at the time ([archived link](https://web.archive.org/web/20250618055301/https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-environment/20230712-death-toll-rises-to-66-in-india-s-monsoon-mayhem)).

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-06/60c634e6e2f8d0dab1ad35ae4fb7c6ed-en.jpeg?itok=Vii9_CBL)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared clip (left) and the video posted in September 2024 (right)

The same Instagram account also posted a [similar video](https://www.instagram.com/p/CudkPFHJ24_/) of the flooding in the same area on July 9, 2023 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/97RS-ZBT8)).

The user told AFP on June 15, 2025: "As far as I remember, the video is approximately two years old, from around the time there was a massive flood in the Sainj Valley."

Moreover, a photo sent from the valley by an AFP reporter includes similar elements to those seen in the circulating video.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2025-06/e0b8bcde659a5e716ca635a82e11289c-en.jpeg?itok=0oFPgsI6)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared clip (left) and a photo sent by an AFP reporter (right), with corresponding features highlighted

AFP has [previously debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.62247KD) other [false claims](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.369J4FW) related to India's [monsoon season](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.32E86PR).

# Old Video of a Crocodile on a Street in Gujarat Falsely Linked to Assam Flood

## The video dates back to 2019 when a crocodile was rescued by NDRF in Vadodara, Gujarat.

[Rujuta Thete](/author/1650578/rujuta-thete)

Published:

[WebQoof](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof)

i

Edited By :[Padmashree Pande](/author/1587567/padmashree-pande)

A video showing men wearing National Disaster Response Force's ([NDRF](https://www.thequint.com/topic/ndrf)) t-shirts and catching hold of a [crocodile](https://www.thequint.com/news/hot-news/video-of-crocodile-on-vadodara-street-goes-viral) on the flooded streets of [Assam](https://www.thequint.com/topic/assam-floods) is making rounds on social media with a claim that it was found on the streets of Silchar.

> This comes amid the [floods](https://www.thequint.com/news/india/assam-floods-death-toll-rises-rescue-teams-deployed) in Assam which have caused 88 deaths till now and affecting more than 12 lakh people.

However, this visual dates back to 2019 when a crocodile was rescued by NDRF after the water logged the streets of Vadodara in Gujarat.

ADVERTISEMENT[REMOVE AD](/plan-selection?utm_source=remove_ad&utm_medium=remove_ad_button)

**CLAIM**

The claim states that a crocodile was spotted in Silchar, Assam.

Similar posts can be seen [here](https://perma.cc/BCW5-6MGU), [here](https://perma.cc/5WNK-U2DE) and [here](https://perma.cc/54S5-GSA4).

**WHAT WE FOUND OUT**

Upon dividing the video into multiple keyframes and running it on Google reverse image search, we came across a [YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0mRS62uE19M) uploaded by 'Minglemine' on **7 August 2019.**

The visuals were same as the viral video.

The video title mentioned that a crocodile was rescued by the NDRF team.

Taking a cue, we performed a keyword search on Google using 'NDRF rescuing crocodile 2019'.

This led us to several news reports by *[The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/city/ahmedabad/10-feet-long-crocodile-rescued-by-ndrf-and-forest-department-in-vadodara/videoshow/70512425.cms), [India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/trending-news/story/water-in-gujarat-recedes-more-crocodiles-seen-on-vadodara-roads-watch-scary-viral-video-1577004-2019-08-04)* and *[The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/when-crocodiles-roamed-vadodara-streets/article29247390.ece?homepage=true).* All of these reports were published in August 2019.

> *[The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/city/ahmedabad/10-feet-long-crocodile-rescued-by-ndrf-and-forest-department-in-vadodara/videoshow/70512425.cms)'s* article mentioned that a 10 feet long crocodile was rescued by the combined efforts of the NDRF and forest department officials on 3 August 2019. According to the wildlife activists, several crocodiles were making their way in Vadodara's water logged streets from the Vishwamitri River.

The viral video is the continuation of the video carried by *[The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/city/ahmedabad/10-feet-long-crocodile-rescued-by-ndrf-and-forest-department-in-vadodara/videoshow/70512425.cms). [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/when-crocodiles-roamed-vadodara-streets/article29247390.ece?homepage=true)'s* report from 24 August 2019 about crocodiles on Vadodara's street also carries a snipet from the viral video.

***(Note: Swipe right to view the images.)***

* ## Comparison between the viral video and 2019's news report.

  (Source: Altered by The Quint)

* ## Comparison between the viral video and 2019's news report.

  (Source: Altered by The Quint)

We also found a [tweet](https://twitter.com/ANI/status/1157653945063477248) from a news agency *Asian News International (ANI)* from 3 August 2019 about a crocodile being rescued by NDRF in Vadsar area of Vadodara.

> Vadodara: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams rescued a crocodile from Vadsar area, earlier today. It was handed over to forest department officials. [#Gujarat](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Gujarat?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/IFXQJezwqc](https://t.co/IFXQJezwqc)
>
> — ANI (@ANI) [August 3, 2019](https://twitter.com/ANI/status/1157653945063477248?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Evidently, an old video of a crocodile spotted on water-logged streets is being falsely shared as an incident from Assam.

# Video Of Bridge Collapse From Indonesia Passed Off As Visuals Of Assam Floods

Written By [Vasudha Beri](/author/vasudha/1)

[Viral](/fact-check/viral/1)

May 19, 2022

![banner_image](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/05/Indonesia-Copy.jpg?quality=71&format=webp&w=1920)

---

As torrential rainfall wreaked havoc in Assam, several social media users shared images and videos from the flood-hit state highlighting the severity of the situation and condition of its residents. One such 21-second-long-video claiming to show a bridge collapse in Assam amid massive flooding is doing the rounds on social media platforms. Newschecker found the video to be old and unrelated to the recent floods in the north eastern state.

Several shared the video claiming to show visuals of Assam floods.

## **Assam floods wreak havoc**

Incessant rainfall due to to strong [southwesterly winds](https://internal.imd.gov.in/press_release/20220517_pr_1631.pdf) from Bay of Bengal, resulted in massive flooding and landslides in Assam. As per report by the [Assam State Disaster Management Authority](http://www.asdma.gov.in/pdf/flood_report/2022/Daily_Flood_Report_18.05.2022.pdf), dated May 18, 2022, a total of 27 districts in the state have been affected. The [death toll](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/9-die-in-assam-floods-over-6-lakh-affected-10-facts-2989045) as of Wednesday stood at nine while over 6.62 lakh people have been affected. More than 48,000 people have taken shelter in 135 relief camps in different districts of Assam, while 113 distribution centres have been set up across the state to ensure there is no shortage of essential commodities in the flood-hit areas.

## Fact Check/Verification

To check whether the viral clip  is from Assam or not, we conducted Google reverse image search by using its keyframes and found an article published in [Tribunnews Wiki](https://www.tribunnewswiki.com/2021/04/05/viral-video-detik-detik-jembatan-lama-kambaniru-di-sumba-timur-ambrol-terseret-arus-sungai) on April 5, 2021 with a title in Indonesian which roughly translates to “Viral Video Moments of the Collapse of the Old Kambaniru Bridge in East Sumba Dragged by the River Current.”

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/05/1s.jpg)

Screengrab from Google search

The article featured stills from the viral video with the caption which roughly translates to “A screenshot of a resident’s amateur video showing the old Kambaniru Bridge collapse under the swift current of the river on Sunday (4/4/2021).”

![Video of bridge collapse is from Indonesia. Not related to Assam Floods.](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/05/Screenshot-2022-05-19-145406.jpg)

Screengrab from Tribunnews Wiki website

On further reverse image search on Yandex, we found a report by website [Suryakepri](https://suryakepri.com/2021/04/04/jembatan-lama-kambaniru-sumba-timur-ambruk/), dated April 4, 2021, which also carried a still from the viral video with a caption in Indonesian which roughly translates to “Bridge collapses, flash floods in East Flores, Sunday (04/04/2021).”

According to the report, “The extreme climate in the East Nusa Tenggara Province caused the old Kambaniru bridge in East Sumba Regency, NTT to collapse in the flood, Sunday.” It added that the bridge was also known as Ahmad Yani bridge.

We found a video uploaded on a verified YouTube channel [KompasTV](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=NF35eTdABjM) on April 5, 2021 with an Indonesian caption which translates to “Flash Floods and Landslides Hit NTT.”  45 seconds into the video, we spotted a snippet from the viral clip.

![](https://newschecker.dietpixels.net/2022/05/Screenshot-2022-05-19-150032.jpg)

Screengrab from KompasTV YouTube channel

Keyframes of the viral video claiming to show a bridge collapse in Assam, were also seen in a YouTube video uploaded on verified channel [Official iNews](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=OZMFqH7PYWk) on April 5, 2021 with the caption in Indonesian which roughly translates to “The Ahmad Yani Bridge in East Sumba Drifted by Flash Floods – iNews Morning 05/04.”

Heavy rainfall led to massive flash floods and landslides in Indonesia and East Timor in April, 2021. Several media outlets carried reports on the same. You can read them [here](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-56635297), [here](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/4/indonesia-flash-floods-kill-44-toll-expected-to-rise) and [here](https://www.voanews.com/a/east-asia-pacific_flash-floods-landslides-kill-dozens-indonesia/6204132.html).

## Conclusion

Video showing a bridge collapse in Indonesia during flash floods of April 2021 shared with a claim to show a bridge collapse in Assam amid massive flooding.

## Result: False Context/False

**Sources**

Report published in [**Tribunnews Wiki**](https://www.tribunnewswiki.com/2021/04/05/viral-video-detik-detik-jembatan-lama-kambaniru-di-sumba-timur-ambrol-terseret-arus-sungai) on April 5, 2021

Report published in **[Suryakepri](https://suryakepri.com/2021/04/04/jembatan-lama-kambaniru-sumba-timur-ambruk/)** on April 4, 2021

Video uploaded on YouTube channel **[KompasTV](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=NF35eTdABjM)** on April 5, 2021

Video uploaded on YouTube channel [**Official iNews**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=OZMFqH7PYWk) on April 5, 2021

# Old, Unrelated Videos From India Falsely Linked To Nepal Floods

## BOOM found that the first video is from a dam in Maharashtra, while the second is from Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.

By -  [Anmol Alphonso](/author/anmol) 

Published -

[![Boomlive](https://www.boomlive.in/h-upload/2026/10/08/1058459-google.webp)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=boomlive.in)

Listen to this Article

Two unrelated videos from India are being shared on social media with false claims linking them to the recent flash floods in Nepal. One video shows a dam filled with water, while another shows a group of boys finding a bag full of Indian currency notes.

BOOM found that neither video is related to the Nepal tragedy. The first video shows a dam in Pune, Maharashtra, while the second is from Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh, and has been online since at least July 2026, predating the floods in Nepal.

The death toll from the devastating floods in Nepal and China has [crossed 1,000](https://apnews.com/article/nepal-flash-floods-death-toll-tibet-china-835459b2978adcd2b3bcf6e0595aee6c), with 987 deaths reported in Nepal and 16 in China. Rescue operations are still underway as landslides and damaged roads and bridges have left several places cut off.

**The Claim:**

One video claims to show the Gandak Barrage, a joint India-Nepal project which was inaugurated by former prime minister of India Jawaharlal Nehru. The second video shows a group of boys finding cash in a bag from the river

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DctJ8YSyhTe/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
>
> [A post shared by BHARAT JUNCTION ✊ (@bharat\_junction.in)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DctJ8YSyhTe/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

Click [here](https://perma.cc/7BPA-AE85?type=standard) to view an archive.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dco5R5Pzq5S/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
>
> [A post shared by Sorry Girls (@sorryygirlss)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dco5R5Pzq5S/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

Click [here](https://perma.cc/J2V8-86FJ?type=standard) to view an archive.

**What We Found:**

**1) Dam Video Is From Maharashtra, Not Nepal**

Taking a cue from replies to the Instagram post, we searched for keywords “Bhatghar Dam” and found that the dam in the video is from Pune district in Maharashtra. The same [visuals were viral last](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=988992700824058) month when the [dam reportedly](https://punemirror.com/city/pune/bhatghar-dam-reaches-100-percent-capacity-water-released-into-nira-river-riverside-villages-on-alert/) reached full capacity.

We also found similar videos from the same location which match the dam seen in the viral video.

**2) Video Of Boys Finding Money Is From Uttar Pradesh**

We ran a reverse image search using keyframes from the second video and found that it had been circulating online since July 2026, pre-dating the Nepal floods which happened on August 26, 2026.

The Instagram handle @parshuram\_676 had replied to a user stating that the video is shot in Vrindavan, Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh. The handle has also been [posting several](https://www.instagram.com/parshuram_676/reel/Dawb3Mjo4ad/) other similar videos of 'finding' a bag filled with money.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Daw7aYJAjoc/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
>
> [A post shared by . 🍁•𝗹ꪋ𝗹𝖚•🍁 (@parshuram\_676)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Daw7aYJAjoc/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

The Times of India [reported](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/how-60-year-old-india-nepal-border-barrage-helped-save-bihar-from-major-flood/articleshow/133645771.cms) on August 31, that while downstream villages in West Champaran faced flooding and evacuations when flood waters from Nepal reached down stream, the controlled release of water helped prevent a catastrophic disaster across north Bihar.
