# Staged video falsely shared as real footage of 2026 Nepal flood casualties

![Harshavardhan Konda](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/f4e6d329389ce6170b84db1fa1435d9a7ce3dcbf51e276c324048fc0eacb7351?s=32&d=mm&r=g)By [Harshavardhan Konda](https://factly.in/author/harshavardhan-konda/ "Posts by Harshavardhan Konda")Updated:[No Comments](https://factly.in/staged-video-falsely-shared-as-real-footage-of-2026-nepal-flood-casualties/#respond)2 Mins Read

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fstaged-video-falsely-shared-as-real-footage-of-2026-nepal-flood-casualties%2F "Share on Facebook")   [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fstaged-video-falsely-shared-as-real-footage-of-2026-nepal-flood-casualties%2F&text=Staged%20video%20falsely%20shared%20as%20real%20footage%20of%202026%20Nepal%20flood%20casualties "Share on X (Twitter)")   [Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fstaged-video-falsely-shared-as-real-footage-of-2026-nepal-flood-casualties%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F%2F2026%2F09%2FNepal-dead-bodies-Thumbnail-.jpg&description=Staged%20video%20falsely%20shared%20as%20real%20footage%20of%202026%20Nepal%20flood%20casualties "Share on Pinterest")   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fstaged-video-falsely-shared-as-real-footage-of-2026-nepal-flood-casualties%2F "Share on LinkedIn")   [Tumblr](https://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffactly.in%2Fstaged-video-falsely-shared-as-real-footage-of-2026-nepal-flood-casualties%2F&name=Staged%20video%20falsely%20shared%20as%20real%20footage%20of%202026%20Nepal%20flood%20casualties "Share on Tumblr")   [Email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Share via Email")

A video ([here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DcnLvAKjtJS/) & [here](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/pbWIp_riVa0)) claiming to show the bodies of victims who died in the Nepal flash floods on 26 August 2026, is circulating widely on social media. Let’s examine the veracity of this claim.

![](https://factly.in/wp-content/uploads//2026/09/Nepal-deadbodies-english-claim-.png)

Archived post can be seen [here](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/56158143?key=240f64d90a6de84adb87ca8fb6f20cfe)

> **Claim:** Video showing the deceased victims during the flash floods that struck Nepal on 26 August 2026.
>
> **Fact:** This video is unrelated to the Nepal floods. It is a staged video shot for entertainment purpose by an Instagram creator. The Nepal floods occurred on 26 August 2026, but this video was uploaded on 03 August 2026. Hence, the claim made in the post is **misleading.**

A reverse image search of the keyframes from the viral video revealed that the [same video](https://www.instagram.com/p/DblC1ypK_ME/) ([archive](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/56115365?key=ab102365307bcab90cf521b737dce525)) was uploaded to Instagram on 03 August 2026 by a content creator named [Simran SK](https://www.instagram.com/simransk944/). This confirms that the video has no connection to the Nepal floods, as it was uploaded well before the actual disaster took place.

A closer review of Simran SK’s Instagram account indicates a pattern of uploading [comedy](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dafa6XIqku8/) and [scripted](https://www.instagram.com/p/DaZdU8kq9X8/) videos. We also found other [scripted videos](https://www.instagram.com/p/DbiiwPuKHWj/) ([archive](https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/55122130?key=b1fa10a02b94e0d711a383124c434e69)) on the account featuring individuals pretending to be dead. Furthermore, during the Assam floods in July 2026, another scripted video from this very account was falsely circulated as a real incident. Our previous fact-check article regarding that instance can be read [here](https://factly.in/a-staged-video-is-falsely-shared-as-showing-the-dead-bodies-of-2026-assam-flood-victims/).

To sum it up, a scripted video is being falsely shared as genuine footage of deceased victims from the 2026 Nepal floods.

# Old family outing video falsely linked to 2026 Bangladesh monsoon floods

* Published on July 16, 2026 at 09:57
* 2 min read
* By [Eyamin SAJID](https://factcheck.afp.com/eyamin-sajid),  [AFP Bangladesh](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-bangladesh)

Flash floods and landslides triggered by heavy rainfall in Bangladesh have killed at least 50 people and displaced thousands, but footage of a woman taking shelter on a tree in a submerged area does not show a flood victim as falsely claimed in social media posts. The clip circulated online in July 2024 and shows a woman at a popular tourist spot in the country, who confirmed to AFP the video is not linked to the recent disaster.

"A pregnant mother has climbed a tree with her nine-month-old unborn child to save her life," reads a Bengali-language Facebook [post](https://perma.cc/4RY3-WBK9?type=image) shared on July 11, 2026.

The post includes a video of a woman trying to position herself on a tree in a submerged area.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-07/e46ee9f6e1501bf70399ae386553775f-en.jpeg?itok=COSnr1rE)

Screenshot of the falsely shared Facebook post taken on July 14, 2026 with a red X added by AFP

The [video](https://perma.cc/5VAY-7Y9K?type=image) appeared in similar [Facebook posts](https://perma.cc/HZB8-8RXG) as monsoon rains triggered [flash floods](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/bangladesh-monsoon-rain-landslide-deaths-displaced-6249356) and landslides in early July, killing at least 50 people and displacing thousands across the country ([archived link](https://perma.cc/U6GT-FE5Z)).

The country's southeastern Chattogram district remains the worst affected with homes, land, roads and markets inundated, forcing thousands of people to seek shelter in government-run centres.

Bangladesh media organisation The Business Standard reported the calamity also killed more than tens of thousands of [livestock and poultry](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/chattogram-floods-kill-over-112-lakh-livestock-and-poultry-losses-top-tk30-crore-1486666) across the region ([archived link](https://perma.cc/334F-9RES)).

Comments from users seeking "God's mercy on the flood victim" suggest they believed the claim is genuine, but the video actually shows a tourist enjoying a family trip.

## Wetland tourist spot

[Reverse image search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=linGPlWGcDw) on [keyframes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pKskDgeuQw4) of the video found a similar footage shared in a [Facebook post](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1192012395155243) on July 15, 2024 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/MPG7-BURV)).

The post mentions "Tanguar Haor", a [natural water reservoir](https://beautifulbangladesh.gov.bd/loc/sylhet/121) in Bangladesh's Sunamganj district declared as [wetland](https://www.ramsar.org/about/our-mission/importance-wetlands) of international importance under the Ramsar international environment treaty to protect wetlands (archived [here](https://web.archive.org/save/https://www.ramsar.org/about/our-mission/importance-wetlands) and [here](https://perma.cc/EQ3A-A7XP)).

Its diverse natural and aquatic features makes the site a popular tourist attraction in the country.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-07/e8dc2bc33a30638ed6154b0840cc236d-en.jpeg?itok=5MdDHGaR)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (L) and the footage shared by the content creator in July 2024

AFP reached out to the woman in the viral video who confirmed it was filmed during a "family outing" in July 2024.

"That is me in the video. My son filmed it on July 13, 2024 when we went to Tanguar Haor for a family trip," Anjana Abedin, a teacher by profession, told AFP on July 13, 2026.

"Some content creators have stolen the video from my page and posted it as a flood scene from Chattogram," she added.

In one of her recent [Facebook posts](https://www.facebook.com/reel/2235143047248285), she refuted the claim and said the video showed scenes from "Tanguar Haor" ([archived link](https://perma.cc/LKK5-BJNJ)).

AFP has previously debunked misinformation about disasters [here](https://factcheck.afp.com/fact-checking-search-results?search_api_fulltext=disasters).

# Old footage shows flood rescue in Japan, not Bangladesh

* This article is more than two years old.
* Published on August 29, 2024 at 07:36
* 2 min read
* By [AFP Bangladesh](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-bangladesh)

A video from 2015 of two people being airlifted to safety after heavy floods hit Japan has racked up hundreds of thousands of views in posts that falsely claimed it was filmed recently in Bangladesh. While Bangladeshi authorities said monsoon rains submerged parts of the South Asian nation in August 2024 and killed dozens of people, the footage was wrongly recirculated in posts praising the Bangladesh army's rescue efforts.

The video has been viewed over 450,000 times after it was [shared on Facebook](https://perma.cc/4LTW-5FY3) on August 22, 2024. Its Bengali-language caption translated as "Bangladesh army is our pride."

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2024-08/9599eec834e6cd36b2d9d59282f753f01894f998.jpeg?itok=g6DIWcJU)

A screenshot of the false post on Facebook

[Flash floods](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/south-asia/floods-ease-in-bangladesh-but-300000-still-in-shelters) wrought havoc in Bangladesh in August, killing at least [40 people](https://www.barrons.com/news/monsoon-floods-in-india-s-gujarat-kill-at-least-28-people-43cc2c4f) (archived links [here](https://perma.cc/6ZAT-V7JK) and [here](https://perma.cc/P5KM-PDSL)).

The South Asian nation of 170 million people, crisscrossed by hundreds of rivers, has seen frequent floods in recent decades.

Monsoon rains cause widespread destruction every year, but climate change is shifting weather patterns and increasing the number of extreme weather events.

The floods added to the woes of a nation still reeling from weeks of political turmoil that culminated in the toppling of autocratic leader Sheikh Hasina, who fled to India by helicopter.

She was replaced by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus, who is heading an interim government that faces the monumental task of charting democratic reforms ahead of expected new elections.

The video has also been shared alongside a similar false claim on Facebook [here](https://perma.cc/427T-9QRX) and [here](https://perma.cc/R4XJ-XVEB).

### Japan flooding video

A reverse image search of the video's keyframes on Google followed by keyword searches found the footage [published](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EEcotUWktuQ) by the International Business Times UK newspaper on YouTube on September 10, 2015 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/YDL5-V7KE)).

"Japan floods: Couple and their dogs rescued from rooftop after Joso City submerged under water," read the video's title.

AFP [reported](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/missing-people-found-japan-floods-authorities-065154070.html) at the time that parts of Joso city north of the Japanese capital Tokyo were washed away when a levee on the Kinugawa River gave way after heavy rains ([archived link](https://perma.cc/GT42-R48G)).

Below is a screenshot comparison between the falsely shared video on Facebook (left) and the footage from the International Business Times UK (right):

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2024-08/d733bf635301d4d541babfc6786e7b680b9cb28c.jpeg?itok=Hm-xrzqe)

A screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video on Facebook (left) and the video from the International Business Times UK (right)

Similar clips have been published in reports about the flooding in Japan by the US-based [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/japan-roof-rescues-water-overwhelms-neighborhood-after-levee-breach-n424761) and Turkey's [TRT World](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PGkPvvNt7-k) (archived links [here](https://perma.cc/97VZ-KU54) and [here](https://perma.cc/GG5V-8N48)).

AFP has also distributed a corresponding picture of the rescue credited to The Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper.

Below is a screenshot of the picture in AFP's archives:

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2024-08/d0223b92b9640cf5683514916f20f889efcd858f.jpeg?itok=bFvwlfZJ)

# Mumbai airport flooded? Republic, others share old image of inundated Chennai airport

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/a4a0477ebec4d5590fdb727dbcaa04b3cec9f6db79e9eea09829393dcc4032a6?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/prantikali/)

[Prantik Ali](https://www.altnews.in/author/prantikali/)

 ![Mumbai airport flooded? Republic, others share old image of inundated Chennai airport](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/FI-template-Prantik-2-1024x536.jpg) 

A video of a waterlogged tarmac at an airport with ground crew crowded around the wheels of an airplane as several aircraft remain stranded in the background is being circulated on social media as a visual of the flooded Mumbai airport.

Maharashtra witnessed heavy torrential rain over the past few days, with the total death toll crossing 27, according to a [Deccan Herald report](https://www.deccanherald.com/india/maharashtra/maharashtra-rains-death-toll-crosses-27-3689665). Several regions of Mumbai have been inundated, [bringing](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/rain-wreaks-havoc-in-maharashtra-brings-mumbai-to-a-standstill/article69948564.ece) daily activities to a standstill.

Claiming that operations at Mumbai airport were disrupted, news outlet Republic shared the video on X on August 19. The caption read: “[#MumbaiRains](https://archive.is/o/NePKB/https://x.com/hashtag/MumbaiRains?src=hashtag_click) | Over 250 flights delayed at Mumbai Airport as heavy rains flooded runways.” The post was later deleted; an archived version can be accessed [here](https://archive.is/NePKB#selection-603.0-607.77).

X user Priya Sinha (@iPriyaSinha), an anchor affiliated with the news channel Bharat 24, also shared the same video on August 19 but later deleted it. ([Archive](https://archive.is/BLAmN))

Several others on X, such as [@limitlessfinan](https://x.com/limitlessfinan/status/1957745315714592896), [@NewsTheTruthh](https://x.com/NewsTheTruthh/status/1957756882774290664), [@Vignesh58Viki](https://x.com/Vignesh58Viki/status/1957747631649878142) and [@diplomattimes](https://x.com/diplomattimes/status/1957769337034473669) shared the video, suggesting it showed the Mumbai airport. (Archived links [1](https://archive.fo/5PhZI), [2](https://archive.fo/aKG5F), [3](https://archive.fo/TLnQd), [4](https://archive.fo/rfnue))

This slideshow requires JavaScript.

#### Fact Check

Alt News did reverse-image searches of some key frames from the viral video, which led us to [an X post](https://x.com/TimesNow/status/1731620662182302153) by Times Now from December 4, 2023, featuring the same clip. Going by the caption, the video showed the Chennai airport ravaged by [Cyclone Michaung](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-67617727), which hit India’s southern states in December 2023.

> [#CycloneMichaung](https://twitter.com/hashtag/CycloneMichaung?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw): Runway at Chennai airport flooded amid heavy rainfall across the city.[#ChennaiRains](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChennaiRains?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Chennai](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Chennai?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/6EyGfYt7CI](https://t.co/6EyGfYt7CI)
>
> — TIMES NOW (@TimesNow) [December 4, 2023](https://twitter.com/TimesNow/status/1731620662182302153?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

This made it clear that the video was not recent and had been online for at least two years.

While investigating we also noticed a yellow signboard at the beginning of the video, which contains what seemed like GPS coordinates of the place (written in degrees, minutes, and seconds) — 12° 59 ‘5.9 ” N 80° 9’ 47.686” E.

On feeding these coordinates on [Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/place/12%C2%B059'05.9%22N+80%C2%B009'47.7%22E/@12.9848743,80.1603854,16.31z/data=!4m4!3m3!8m2!3d12.9849722!4d80.1632461?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDgxOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D), the location showed up as Chennai, Tamil Nadu, not Mumbai, Maharashtra. The location was marked in the vicinity of ‘MAA’ on Google Maps, which is the airport code for Chennai International Airport.

Thus, claims suggesting that the video shows the waterlogged condition of Mumbai airport after the recent heavy rains there are false and misleading. The video actually shows the flooded Chennai International Airport after Cyclone Michaung in December 2023.

# Times of India publishes old video as Nagpur airport flooded due to recent rains

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/1aa40b8ea2fcd3213bde31a79dd440aa1ecb520ae7d7349253a1befe72c5ce0d?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/arjun/)

[Arjun Sidharth](https://www.altnews.in/author/arjun/)

 ![Times of India publishes old video as Nagpur airport flooded due to recent rains](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/FINagpurairport-2-1024x536.jpeg) 

With the entire country under the spell of monsoon, social media has been inundated with photographs and videos of the mayhem caused by the rains. One such video is being shared, which is claimed to be of Nagpur airport. [*Times of India*](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/city/mumbai/nagpur-rains-heavy-downpour-floods-airport/videoshow/64887671.cms?from=mdr) on its website uploaded a video on July 8, 2018 and reported that the airport has been flooded due to heavy rain. The video shows rain water being mopped off the floor near the check-in counter. The video has now been [deleted by *Times of India*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CSYk1Xzga9E). A screenshot of the same is posted below.

Social media users on Twitter and [Facebook](https://facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=2039065266165893&id=100001873173180) took potshots at the BJP government and Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the state of the airport at Nagpur.

> Even DXB, Heathrow and Kennedy airport can’t provide you shower while checking-in but Nagpur Airport surely can. [#Nagpur](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Nagpur?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#NagpurRains](https://twitter.com/hashtag/NagpurRains?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#NagpurAirport](https://twitter.com/hashtag/NagpurAirport?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Rain](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Rain?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Worldcup](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Worldcup?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/Jj1aS1MqJH](https://t.co/Jj1aS1MqJH)
>
> — k!t@π¶ ~ 🏆 (@ChhapriSala) [July 6, 2018](https://twitter.com/ChhapriSala/status/1015224279544291328?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Vijay Darda, Chairman of Lokmat India also tweeted the video claiming it is of Nagpur airport.

> Rains in [#Nagpur](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Nagpur?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) have flooded roads, inundated many parts of the city including Vidhan Bhavan campus; leakages at airport too. Why are our infrastructure & maintenance so shoddy? Why do citizens have to suffer due to callous, careless attitude of authorities? Shame on the system! [pic.twitter.com/C2AVUoG97J](https://t.co/C2AVUoG97J)
>
> — Vijay Darda (@vijayjdarda) [July 6, 2018](https://twitter.com/vijayjdarda/status/1015225392179785728?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

### **Where is the video from?**

Alt News broke up the video into individual frames using the *InVid* software for videos, and found instances wherein this video had been uploaded earlier. We followed a link to a YouTube video according to which this is an airport in Kerala. The videos uploaded on YouTube claim that this is the Kozhikode (Calicut) airport.

In fact, Alt News found that this video had been uploaded as early as March 2018. The video posted below was uploaded on the YouTube channel *Asianet HD* on March 24, 2018.

In all likelihood, the flooding of the check-in section as seen in the video could be due to a leakage in the air conditioning system. Alt News could not independently verify the claim that it is the Kozhikode airport in Kerala. However, the fact that this video has been online since at least March 2018 establishes that this is not the Nagpur airport flooded due to the recent rain that lashed the city.

### **Video of Mexico City airport passed off as flooding of Mumbai airport**

[Similar mischief](https://www.altnews.in/no-mumbai-airport-is-not-flooded-old-video-from-mexico-shared-on-social-media/) was played with the Mumbai airport which, it was claimed, was flooded after a video showing an inundated tarmac was shared widely. However, the video was of Mexico City international airport and was first posted in August 2017.

> Mumbai Airport flooded. Flights delayed and cancelled. Please check your flight status online before heading to the airport. [#MumbaiRains](https://twitter.com/hashtag/MumbaiRains?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#MumbaiRains2018](https://twitter.com/hashtag/MumbaiRains2018?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Weather](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Weather?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Airport](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Airport?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/yfRGBshLUS](https://t.co/yfRGBshLUS)
>
> — The News Jockey (@TheNewsJockey) [July 10, 2018](https://twitter.com/TheNewsJockey/status/1016738526510055430?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Infrastructural durability is understandably a cause of concern when faced with nature’s fury, particularly in India where public works are infamous for often being brittle. This does not however warrant creating panic by sharing an old video which a mainstream news organisation like *Times of India* has unfortunately succumbed to. An old video of March 2018 was presented as a current event and could have been avoided by resorting to basic verification.

# PTI image of flooded Gujarat airport joins the long list of fake images in recent times

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/c779ce91267626f6fbe79dece0497237aef460a41ec675c0a293ddd244a72801?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/altnews/)

[Alt News Desk](https://www.altnews.in/author/altnews/)

 ![PTI image of flooded Gujarat airport joins the long list of fake images in recent times](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/pti-post-fi-1024x538.jpg) 

Overworked or lazy? While glorifying achievements or talking about disasters, fake pictures which are not remotely representative of an event have been repeatedly used to portray events. From media outlets to political parties, everybody is guilty of doing so at some point in time. Therefore, it comes as no surprise that a PTI photographer used a picture of a flooded Chennai Airport from 2015 to depict a flooded Ahmedabad airport. The PTI image was splashed across the front page of Indian Express and tweeted by others like India Today, Hindu, Indiatimes etc and became a cause of much embarrassment for the largest news agency of India.

Folks on social media discovered that the images were of Chennai airport flooding and not Ahmedabad and there was a huge amount of outrage following that. Smriti Irani tweeted about it alerting Twitter users and news establishments. She also suggested to PTI News to get an explanation as to how this happened.

> Attention: photographs of Chennai floods have been used and passed off as Ahmedabad [@PTI\_News](https://twitter.com/PTI_News) Kindly alert all news establishments.
>
> — Smriti Z Irani (@smritiirani) [July 28, 2017](https://twitter.com/smritiirani/status/890775272697417728)

> It would be prudent [@PTI\_News](https://twitter.com/PTI_News) to get an explanation as to how this happened.
>
> — Smriti Z Irani (@smritiirani) [July 28, 2017](https://twitter.com/smritiirani/status/890776630808858624)

PTI in turn regretted the error and tweeted that they had terminated the services of the concerned photographer

> PTI deeply regrets the error and has terminated the services of the concerned photographer; [@smritiirani](https://twitter.com/smritiirani) and [@shashidigital](https://twitter.com/shashidigital)
>
> — Press Trust of India (@PTI\_News) [July 28, 2017](https://twitter.com/PTI_News/status/890816815638560768)

Using fake images has become an epidemic on social media. It is good to see that the problem has been recognised and the use of a misleading image from Chennai to show Gujarat floods has got the attention it deserved, not just in social media but also from PTI and a Union Minister.

Alt News would like to bring some other instances of fake images to the attention of the honourable Minister requesting for her intervention so that action can be taken against the propagators of the following fake images.

1. Alt News [exposed](http://www.altnews.in/home-ministry-annual-report-uses-picture-spain-morocco-border-show-indian-border-floodlighting/) how a picture of lights along the Spain Morocco border passed off as floodlights along the India-Pakistan border in the Annual report of Ministry of Home Affairs. The blooper got a fair amount of publicity in the media and the MHA even announced an investigation to find out how it happened. Nothing further was heard about the progress of the investigation.

2. A picture of Motorway A2 of Poland was used in a poster by the official Twitter account of BJP to show the reform measures under Modi government in the area of road projects.

3. Akhilesh Mishra, a former director of MyGov under Modi Government once tweeted a picture of Guangzhou, China, claiming it is Ahmedabad Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS). “Contrast this with the mess in Delhi,” he tweeted.

4. BJP ruled South Delhi Municipal corporation was once submitted a photoshopped image to a court of law. “A Delhi High Court bench spotted doctored photographs of roads and pavements in Dwarka wiped digitally clean by the agencies to claim they had acted upon complaints by residents about poor civic facilities.”

5. Press Information Bureau, the nodal agency for communicating to media on behalf of the government had tweeted a photoshopped picture to show Prime Minister Modi doing an aerial survey of the Chennai floods. The image became the butt of many jokes on social media mocking PIB but it is not known if any action was taken against those responsible for it.

> PIB tweets [#photoshopped](https://twitter.com/hashtag/photoshopped?src=hash) image of PM [@narendramodi](https://twitter.com/narendramodi) 's [#Chennai](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Chennai?src=hash) visit, later deleted <https://t.co/gSncqHQ53J> [pic.twitter.com/s9dXBc0lfB](https://t.co/s9dXBc0lfB)
>
> — ABP News (@abpnewstv) [December 3, 2015](https://twitter.com/abpnewstv/status/672455400986304512)

6. A few months ago, the official Twitter account of BJP Delhi [passed off](http://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/bjp-does-a-copy-paste-job-on-twitter-boasts-about-south-delhi-led-lights-with-photo-of-canadian-street/617843) the photo of a Canadian street to show replacement of street lights by the South Delhi Municipal Corporation.

The above is just a selection from the long list of instances where fake, misleading or photoshopped images have been used by official handles of the government or the ruling party. It is only fair that those responsible for circulating fake images from official handles are held accountable for their actions. In addition to this, there are [numerous instances](http://www.altnews.in/epidemic-fake-videos-hits-indian-social-media-ecosystem/) where fake images and videos have been circulated in social media with an objective of polarising communities and inciting violence. This is an epidemic that needs urgent attention.

# #FactCheck: Old Dubai Airport Video Falsely Shared as Delhi Airport Footage After Heavy Rain

![Research Wing]()

Research Wing

Innovation and Research

PUBLISHED ON

Sep 7, 2026

10

### Executive Summary

A post is being widely circulated on social media claiming that the entire Delhi airport was submerged following heavy rainfall. The post questions the airport’s drainage system and attributes the situation to the negligence of its staff. The post further claims that the airport’s arrangements were exposed after just one spell of rain and that its drainage system needs to be upgraded using better technology. A research by the research wing of CyberPeace found that the viral video is not from Delhi airport but dates back to April 2024. At the time, heavy rainfall in Dubai caused flood-like conditions at the airport, affecting flight operations on waterlogged runways as well. Thus, an old video from Dubai is being falsely shared on social media as footage of Delhi airport.

‍

### Claim:

### ‍

A user on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter) shared the viral video with the caption: “Delhi Airport — the entire airport is submerged. This is the situation after just one spell of rain. A minor issue of drainage and negligence by the staff — the public is aware — now the negligence will be punished. ‘The drainage system technology must be developed.’”

<https://x.com/RJMediaGroups/status/2096470339060736149>

<https://archive.ph/tKLet>

‍

‍

### Factcheck

‍

As part of our investigation, we conducted a reverse image search of keyframes from the video. During the search, we found the original video on a YouTube channel named The Indian Express, which was uploaded on April 17, 2024. According to the video description, the incident took place in Dubai. The post link and screenshot are provided below.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O9F1qTMIO5M>

‍

‍

During our investigation, we found visuals similar to those in the viral video on the YouTube channel AlArabiyaEnglish. The video was uploaded on April 16, 2024. According to the information provided in the video description, several parts of the UAE were affected by flooding following sudden heavy rainfall on April 16, 2024. The heavy rains also affected operations at Dubai Airport, disrupting several flights. According to the report, the UAE recorded a record 254 mm of rainfall in less than 24 hours. In view of the adverse weather conditions, Dubai Airport advised passengers to travel only if absolutely necessary. The post link and screenshot are provided below.

https://www.youtube.com/shorts/KzIstkiOdp4

‍

### Conclusion:

‍

Our investigation found that the viral video does not show Delhi Airport after heavy rainfall. The visuals are actually from Dubai Airport, where severe rainfall in the UAE in April 2024 led to flooding and disruptions to airport operations. Therefore, the viral video is old and has been falsely shared on social media with the misleading claim that it shows the current condition of Delhi Airport.

MISINFORMATION: A JUDICIAL OVERVIEW

10

May 13, 2024](/resources/blogs/misinformation-a-judicial-overview)

### Introduction

Misinformation in India has emerged as a significant societal challenge, wielding a potent influence on public perception, political discourse, and social dynamics. A potential number of first-time voters across India identified fake news as a real problem in the nation. With the widespread adoption of digital platforms, false narratives, manipulated content, and fake news have found fertile ground to spread unchecked information and news.

In the backdrop of India being the largest market of WhatsApp users, who forward more content on chats than anywhere else, the practice of fact-checking forwarded information continues to remain low. The heavy reliance on print media, television, unreliable news channels and primarily, social media platforms acts as a catalyst since studies reveal that most Indians trust any content forwarded by family and friends. It is noted that out of all risks, misinformation and disinformation ranked the highest in India, coming before infectious diseases, illicit economic activity, inequality and labour shortages. World Economic Forum analysts, in connection with their 2024 Global Risk Report, note that *“misinformation and disinformation in electoral processes could seriously destabilise the real and perceived legitimacy of newly elected governments, risking political unrest, violence and terrorism and long-term erosion of democratic processes.”*

### The Supreme Court of India on Misinformation

The Supreme Court of India, through various judgements, has noted the impact of misinformation on democratic processes within the country, especially during elections and voting. In 1995, while adjudicating a matter pertaining to keeping the broadcasting media under the control of the public, it noted that democracy becomes a farce when the medium of information is monopolized either by partisan central authority or by private individuals or oligarchic organizations.

In 2003, the Court stated that “*Right to participate by casting a vote at the time of election would be meaningless unless the voters are well informed about all sides of the issue in respect of which they are called upon to express their views by casting their votes. Disinformation, misinformation, non-information all equally create an uninformed citizenry which would finally make democracy a mobocracy and a farce.*” It noted that elections would be a useless procedure if voters remained unaware of the antecedents of the candidates contesting elections. Thus, a necessary aspect of a voter’s duty to cast intelligent and rational votes is being well-informed. Such information forms one facet of the fundamental right under Article 19 (1)(a) pertaining to freedom of speech and expression. Quoting James Madison, it stated that a citizen’s right to know the true facts about their country’s administration is one of the pillars of a democratic State.

On a similar note, the Supreme Court, while discussing the disclosure of information by an election candidate, gave weightage to the High Court of Bombay‘s opinion on the matter, which opined that non-disclosure of information resulted in misinformation and disinformation, thereby influencing voters to take uninformed decisions. It stated that a voter had the elementary right to know the full particulars of a candidate who is to represent him in Parliament/Assemblies.

While misinformation was discussed primarily in relation to elections, the effects of misinformation in other sectors have also been discussed from time to time. In particular, The court highlighted the World Health Organisation’s observation in 2021 while discussing the spread of COVID-19, noting that the pandemic was not only an epidemic but also an “infodemic” due to the overabundance of information on the internet, which was riddled with misinformation and disinformation. While condemning governments’ direct or indirect threats of prosecution to citizens, it noted that various citizens who relied on the internet to provide help in securing medical facilities and oxygen tanks were being targeted by alleging that the information posted by them was false and was posted to create panic, defame the administration or damage national image. It instructed authorities to cease such threats and prevent clampdown on information sharing.

More recently, in *Facebook v. Delhi Legislative Assembly [(2022) 3 SCC 529],* the apex court, while upholding the summons issued to Facebook by the Delhi Legislative Assembly in the aftermath of the 2020 Delhi Riots, noted that while social media enables equal and open dialogue between citizens and policymakers, it is also a tool in the where extremist views are peddled into mainstream media, thereby spreading misinformation. It noted Facebook’s role in the Mynmar, where misinformation and posts that Facebook employees missed fueled offline violence. Since Facebook is one of the most popular social media applications, the platform itself acts as a power center by hosting various opinions and voices on its forum. This directly impacts the governance of States, and some form of liability must be attached to the platform. The Supreme Court objected to Facebook taking contrary stands in various jurisdictions; while in the US, it projected itself as a publisher, which enabled it to maintain control over the material disseminated from its platform, while in India, *“it has chosen to identify itself purely as a social media platform, despite its similar functions and services in the two countries.*”

### Conclusion

The pervasive issue of misinformation in India is a multifaceted challenge with profound implications for democratic processes, public awareness, and social harmony. The alarming statistics of fake news recognition among first-time voters, coupled with a lack of awareness regarding fact-checking organizations, underscore the urgency of addressing this issue. The Supreme Court of India has consistently recognized the detrimental impact of misinformation, particularly in elections. The judiciary has stressed the pivotal role of an informed citizenry in upholding the essence of democracy. It has emphasized the right to access accurate information as a fundamental aspect of freedom of speech and expression. As India grapples with the challenges of misinformation, the intersection of technology, media literacy and legal frameworks will be crucial in mitigating the adverse effects and fostering a more resilient and informed society.

### Introduction

In order to effectively deal with growing cyber crime and threats the Telangana police has taken initiative by launching Law Enforcement Chief Information Security Officers (CISO) Council, an innovative project launched in Telangana, India, which is a significant response to the growing cyber threat landscape. With cyber incidents increasing in the recent years and concerning statistics such as a tenfold rise in password-based attacks and an increase in ransomware attacks, the Council aims to strengthen the region's digital defenses. It primarily focuses on reducing vulnerability, improving resilience, and providing real-time threat intelligence. By promoting partnerships between the public and private sectors, offering legal and regulatory guidance, and facilitating networking and learning opportunities, this collaborative effort involving industry, academia, and law enforcement is a crucial move towards protecting critical infrastructure and businesses from cyber threats, the Telangana police in partnership with industry and academia, has launched the Law Enforcement CISO (Chief Information Security Officers) Council of India on 7th October 2023. Chief of the Central Crime Station Stephen Ravindra said that the forum is a path-breaking initiative and the Council represents an open platform for all the enforcement agencies in the country. The upcoming inititiative inculcate close association with different stakeholders, which includes government departments, startups, centers of excellence and international collaborations, carving a nieche for a sturdy cybersecurity envirnoment.

### Enhancing Cybersecurity is the Need of the Hour:

The recent launch of the Law Enforcement CISO Council in Hyderabad, India emphasized the need for government organizations and industries to prioritize the protection of their digital space. Cyber incidents, ransomware attacks, and threats to critical infrastructure have been on the rise, making it essential to take proactive cybersecurity measures. Disturbing statistics regarding cyber threats, such as password-based attacks, BEC (Business Email Compromise) attempts, and vulnerabilities in the supply chain, highlight the importance of addressing these issues urgently. This initiative aims to provide real-time threat intelligence, legal guidance, and encourages collaboration between public and private organizations in order to combat cybercrime. Given that every cyber attack has criminal elements, the establishment of these councils is a crucial step towards minimizing vulnerabilities, enhancing resilience, and ensuring the security of our digital world.

### International Issue & Domestic Issue:

The announcement by the Telangana State Police, is a proactive step to form a first-of-its-kind Law Enforcement CISO Council (LECC), as part of an initiative from the State government to give a further impetus to cyber security. Jointly with its law enforcement partners, the Telangana Police has decided to make cyber cops more efficient and shape them on par with the technology advancements. The Telangana police have proved its commitment for a secure cyber environment by recovering INR 2.2 crore and  INR 6.8 crore lost by people in cyber frauds which is industry’s highest rate of helping the victims.

The Police department complemented efforts by corporate executives for their personal interest in the subject and mentioned police officers’ expertise and inputs from professionals from the industry need to work cohesively to prevent further increase in the number of cyber crime cases. Data indicates that the exponential increase in cyber threats in recent times necessitates an informed and prudent action with the cooperation and collaboration of the IT Department of Telangana, centers of excellence, start-ups, white hats or ethical hackers, and international associations.

A report from Telangana commissioner states the trend of a surge in the number of cyber incidents and vulnerabilities of Government organizations, Critical Infrastructure and MSMEs and stressed that every cyber security breaches have an element of criminality in it. The Law Enforcement CISO Council is a progressive step in this direction which ensures a reduced cyber attacks, enhanced resilience, actionable strategic and tactical real-time threat intelligence, legal guidance, opportunities for public private partnerships, networking, learning and much more.

The Secretary of SCSC, shared some alarming statistics on the threats that are currently rampant across the digital world. To combat it in today’s era of widespread digital dependence, the program launched by the Telangana Police stands as a commendable step or an initiative that offers a glimmer of aspiration. It brings together all the heroes who want to protect the digital spaces and counter the growing number of threats.

### **Contribution of Telangana Police for carving a niche to be followed:**

The launch of the Law Enforcement CISO Council in Telangana represents a pivotal step in addressing the pressing challenges posed by escalating cyber threats. As highlighted by the Director General of Police, the initiative recognizes the critical need to combat cybercrime, which is growing at an alarming rate. The Council not only acknowledges the casual approach often taken towards cybersecurity but also aims to rectify it by fostering collaboration between law enforcement, industry, and academia.

One of the most significant positive aspects of this initiative is its commitment to sharing intelligence, ensuring that the hard-earned lessons from cyber fraud victims are translated into protective measures for others. By collaborating with the IT Department of Telangana, centers of excellence, startups, and ethical hackers, the Council is poised to develop robust Standard Operating Protocols (SOPs) and innovative tools to counter cyber threats effectively.

Moreover, the Council's emphasis on Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) underscores its proactive approach in dealing with the evolving landscape of cyber threats. It offers a platform for networking and learning, enabling information sharing, and will contribute to reducing the attack surface, enhancing resilience, and providing real-time threat intelligence. Additionally, the Council will provide legal and regulatory guidance, which is crucial in navigating the complex realm of cybercrime. This collective effort represents a promising way forward in safeguarding digital spaces, critical infrastructure, and industries against cyber threats and ensuring a safer digital future for all.

### ‍**Conclusion:**

The Law Enforcement CISO Council in Telangana is an innovative effort to strengthen cybersecurity in the state. With the rise in cybercrimes and vulnerabilities, the council brings together expertise from various sectors to establish a strong defense against digital threats. Its goals include reducing vulnerabilities, improving resilience, and ensuring timely threat intelligence. Additionally, the council provides guidance on legal and regulatory matters, promotes collaborations between the public and private sectors, and creates opportunities for networking and knowledge-sharing. Through these important initiatives, the CISO Council will play a crucial role in establishing digital security and protecting the state from cyber threats.

#FactCheck: False Claim Says Indian Army Shot Two Women, Burnt Houses in Manipur

#FactCheck: False Claim Says Indian Army Shot Two Women, Burnt Houses in Manipur

10

September 19, 2026](/resources/blogs/factcheck-false-claim-says-indian-army-shot-two-women-burnt-houses-in-manipur)

### Executive Summary

A claim is being shared on social media alleging that two women were shot dead and their homes were set on fire in Manipur. The post alleges that the Indian Army carried out the attack on the orders of Lieutenant General V. M. Bhuvana Krishnan, Commander of the Eastern Command. CyberPeace Research found the claim to be false. According to available reports, suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district. During an exchange of fire with security forces, the attackers set at least two houses on fire.

‍

### Claim:

‍  
The Indian Army, on the orders of Eastern Command Commander Lieutenant General V. M. Bhuvana Krishnan, shot two women in Manipur and set their homes on fire, following which the situation in the state deteriorated severely.

<https://x.com/indiantiwari01/status/2100204995425743103?s=20>

https://archive.ph/SOm7I

### Fact Check

‍

To verify the viral claim, we conducted a Google search using relevant keywords. During the search, we found a report published on The Times of India website on September 16, 2026. According to the report, suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and set at least two houses on fire. Security forces engaged the attackers in an exchange of fire during the incident.According to officials, a large number of militants armed with sophisticated weapons attacked Chawangkining Naga village at around 10:30 p.m. on Tuesday. The attack took place hours after two Kuki women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in neighbouring Tamenglong district.CRPF personnel deployed in the nearby area returned fire, triggering intermittent firing that continued for nearly six hours until around 4:30 a.m. on Wednesday.An official said, “Intermittent firing was reported for nearly six hours till 4:30 a.m. on Wednesday. The CRPF returned fire, preventing the militants from entering the village.” He added that two wooden houses on the outskirts of the village were nevertheless set ablaze.

<https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/militants-torch-2-houses-in-manipur-village-trade-fire-with-crpf/articleshow/134277946.cms>

‍

‍

As part of our further investigation, we conducted a reverse image search of keyframes from the video. During the search, we found the visuals from the viral video on the YouTube channel of @ukhrultimes. According to the accompanying information, intermittent firing continued for nearly six hours in Chawangkining Naga village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on the night of September 15, 2026. During the incident, two houses on the outskirts of the village were completely burnt down, while several others were damaged.According to local reports, suspected militants targeted the village despite the deployment of CRPF personnel in the area and engaged in an exchange of fire with security forces. Meanwhile, the Liangmai Naga Council, Manipur (LNC-M), condemned the attack and alleged that suspected Kuki militants operating from the Songtung Suspension of Operations (SoO) camp were behind the firing. However, these allegations regarding the identity of the attackers should be reported as allegations and should not be presented as independently verified facts.

<https://www.youtube.com/shorts/QuZ2FoLyA5A>

‍

‍

At the end of our investigation, we found a report published on The Hindu website on September 16, 2026. According to the report, officials said that suspected militants had attacked Chawangkining Naga village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district. During the attack, they engaged in an exchange of fire with security forces and set at least two houses on the outskirts of the village on fire. The report quoted an official as saying that a large number of militants armed with sophisticated weapons attacked the village at around 10:30 p.m. on September 15. The incident took place hours after two Kuki women were shot dead in Leisangphai village in neighbouring Tamenglong district.

<https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/manipur/militants-burn-down-two-houses-in-manipur-village-exchange-fire-with-security-forces/article71471093.ece>

‍

### Conclusion

### ‍

Our investigation revealed that separate incidents of the killing of two women and the burning of their houses in Manipur are being falsely shared on social media, claiming them to be actions taken by the Indian Army. According to available reports, on September 15, 2026, two Kuki women were shot dead by unidentified armed assailants in Leisangphai village, Tamenglong district. On the same night, suspected militants attacked Chawangkining Naga village, Kangpokpi district. Security forces exchanged fire, and two houses on the outskirts of the village were set on fire. No credible report has confirmed the links between these incidents and the orders of the Indian Army or Eastern Command Commander Lieutenant General V.M. Bhuvana Krishnan. Therefore, the claim that the Indian Army shot two women and set their houses on fire by linking the two incidents is false and misleading.

#### **2011 Japan tsunami video**

The accompanying images resembled scenes from the viral video. The British outlet reported that following the tsunami that hit Japan on March 11, 2011, a newly released video showed cars, minibuses, vans, light aircraft, and helicopters being washed away. These visuals were from Japan’s Sendai Airport. Over 14,000 people were killed in the natural disaster.

Daily Mail also stated that the video was released by the Japan Coast Guard, a government agency. Several media outlets promoted these visuals, including The Telegraph UK and [The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/video/raw-footage-of-planes-swept-away-by-japan-tsunami/83E82791-4FE7-4808-A834-A7D766CB64B9.html).

# Video of 2011 Japan tsunami shared as ‘Three Gorges Dam of China’ overflowing

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/73203c41f00c9a985ef534dd36e095c10bda94e82211d80db4b5740baa9d3fa7?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/kinjal/)

[Kinjal](https://www.altnews.in/author/kinjal/)

 ![Video of 2011 Japan tsunami shared as ‘Three Gorges Dam of China’ overflowing](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/FAKE-4-1024x536.jpeg) 

Floods caused by heavy rains have [ravaged](https://www.bbc.com/hindi/media-57922603) parts of China recently. 80,000 people were evacuated from the Sichuan area due to [incessant rainfall and floods](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/heavy-rain-sichuan-causes-economic-losses-houses-collapse-state-media-2021-08-09/). Because of the continuous rainfall, the water levels in the country’s [Three Gorges Dam](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/why-is-china-facing-record-floods/articleshow/84612391.cms?from=mdr) have been rising steadily.

Against this backdrop, a video of a large boat overturning in floodwater is being shared widely on social media. It is being claimed that the footage shows the Three Gorges Dam of China.

> Due to heavy rain the Gorges Dam in China was opened. See what happened next. [@MeenaDasNarayan](https://twitter.com/MeenaDasNarayan?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/YcVjtlYU0T](https://t.co/YcVjtlYU0T)
>
> — Narayan Ned (@NarayanNed) [August 7, 2021](https://twitter.com/NarayanNed/status/1423905256061034497?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Another Twitter user posted the video as scenes from China’s Three Gorges Dam. ([Archive link](https://web.archive.org/web/20210810084423/https://mobile.twitter.com/SaGHar1214/status/1423353696273018887))

> The Gorges Dam in China on 2nd August 2021 due to heavy overflowing..!![#China](https://twitter.com/hashtag/China?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#ChinaFloods](https://twitter.com/hashtag/ChinaFloods?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#chinaflood](https://twitter.com/hashtag/chinaflood?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#Flood](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Flood?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#چائینہ](https://twitter.com/hashtag/%DA%86%D8%A7%D8%A6%DB%8C%D9%86%DB%81?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/fCWvD0w0N7](https://t.co/fCWvD0w0N7)
>
> — IjAz Ali SaGHar (@SaGHar1214) [August 5, 2021](https://twitter.com/SaGHar1214/status/1423353696273018887?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

A Facebook page named [‘Tobacco World’](https://www.facebook.com/www.ptb.gov.pk/videos/343856633872877/?__tn__=%2CO-R) shared the visuals with the same claim. ![](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/word-image-23.jpeg)

Alt News received a few requests to verify the video on its mobile app. The footage has also been circulated on WhatsApp as scenes from the recent floods in China.

This slideshow requires JavaScript.

#### **Fact-check**

Alt News performed a keyword search and we located the original video posted by Russian news channel RT as the 2011 tsunami in Japan. According to the caption, this video shows the aftermath of the tsunami in the Japanese city of Mayako. It is also mentioned that the waves were so high that everything that came in their way was swept away, including boats and vehicles. According to officials, more than 1,400 people were killed in the quake and hundreds went missing after the tsunami hit.

Comparing the frames from both the video’s establishes that this footage is of the 2011 tsunami in Japan.

This slideshow requires JavaScript.

More visuals from the 2011 tsunami in Japan can be found in these reports from [The Atlantic](https://amp.theatlantic.com/amp/photo/473211/), [Nairaland Forum](https://www.nairaland.com/2604310/thing-happened-japan-terrible-didnt), and [ABC News](https://youtu.be/pl7t52hMYwc).

A video of cars, buses, and aeroplanes drifting in floodwater was previously shared as China too. Alt News investigated this clip and discovered that this was also shot during the [tsunami that hit Japan](https://www.altnews.in/hindi/2011-video-from-japan-shared-as-flood-situation-in-china/) in 2011.

# News18 Kannda uses 2019 image from Bihar floods as aftermath of recent Mumbai rains

[![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/399cb9e278d29dd4eb8ecba351839b095c6c8018bb34676193b64b2a8d8c69b3?s=24&d=identicon&r=g)](https://www.altnews.in/author/archit-mehta/)

[Archit](https://www.altnews.in/author/archit-mehta/)

 ![News18 Kannda uses 2019 image from Bihar floods as aftermath of recent Mumbai rains](https://www.altnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/FI-3-1024x536.jpg) 

The ongoing monsoons have caused havoc across the country. Several cities have flooded due to heavy rainfall and as per the [July 23](https://mausam.imd.gov.in/Forecast/marquee_data/PRESS%20RELEASE%2023%20%20JULY%202021%20MONSOON.pdf) forecast by India Meteorological Department, heavy or extremely heavy rainfalls can be witnessed in multiple states. The [death toll in Maharashtra’s Raigad district](https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/maharashtra-rain-36-dead-in-landslides-in-maharashtras-raigad-district-after-heavy-rain-2493068) rose to 36 due to landslides caused by incessant rainfall. Mumbai is also experiencing a heavy downpour. Several [trains were cancelled or diverted](https://twitter.com/Central_Railway/status/1418486916295581696) for safety.

On July 18, [News18 Kannada](https://web.archive.org/web/20210723115611/https://kannada.news18.com/photogallery/national-international/maharashtra-govt-to-pay-rs-5-lakh-each-to-kin-of-deceased-sesr-595903.html) posted an image of coats inside a store filled with muddy water. The caption of the image read, “120mm of rain in Mumbai in the last 12 hours. Heavy rains are expected in two days, the Met Department said.”

The image has also been shared on Twitter with the claim it’s from Mumbai. ([1](https://web.archive.org/web/20210723114928/https://twitter.com/RealAtmnirbhar/status/1416663008994947073),[2](https://web.archive.org/web/20210723114937/https://twitter.com/HighnPositive/status/1416671592294215684),[3](https://archive.is/5x6NL))

> You can imagine what havoc the rain is causing in [#Mumbai](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Mumbai?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) .[#MumbaiRainUpdate](https://twitter.com/hashtag/MumbaiRainUpdate?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#MumbaiRains](https://twitter.com/hashtag/MumbaiRains?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) Weather 😑 [pic.twitter.com/jGdTn2qljt](https://t.co/jGdTn2qljt)
>
> — Khan Arshad (@RealAtmnirbhar) [July 18, 2021](https://twitter.com/RealAtmnirbhar/status/1416663008994947073?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Similarly, a [Facebook user](https://www.facebook.com/465166886836770/posts/4348717281815025) also posted the image in question with the same claim.

#### Old image from Bihar

Alt News performed a reverse image search and found that the image is three years old and is from Patna, Bihar.

According to a September 2019 [report](https://www.naidunia.com/national-pics-heavy-rain-in-bihar-patna-raymond-showroom-flooded-3169956) by Nai Dunia the image is from a Raymond showroom located at Hathwa Market. The store was flooded after the city received 158 mm of rain in the span of 24 hours.

YouTube channels [Live Cities Media Private Limited](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-wxAaMDJ62o) and [NMF News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BXErLmMaeac) showed other images from the showroom.

ANI uploaded a [video](https://youtu.be/RzAOGUJi6qI) of dewatering machines trying to clear waterlogging in Patna’s SK Puri area.

News18 Kannada posted an image from the 2019 monsoons in Patna while reporting the 2021 monsoon in Mumbai.

# Video of boat cruising down waterlogged road in Thai capital is AI-generated

* Published on September 29, 2026 at 10:31
* 2 min read
* By [Chayanit ITTHIPONGMAETEE](https://factcheck.afp.com/chayanit-itthipongmaetee),  [AFP Thailand](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-thailand)

Bangkok residents and rescuers turned to inflatables and small boats to navigate the Thai capital after days of heavy rain in late September 2026, but video circulating on social media showing a traditional long-tail boat motoring through waterlogged streets is AI-generated. The circulating clip includes several visual anomalies indicative of synthetic content and was flagged as being the product of generative AI by a detection tool.

"Boats have to be used in Bangkok, Thailand," says the Burmese-language caption of a [TikTok video](https://mvau.lt/media/2b663c20-8551-44d5-8ba3-0d20ae2dc4b2) shared on September 28, 2026.

The video appears to show a traditional long-tailed boat motoring by parked cars on a submerged road as pedestrians in colourful raincoats wade through the floodwaters.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/10cf9c244ffbc82cf7b4c8ca63b703cb-en.jpeg?itok=4wnhVyBb)

Screenshot of false post captured on September 29, 2026, with a red X and AI label added by AFP

The video surfaced as [days of heavy rain](https://www.afp.com/en/bangkok-declares-disaster-after-homes-flooded-roads-submerged-heavy-rain) flooded Bangkok, driving [thousands of residents](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/bangkok-floods-thousands-shelters-heavy-rain-6413256) into shelters and left homes, shops and roads waterlogged (archived [here](https://perma.cc/ZB9F-M8KB) and [here](https://perma.cc/TT6E-SCYZ)).

AFP journalists in Bangkok observed residents [using inflatables](https://perma.cc/2ZRL-4UND) and [small boats](https://perma.cc/TKN2-S4M3) to navigate flooded neighbourhoods.

The widespread flooding has killed at least four people in the Thai capital, the [government said](https://iol.co.za/news/world/2026-09-29-four-dead-in-bangkok-floods-as-thailand-toll-rises-to-23-ministry/) on September 29, as the toll from floods across the country since mid-September rose to 23 ([archived link](https://perma.cc/7EFE-WNUW)).

The video supposedly showing people in Bangkok using a long-tail boat was also shared in similar [Thai](https://perma.cc/N7GQ-QQTF) and [Burmese](https://perma.cc/DF58-9KPQ) posts on Facebook.

"From motoring on Saen Saep canal, to cruising on the roads," read a comment one of the posts.

Another said: "Thailand only. Cars and boats share the same lane. Please help share this video so people around the world want to come and experience this way of life that cannot be found elsewhere."

The video, however, is AI-generated.

A closer examination of the circulating footage shows there is garbled text on visible street signs -- a hallmark of synthetic media.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/9d5b8a1fc06fc6a4a8e019f9b05bb92c-en.jpeg?itok=RVYe4I1e)

Screenshot of the falsely shared video, with garbled street sign text highlighted by AFP

The video features road and building signs reading "SCB Park Plaza" but a visual comparison with [Google Street View imagery](https://www.google.com/maps/place/SCB+Park+Plaza+West/@13.8285713,100.5647099,7a,88.2y,167.72h,91.96t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1soEefMeXHq6jGAzumGer8YA!2e0!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.clients6.google.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fcb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile%26w%3D900%26h%3D600%26pitch%3D-1.9639971750958125%26panoid%3DoEefMeXHq6jGAzumGer8YA%26yaw%3D167.71809946516146!7i16384!8i8192!4m6!3m5!1s0x30e29cf9d90531ab:0x2643b09a2b04cbe8!8m2!3d13.827917!4d100.5637806!16s%2Fg%2F11bzthw8yh?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDkyMy4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) of the Siam Commercial Bank headquarters on Ratchadaphisek Road reveals distinct differences ([archived link](https://perma.cc/AD96-EFQF?type=image)).

While the falsely shared clip shows a large concrete flyover running directly above the flooded street, no such elevated structure exists in front of SCB Park Plaza.

Furthermore, the modern glass and angled architectural design of the real Siam Commercial Bank complex does not match the white, rectangular high-rises depicted in the falsely shared video.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/04f0cd032e40880f46ea8869c518dc77-en.jpeg?itok=Xrc6k26B)

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (L) and Google Street View imagery of the area around SCB Park Plaza, with differences highlighted by AFP

An analysis of the video using Meta's AI detection tool found digital signatures indicating the footage was created using generative AI tools.

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_in_article/public/medias/factchecking/g2/2026-09/f34a70d136658078bfbfedc7f02db768-en.jpeg?itok=8vK8CZP8)

Screenshot of results from Meta's AI detection tool

AFP has [previously debunked](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.86C73WE) other AI-generated images [depicting flooding](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.84Y33CR) in Thailand.
